```
1	# Tuning & Balance
2	
3	Every gameplay tunable lives in one place: [`lib/game/config.ts`](../lib/game/config.ts).
4	Each constant there carries a one-line comment; this guide is the companion that
5	groups them by **what they affect**, names the **system that reads each**, and
6	flags the **balance trade-offs** and the few that are **save-sensitive**.
7	
8	To rebalance, edit `config.ts` — not the systems. Item-level numbers (a pickaxe's
9	power, a sword's damage, a food's hunger) are **not** here; they live with the
10	content in [`items.ts`](../lib/game/items.ts) (see the [reference](reference.md)).
11	Worldgen constants live in the frozen `GEN` object in
12	[`generation.ts`](../lib/world/generation.ts) and are pinned by hash tests — see
13	[testing.md](testing.md).
14	
15	## Player feel — physics & movement
16	
17	`GRAVITY`, `JUMP_VELOCITY`, `WALK_SPEED`, `SPRINT_SPEED`, `CROUCH_SPEED`,
18	`PLAYER_HEIGHT`, `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`, `EYE_HEIGHT`, `WORLD_BORDER_PADDING`.
19	
20	Read by `systems/playerMotion.ts`. These set the moment-to-moment feel.
21	`JUMP_VELOCITY` vs `GRAVITY` together fix jump height (currently a ~1-block hop);
22	raise gravity for a snappier, heavier fall. `SPRINT_SPEED` is deliberately far
23	above `WALK_SPEED` so sprinting feels like a meaningful choice (and it's what burns
24	hunger fastest). `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`/`PLAYER_HEIGHT` are also the collision box, so
25	changing them affects which gaps the player fits through.
26	
27	## Survival pressure — the main difficulty dial
28	
29	`MAX_HEARTS`, `MAX_HUNGER`, `RESPAWN_SECONDS`, `HEALTH_REGEN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`,
30	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER`, `SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER`, `SPRINT_BLOCKS_PER_HUNGER`,
31	`WALK_BLOCKS_PER_HUNGER`, `JUMPS_PER_HUNGER`, `WATER_DAMAGE_DELAY_SECONDS`,
32	`WATER_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `WATER_DAMAGE_HP`.
33	
34	Read by `systems/playerStats.ts` (drain + regen) and `systems/playerLife.ts`
35	(respawn). This group is where "how hard is it to stay alive" is set. The
36	`*_PER_HUNGER` budgets control how fast activity drains food — lower numbers = more
37	eating. The two gates are the key feedback loop: you must stay above
38	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER` (12) to heal and above `SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` (6) to sprint, so
39	hunger pressure indirectly throttles both combat recovery and escape speed. Keep
40	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER > SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` so there's a "can run but can't heal" band.
```

The random-tick group\ncontrols crop growth statistically: each interval samples `RANDOM_TICK_SAMPLES`\ncolumns within `RANDOM_TICK_RADIUS` of the player and advances eligible crops with\n`CROP_GROWTH_CHANCE` probability — together ≈ 50 s/stage (~2.5 min to mature). More\nsamples or a larger radius means crops far from the player keep growing, at more\nper-tick work. Breeding is bounded by `PASSIVE_CAP` (24) plus the crop cost of\nfeeding, so animals can't explode in number.\n\nThe same sampler drives the **living world** (read by `systems/randomTicks.ts`\nand `systems/treeGrowth.ts`). `SAPLING_GROWTH_CHANCE` (0.12) is deliberately\nbelow `CROP_GROWTH_CHANCE` so a tree is a slower, bigger event than a wheat\nstage; a sapling only matures while it sits on grass/dirt/farmland.\n`LEAVES_SAPLING_DROP_CHANCE` (0.08) is the per-break odds a leaf block yields a\nsapling — its only drop, so the rate sets how renewable wood is. `GRASS_SPREAD_CHANCE`\n(0.18) is the per-tick odds exposed dirt re-grasses when a face-neighbour column's\ntop block is grass — raise it to heal terrain faster, lower it to leave scars\nlonger. Bone meal short-circuits the wait: `BONE_MEAL_PER_BONE` (3) is the grind\nyield, and one application advances a crop a random `1..BONE_MEAL_CROP_STAGES_MAX`\n(2) stages or grows a sapling instantly."

```
3:## Schema
8:- `worldType` (optional) — the generation preset (`"default"` | `"flat"` | `"amplified"` | `"islands"`); absent ⇒ `"default"`. Like `seed`, it is fixed for the world's life and the world must always regenerate with it, since the block-diffs were recorded against that terrain
9:- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
17:- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`
19:Each world's `SaveData` is stored in its own localStorage key, `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` — `readSave`/`writeSave` take the key as a parameter and the `Storage` is injectable for tests; `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is now read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)
29:### Version history
31:- **v5** (unchanged for villagers & trading) — the villager mob is transient like every mob, and trading needs no persisted state: a trade is a station-gated recipe (`station: "villager"`) run through the existing `craft` command, the open trade station (`craftingStation`) is session-only, and there are no per-trade use caps to store. **Emerald** and any traded goods save by string id in the existing inventory slots. No worldgen change (villagers spawn into the passive population; there are no village structures), so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
32:- **v5** (unchanged for creepers & TNT) — the creeper mob, gunpowder, and the explosion system add no persisted state: mobs are transient, **a creeper's lit fuse and a primed TNT block's countdown are session-only** (`MobState.fuseTimer` and `state.primedTnt` are never serialized — like the boss and in-flight arrows). Gunpowder and the TNT item save by string id; a **placed TNT block persists in the block diff** like any block, and a save written mid-fuse reloads with that TNT as an inert, un-lit block (and no creeper). There is no worldgen change — creepers are spawned and TNT is crafted — so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved. Blast-destroyed blocks are ordinary block-diff edits.
33:- **v5** (unchanged for cow/pig & coal) — the cow and pig mobs (and their meat/leather drops) add no persisted state; mobs are transient and the new foods save by string id. Coal ore, coal, and charcoal are likewise additive (the ore persists in the block diff, the items by string id), so the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the new coal worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`**: a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. Coal runs on its own PRNG (`placeCoal`), so only underground coal cells differ from a v7 world — the surface, existing ores, trees, and structures are byte-identical (the meshing and structural-probe tests stay green; only the byte hashes were re-rolled).
34:- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
35:- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
36:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5.
37:- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
43:## Profiles & worlds
48:- **`minecraft_worlds_v1`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`) — the world index. Each `WorldMeta` is `{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldType, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`; `profileId` is the 1:N owner link and `lastPlayedAt` drives the most-recent-first ordering. The `seed` is resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric text → clamped int, other text → stable FNV hash via `resolveSeed`); `worldType` is the chosen generation preset (sanitized to `"default"` on read for unknown/legacy entries). Both are the source of truth for regeneration and are also written into the per-world `SaveData` blob.
51:`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 8) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.
53:**World types.** A world's `worldType` selects a generation preset (`lib/world/worldTypes.ts`). `generateWorld(world, worldType)` forks on it before any block write (`terrainConfigFor`, `lib/world/generation.ts`), varying only sea level and per-biome surface height; everything else reads `GEN`. The `"default"` branch returns the GEN values verbatim, so default worlds stay **byte-identical** to the pre-feature generator — the existing determinism hashes are unchanged. Each non-default type is its own deterministic save contract with its own SHA-256 baseline in `generation.test.ts`; `worldgenVersion` still guards all types (a deliberate change to any type's config bumps `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, discarding stale worlds of that vintage).
57:### Legacy migration
61:## Autosave
63:Every 15s via `setInterval`, plus on `beforeunload`, all writing to the active world's `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key. "Save & Quit to Worlds" also persists synchronously before leaving, because the interval is cleared on unmount and `beforeunload` does not fire on an in-app world switch.
65:## Compatibility rules
73:- Note save-format/worldgen impact in PRs.
```

> AGENT

Done. The **Living World** feature is implemented on the `feat/living-world` branch as four focused, bisectable commits — each independently lint/typecheck/test-green.

## What shipped

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `c4d0662` | **Saplings** — leaves drop a sapling (~8%, their only drop now), plant on grass/dirt, mature into trees via the random-tick system once on soil |
| `17fd57e` | **Bone meal** — ground from bones (1→3), grows saplings instantly / advances wheat 1–2 stages |
| `56b647d` | **Grass spread** — exposed dirt re-grasses beside a grass neighbour |
| `f79895a` | **Docs** — manual, reference, tuning, adding-content, save-format, testing coverage map, CHANGELOG |

**Key design choices that paid off:**
- Tree-building lives in a new `systems/treeGrowth.ts` shared by the sapling tick handler and bone meal; it writes through `blockChanges` (so trees persist + relight) and deliberately shares **no** code with worldgen's hash-pinned `placeTrees` — so the generation hashes stayed **byte-identical** and there's **no save/worldgen-version bump**.
- Saplings reuse the wheat approach (solid cube, atlas-painted) — no new geometry path.
- `Sapling` is appended at `BlockId` id 50 so saved block ids never shift.

**One thing I found and fixed along the way:** an existing mining test broke because the test seed spawns the player *on a tree canopy*, so "the block underfoot" was leaves — which now correctly drop nothing most of the time. I pinned that test to a known dropping block instead of relying on spawn terrain.

## Verification — full AGENTS.md gate, all green
- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check` ✓
- `bun test` — **561 pass / 0 fail** (incl. new sapling/grass-spread/bone-meal/leaves-drop cases; `generation.test.ts` green & unchanged, confirming zero worldgen impact)
- `bun run build` ✓
- `bun run test:e2e` — **14/14 pass** (boots and renders the new atlas without errors)

## Not done (your call)
- **A manual eyeball of the sapling's in-game texture** — the e2e suite confirms the atlas builds and the world renders, but I haven't visually inspected the painted sprout sprite during real play (planting/growing). If you want, I can run `bun run dev` and screenshot it.
- **I did not push or open a PR** — per your workflow (commit locally, you review before push). The four commits are local on `feat/living-world`; review them with `git log -p main..feat/living-world`, and tell me when you'd like it pushed / a PR opened against `hutusi/monecraft`.

Here's how I'd prioritize what's next:

## Top recommendation: Creative + Peaceful game modes ⭐
- **The single biggest missing axis.** The game has exactly one mode. With all the building blocks now in place — and especially the new living world — a **Creative** mode (flight, instant break, infinite blocks from a creative palette, no damage/hunger) unlocks free-building, which is half of why people play voxel games. **Peaceful** (no hostile spawns) broadens the audience and pairs naturally.
- Touches many systems but each touch is small (gate damage/hunger/spawning/mining, add flight to motion), and the save change is just an additive `gameMode` field — low risk, like the world-type picker that already exists.

## Strong alternatives
- **Village structures** — generate real settlements (house clusters, paths, wells) with villagers spawning in them, grounding the trade economy. This is the other gap the docs explicitly flag; it's a worldgen change (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump + hash re-baseline).
- **Status effects & potions (brewing)** — a brewing stand + effects (speed, strength, regen, poison, fire/water resistance). High depth and unlocks future systems (enchanting), but the heaviest: it needs a new status-effect subsystem that doesn't exist yet.
- **Fishing** — a self-contained, low-risk addition that fits the renewable theme: craft a rod, cast into water, reel in fish (food) and junk. Smallest of the four.

### 1. **`lib/world/queries.ts` — The Core Raycast System**

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/world/queries.ts`

#### `voxelRaycast` Function Signature
```typescript
export function voxelRaycast(
  world: VoxelWorld, 
  origin: THREE.Vector3, 
  direction: THREE.Vector3, 
  maxDist = 6
): RaycastResult | null
```

Where `RaycastResult` is:
```typescript
export type RaycastResult = {
  hit: THREE.Vector3;           // The solid block coordinates
  previous: THREE.Vector3;       // Last empty cell before the hit (face-adjacent)
  distance: number;              // Ray parameter where ray enters hit cell
};
```

**Water Treatment:** Confirmed — `voxelRaycast` **ignores/passes through Water entirely**. Test at line 62-66 of `queries.test.ts` explicitly verifies: "water is not a raycast target" — placing `BlockId.Water` at target returns `null`.

**DDA Loop (lines 40–63):**
```typescript
while (t <= maxDist) {
  if (world.isSolid(x, y, z)) return { hit: new THREE.Vector3(x, y, z), previous, distance: t };
  previous = new THREE.Vector3(x, y, z);

  if (tMaxX < tMaxY) {
    if (tMaxX < tMaxZ) {
      x += stepX;
      t = tMaxX;
      tMaxX += invDx;
    } else {
      z += stepZ;
      t = tMaxZ;
      tMaxZ += invDz;
    }
  } else if (tMaxY < tMaxZ) {
    y += stepY;
    t = tMaxY;
    tMaxY += invDy;
  } else {
    z += stepZ;
    t = tMaxZ;
    tMaxZ += invDz;
  }
}
```

The loop uses standard 3D-DDA (Digital Differential Analyzer) by tracking the `t` parameter (ray distance) where the ray crosses each voxel boundary in each axis. You could adapt this same stepping logic to stop at Water instead of solids.

- **`collidesAt(world, position, halfWidth, height)`** (lines 70–96): AABB collision testing. **Water is explicitly non-solid** — line 83 checks `if (!world.isSolid(x, y, z)) continue;` which skips water. Comment at line 69: "Water never collides."

**Dungeon loot table structure** (dungeonLoot.ts, lines 13–40):
```typescript
export type LootEntry = MobDrop;
export type LootTier = "common" | "rare";
export const RARE_CHEST_CHANCE = 0.25;

export const DUNGEON_LOOT: Record<LootTier, LootEntry[]> = {
  common: [
    { itemId: "bone", min: 1, max: 3 },
    { itemId: "bread", min: 1, max: 3, chance: 0.8 },
    { itemId: "cooked_chicken", min: 1, max: 2, chance: 0.5 },
    // ... more entries
  ],
  rare: [
    { itemId: "diamond_ore", min: 1, max: 2, chance: 0.3 },
    // ... more entries
  ]
};
```

**Mob roll function signature** (mobLoot.ts, lines 56–65):
```typescript
export function rollMobDrops(kind: MobKind, rng: () => number): Array<{ itemId: string; count: number }> {
  const drops: Array<{ itemId: string; count: number }> = [];
  for (const entry of MOB_DROPS[kind]) {
    if (entry.chance !== undefined && clampUnit(rng()) >= entry.chance) continue;
    const span = entry.max - entry.min + 1;
    const count = entry.min + Math.floor(clampUnit(rng()) * span);
    if (count > 0) drops.push({ itemId: entry.itemId, count });
  }
  return drops;
}
```

**Dungeon roll function signature** (dungeonLoot.ts, lines 77–82):
```typescript
export function rollDungeonLoot(rng: () => number): Array<{ itemId: string; count: number }> {
  const rare = clampUnit(rng()) < RARE_CHEST_CHANCE;
  const drops = rare ? rollEntries(DUNGEON_LOOT.rare, rng) : [];
  drops.push(...rollEntries(DUNGEON_LOOT.common, rng));
  return drops;
}
```

**Key observations:**
- Tables use `{ itemId, min, max, chance? }` shape; `chance` is optional (default: always drop)
- Roll functions accept an injectable `rng: () => number` (returns [0, 1)) for determinism in tests
- Each roll call samples the RNG once per entry for the chance gate, once per entry for the count span
- Helper `rollEntries` at line 61 shows the core loop pattern for any loot table
- Output is always `Array<{ itemId: string; count: number }>` — one entry per item that yielded a positive count

### 2. **Adding Items to Inventory**

**File path:**
`/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/inventory.ts`

**Primary add-item function signature** (lines 30–75):
```typescript
export function adjustSlotCount(
  slots: InventorySlot[],
  slotId: string,
  delta: number,
  preferredIndex?: number
): InventorySlot[] | null
```

**Behavior:**
- `delta > 0`: adds items, filling existing stacks first, then empty slots; overflow is silently dropped if inventory is full
- `delta < 0`: removes items, returns `null` if insufficient count (all-or-nothing)
- `preferredIndex` (optional): fills/consumes from that slot first before scanning others
- Returns a new array on success, or `null` if the operation doesn't apply (keeps previous array on `null`)

**Real-world call example 1 — mob drops** (GameEngine.ts):
```typescript
const drops = mob.ageTimer <= 0 ? rollMobDrops(mob.kind, this.rng) : [];
for (const drop of drops) {
  state.inventory = inv.adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, drop.itemId, drop.count) ?? state.inventory;
}
```

**Real-world call example 2 — block drops** (mining.ts, lines 44–48):
```typescript
function addBlockDrop(state: GameState, block: BlockId, rng: () => number): void {
  for (const drop of rollBlockDrops(block, rng)) {
    state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, drop.itemId, drop.count) ?? state.inventory;
  }
}
```

**Pattern:** Loop over rolled drops, call `adjustSlotCount` for each, and assign the result back (using `?? state.inventory` to preserve on `null`).

**Tool durability consumption** (lines 78–91):
```typescript
export function consumeToolDurability(slots: InventorySlot[], index: number, amount = 1): InventorySlot[] | null {
  if (amount <= 0) return null;
  if (index < 0 || index >= slots.length) return null;
  const next = cloneSlots(slots);
  const slot = next[index];
  if ((slot.kind !== "tool" && slot.kind !== "weapon") || !slot.id || slot.count <= 0 || !slot.maxDurability) return null;
  const nextDurability = (slot.durability ?? slot.maxDurability) - amount;
  if (nextDurability <= 0) {
    next[index] = createEmptySlot();
    return next;
  }
  slot.durability = nextDurability;
  return next;
}
```

```typescript
export function consumeToolDurability(slots: InventorySlot[], index: number, amount = 1): InventorySlot[] | null {
  if (amount <= 0) return null;
  if (index < 0 || index >= slots.length) return null;
  const next = cloneSlots(slots);
  const slot = next[index];
  if ((slot.kind !== "tool" && slot.kind !== "weapon") || !slot.id || slot.count <= 0 || !slot.maxDurability) return null;
  const nextDurability = (slot.durability ?? slot.maxDurability) - amount;
  if (nextDurability <= 0) {
    next[index] = createEmptySlot();
    return next;
  }
  slot.durability = nextDurability;
  return next;
}
```

**Tool-gating pattern in `tryUseHeldItem`** (interact.ts, lines 184–234):
```typescript
export function tryUseHeldItem(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent, rng: () => number): boolean {
  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];
  if (!slot?.id || slot.count <= 0) return false;
  
  // Tool type check (checks for suffix or exact match)
  const isHoe = slot.id.endsWith("_hoe");
  const isSeeds = slot.id === "seeds";
  const isTorch = slot.id === "torch";
  // ... more checks ...
  
  if (!isHoe && !isSeeds && !isTorch && !isSapling && !isBoneMeal) return false;
  
  // Get aim target
  const { world, player } = state;
  scratchEye.set(player.position.x, player.position.y + EYE_HEIGHT, player.position.z);
  lookDirection(player.yaw, player.pitch, scratchDir);
  const result = voxelRaycast(world, scratchEye, scratchDir, MINE_REACH);
  if (!result) return false;
  const { x, y, z } = result.hit;
  const block = world.get(x, y, z) as BlockId;

  // Hoe: till grass/dirt → farmland
  if (isHoe) {
    if (block !== BlockId.Grass && block !== BlockId.Dirt) return false;
    state.blockChanges.set(x, y, z, BlockId.Farmland);
    state.inventory = consumeToolDurability(state.inventory, state.selectedSlot, 1) ?? state.inventory;
    state.worldMeshDirty = true;
    emit({ type: "tilledSoil" });
    return true;
  }
  // ... more tool handlers ...
}
```

**ItemDef shape for tools** (from types.ts):

```typescript
export type ItemDef = {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  kind: ItemKind;
  minePower?: number;
  mineTier?: number;
  maxDurability?: number;
  // ... other optional properties
};
```

**Key observations:**
- Tools have `kind: "tool"`, optional `minePower` and `mineTier` (for mining), and required `maxDurability`
- `consumeToolDurability(inventory, slotIndex, amount)` decrements durability and empties the slot at zero
- Tool gating in `tryUseHeldItem` checks by suffix (`endsWith("_hoe")`) or exact ID match
- Each tool call: raycast for block, check conditions, execute action, then `consumeToolDurability` if applicable
- Returns `true` when the interaction is consumed, `false` to fall through to block placement

```typescript
  if (state.timers.bowCooldownTimer > 0) return false;
  if ((countsById(state.inventory).get("arrow") ?? 0) < 1) return false;

  const { position, yaw, pitch } = state.player;
  scratchOrigin.set(position.x, position.y + EYE_HEIGHT, position.z);
  lookDirection(yaw, pitch, scratchForward);
  spawnArrow(state, scratchOrigin.x, scratchOrigin.y, scratchOrigin.z, scratchForward, {
    speed: ARROW_SPEED,
    damage: BOW_ARROW_DAMAGE,
    knockback: BOW_KNOCKBACK,
    fromPlayer: true,
    ttl: ARROW_TTL
  });

  state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, "arrow", -1) ?? state.inventory;
  state.inventory = consumeToolDurability(state.inventory, state.selectedSlot, BOW_DURABILITY_PER_SHOT) ?? state.inventory;
  state.timers.bowCooldownTimer = BOW_COOLDOWN_SECONDS;
  emit({ type: "bowFired" });
  return true;
}
```

The underlying spawn helper is in `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts` (lines 23–44):

```typescript
export function spawnArrow(state: GameState, originX: number, originY: number, originZ: number, dir: THREE.Vector3, opts: SpawnArrowOptions): ProjectileState {
  scratchDir.copy(dir);
  if (scratchDir.lengthSq() < 1e-9) scratchDir.set(0, 0, -1);
  scratchDir.normalize();

  const velocity = scratchDir.clone().multiplyScalar(opts.speed);
  const projectile: ProjectileState = {
    id: state.nextProjectileId,
    position: new THREE.Vector3(originX + scratchDir.x * MUZZLE_OFFSET, originY + scratchDir.y * MUZZLE_OFFSET, originZ + scratchDir.z * MUZZLE_OFFSET),
    velocity,
    yaw: Math.atan2(scratchDir.x, scratchDir.z),
    pitch: Math.asin(Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, scratchDir.y))),
    damage: opts.damage,
    knockback: opts.knockback,
    fromPlayer: opts.fromPlayer,
    ttl: opts.ttl
  };

  state.nextProjectileId += 1;
  state.projectiles.push(projectile);
  return projectile;
}
```

**Key pattern:** Read held item → get eye position (`EYE_HEIGHT` offset) → compute look direction → offset 0.6m forward (MUZZLE_OFFSET to prevent self-collision) → create state object with auto-incremented id → push to array → consume arrow from inventory (via `adjustSlotCount(..., "arrow", -1)`) → decay bow durability → emit event.

#### Thrown Spears (right-click/E key)

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/spears.ts` (lines 21–45)

```typescript
export function tryThrowSelectedSpear(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];
  if (!slot?.id?.endsWith("_spear") || slot.kind !== "weapon" || !slot.throwDamage) return false;
  if (state.timers.spearThrowCooldown > 0) return true;

  lookDirection(state.player.yaw, state.player.pitch, scratchDirection);
  const position = new THREE.Vector3(state.player.position.x, state.player.position.y + EYE_HEIGHT, state.player.position.z).addScaledVector(
    scratchDirection,
    0.55
  );
  state.thrownSpears.push({
    id: state.nextThrownSpearId,
    itemId: slot.id,
    position,
    velocity: scratchDirection.clone().multiplyScalar(SPEAR_THROW_SPEED),
    damage: slot.throwDamage,
    age: 0,
    stuckTimer: null
  });
  state.nextThrownSpearId += 1;
  state.timers.spearThrowCooldown = SPEAR_THROW_COOLDOWN_SECONDS;
  state.inventory = consumeToolDurability(state.inventory, state.selectedSlot, 1) ?? state.inventory;
  emit({ type: "attackSwung" });
  return true;
}
```

**Key pattern:** Validate held item is a spear (ends with `"_spear"`, kind is `"weapon"`, has `throwDamage`) → check cooldown → eye position + 0.55m forward offset → create state with itemId (preserved for rendering material color) → push to array → decay durability → emit event.

### 3. PER-TICK UPDATE & REMOVAL

#### Arrows (gravity + swept collision + TTL)

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/projectileAI.ts` (lines 38–157)

```typescript
export function tickProjectiles(state: GameState, dt: number, deps: ProjectileTickDeps): void {
  const { world, projectiles } = state;
  if (projectiles.length === 0) return;
  const dead: number[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < projectiles.length; i += 1) {
    const p = projectiles[i];
    p.ttl -= dt;
    if (p.ttl <= 0) {
      dead.push(i);
      continue;
    }

    const substeps = Math.min(ARROW_MAX_SUBSTEPS, Math.max(1, Math.ceil((p.velocity.length() * dt) / ARROW_MAX_SEGMENT)));
    const sdt = dt / substeps;
    let removed = false;

    for (let s = 0; s < substeps && !removed; s += 1) {
      p.velocity.y -= ARROW_GRAVITY * sdt;  // Gravity integration
      const segLen = p.velocity.length() * sdt;
      if (segLen < 1e-9) continue;
      segDir.copy(p.velocity).divideScalar(p.velocity.length());

      // Swept block collision (voxel raycast)
      let blockT = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
      const blockHit = voxelRaycast(world, p.position, segDir, segLen);
      if (blockHit && blockHit.distance <= segLen) blockT = blockHit.distance;

      // Nearest entity collision (mobs for player arrows, player for mob arrows)
      let entityT = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
      let hitMobIndex = -1;
      if (p.fromPlayer) {
        for (let m = 0; m < state.mobs.length; m += 1) {
          const mob = state.mobs[m];
          const t = closestParam(
            p.position.x, p.position.y, p.position.z,
            segDir.x, segDir.y, segDir.z,
            segLen,
            mob.position.x, mob.position.y, mob.position.z
          );
          const horiz = Math.hypot(p.position.x + segDir.x * t - mob.position.x, p.position.z + segDir.z * t - mob.position.z);
          const vert = Math.abs(p.position.y + segDir.y * t - mob.position.y);
          if (horiz <= mobBodyRadius(mob) && vert <= mob.halfHeight + ARROW_HIT_RADIUS && t < entityT) {
            entityT = t;
            hitMobIndex = m;
          }
        }
      } else {
        // Player hit detection (mob arrows hitting player)
        const feet = state.player.position;
        const midY = feet.y + PLAYER_HEIGHT / 2;
        const t = closestParam(p.position.x, p.position.y, p.position.z, segDir.x, segDir.y, segDir.z, segLen, feet.x, midY, feet.z);
        const horiz = Math.hypot(p.position.x + segDir.x * t - feet.x, p.position.z + segDir.z * t - feet.z);
        const vert = Math.abs(p.position.y + segDir.y * t - midY);
        if (horiz <= PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH + ARROW_HIT_RADIUS && vert <= PLAYER_HEIGHT / 2 + ARROW_HIT_RADIUS) entityT = t;
      }

      if (entityT !== Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY && entityT <= blockT) {
        const hx = p.position.x + segDir.x * entityT;
        const hy = p.position.y + segDir.y * entityT;
        const hz = p.position.z + segDir.z * entityT;
        if (p.fromPlayer) {
          const mob = state.mobs[hitMobIndex];
          mob.hp -= p.damage;
          knock.set(segDir.x, 0, segDir.z);
          if (knock.lengthSq() > 1e-6) {
            knock.normalize();
            mob.direction.copy(knock);
            mob.position.addScaledVector(knock, p.knockback);
            mob.position.y += 0.1;
          }
          deps.emit({ type: "mobHit", kind: mob.kind });
          deps.emit({ type: "arrowHit", x: hx, y: hy, z: hz, target: "mob" });
          if (mob.hp <= 0) deps.removeMobAt(hitMobIndex);
        } else {
          deps.applyDamage(p.damage);
          state.player.velocity.x += segDir.x * p.knockback;
          state.player.velocity.z += segDir.z * p.knockback;
          deps.emit({ type: "arrowHit", x: hx, y: hy, z: hz, target: "player" });
        }
        removed = true;
      } else if (blockT !== Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) {
        deps.emit({
          type: "arrowHit",
          x: p.position.x + segDir.x * blockT,
          y: p.position.y + segDir.y * blockT,
          z: p.position.z + segDir.z * blockT,
          target: "block"
        });
        removed = true;
      } else {
        p.position.addScaledVector(segDir, segLen);
      }
    }

    if (!removed) {
      const speed = p.velocity.length();
      p.yaw = Math.atan2(p.velocity.x, p.velocity.z);
      p.pitch = Math.asin(speed > 1e-6 ? Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, p.velocity.y / speed)) : 0);
      if (
        p.position.x < 1 ||
        p.position.z < 1 ||
        p.position.x > world.sizeX - 1 ||
        p.position.z > world.sizeZ - 1 ||
        p.position.y < 0 ||
        p.position.y > world.sizeY
      ) {
        removed = true;
      }
    }
    if (removed) dead.push(i);
  }

  for (let i = dead.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) projectiles.splice(dead[i], 1);
}
```

**Key mechanics:**
- **TTL decay** (line 45): Arrows despawn after `ARROW_TTL` (4 seconds).
- **Gravity**: Each substep applies `ARROW_GRAVITY * sdt` to velocity.y (downward).
- **Swept collision**: Multi-substep raycasting (capped at `ARROW_MAX_SUBSTEPS=4`, max segment `ARROW_MAX_SEGMENT=0.5` blocks per step) prevents fast arrows from skipping thin walls or mobs.
- **Hit resolution**: Whichever hits first (entity or block) — entity deals damage and removes arrow, block emits hit event and removes arrow.
- **Out-of-bounds removal**: Arrows vanish outside world bounds.
- **Removal**: Dead arrows collected in array, then **removed in reverse order** (line 156) to avoid index shifting.

#### Thrown Spears (gravity + swept collision + stick timer)

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/spears.ts` (lines 56–112)

```typescript
export function tickThrownSpears(state: GameState, dt: number, removeMobAt: (index: number) => void, emit: EmitGameEvent): void {
  state.timers.spearThrowCooldown = Math.max(0, state.timers.spearThrowCooldown - dt);
  if (state.thrownSpears.length === 0) return;

  const survivors: ThrownSpearState[] = [];
  for (const spear of state.thrownSpears) {
    if (spear.stuckTimer !== null) {
      spear.stuckTimer += dt;
      if (spear.stuckTimer < SPEAR_STUCK_SECONDS) survivors.push(spear);
      continue;
    }

    spear.age += dt;
    if (spear.age >= SPEAR_THROW_LIFETIME_SECONDS) continue;

    scratchDisplacement.copy(spear.velocity).multiplyScalar(dt);
    const distance = scratchDisplacement.length();
    const terrainHit = distance > 0 ? voxelRaycast(state.world, spear.position, scratchDisplacement, distance) : null;
    const terrainFraction = terrainHit && distance > 0 ? terrainHit.distance / distance : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;

    let hitIndex = -1;
    let hitFraction = terrainFraction;
    for (let i = 0; i < state.mobs.length; i += 1) {
      const mob = state.mobs[i];
      const fraction = segmentHitFraction(spear, scratchDisplacement, mob.position, SPEAR_HIT_RADIUS + mob.halfHeight * 0.35);
      if (fraction === null || fraction >= hitFraction) continue;
      hitFraction = fraction;
      hitIndex = i;
    }

    if (hitIndex >= 0) {
      const mob = state.mobs[hitIndex];
      const kind = mob.kind;
      mob.hp -= spear.damage;
      scratchDirection.copy(spear.velocity).setY(0);
      if (scratchDirection.lengthSq() > 0.0001) {
        scratchDirection.normalize();
        mob.direction.copy(scratchDirection);
        mob.position.addScaledVector(scratchDirection, 0.9);
      }
      emit({ type: "mobHit", kind });
      if (mob.hp <= 0) removeMobAt(hitIndex);
      continue;
    }

    if (terrainHit) {
      spear.position.addScaledVector(scratchDisplacement, terrainFraction);
      spear.stuckTimer = 0;  // Begin stuck timer
      survivors.push(spear);
      continue;
    }
    spear.position.add(scratchDisplacement);
    spear.velocity.y -= SPEAR_THROW_GRAVITY * dt;  // Gravity
    survivors.push(spear);
  }
  state.thrownSpears = survivors;
}
```

**Key mechanics:**
- **Two-state lifecycle:**
  - **Flying** (`stuckTimer === null`): Gravity, collision, damage.
  - **Stuck** (`stuckTimer !== null`): Decays timeout, then removed once `SPEAR_STUCK_SECONDS` (2 seconds) elapses.
- **Age limit**: Despawns at `SPEAR_THROW_LIFETIME_SECONDS` (4 seconds) if still flying.
- **Single-pass raycast** (unlike arrows): Simplest collision — terrain or mob.
- **Removal via filter**: Uses `survivors` array to exclude expired spears; `state.thrownSpears = survivors;` replaces the whole array.

#### Invocation Order

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` (lines 258, 266)

```typescript
  tickThrownSpears(state, dt, this.removeMobAt, this.emit);      // Line 258
  // ...other systems...
  tickProjectiles(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);                  // Line 266
```

Both run **every frame** in `step()`. Spears tick first, then projectiles. Both run **even when the player is dead** (see lines 233–234) so in-flight projectiles and stuck spears resolve instead of freezing during respawn.

### 4. RENDERING

#### Arrow Mesh Sync

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/projectileVisuals.ts` (lines 22–63)

```typescript
export function createProjectileVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): ProjectileVisuals {
  const geometry = buildExtrudedSpriteGeometry(renderSpritePixels("arrow"));
  const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ vertexColors: true, roughness: 0.6, metalness: 0.1 });
  const meshes = new Map<number, THREE.Mesh>();
  const seen = new Set<number>();

  const removeMesh = (id: number): void => {
    const mesh = meshes.get(id);
    if (!mesh) return;
    scene.remove(mesh);
    meshes.delete(id);
  };

  return {
    sync(projectiles) {
      seen.clear();
      for (const p of projectiles) {
        seen.add(p.id);
        let mesh = meshes.get(p.id);
        if (!mesh) {
          mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
          meshes.set(p.id, mesh);
          scene.add(mesh);
        }
        mesh.position.set(p.position.x, p.position.y, p.position.z);
        if (p.velocity.lengthSq() > 1e-6) {
          scratchDir.copy(p.velocity).normalize();
          mesh.quaternion.copy(scratchQuat.setFromUnitVectors(UP_Y, scratchDir));
        }
      }
      for (const id of meshes.keys()) {
        if (!seen.has(id)) removeMesh(id);
      }
    },

    dispose() {
      for (const id of [...meshes.keys()]) removeMesh(id);
      geometry.dispose();
      material.dispose();
    }
  };
}
```

**Key pattern:**
- **Shared geometry**: One extruded-sprite geometry (arrow sprite pixels rendered at 0.03 pixel size, 0.03 depth) shared across all arrows.
- **Shared material**: One `MeshStandardMaterial` (vertexColors, roughness 0.6, metalness 0.1) for all arrows.
- **Per-arrow mesh**: Map keyed by projectile id; **lazy-created** on first sync frame.
- **Sync logic**: 
  - For each projectile in the live array, ensure a mesh exists.
  - Position mesh at projectile position.
  - Rotate mesh to face velocity direction using `setFromUnitVectors(UP_Y, velocity)` — the sprite points up (+Y) in local space; this rotates it to point along the flight direction.
  - Cleanup: Remove meshes whose ids are no longer in the projectile array.
- **Geometry source**: `buildExtrudedSpriteGeometry()` from `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/extrudedSprite.ts` — converts 16x16 RGBA sprite pixels into a thin 3D mesh with per-face shading.

#### Spear Mesh Sync

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/spearVisuals.ts` (lines 38–75)

```typescript
export function createSpearVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): SpearVisuals {
  const models = new Map<number, SpearModel>();
  const seen = new Set<number>();

  const removeModel = (id: number) => {
    const model = models.get(id);
    if (!model) return;
    scene.remove(model.group);
    for (const geometry of model.geometries) geometry.dispose();
    for (const material of model.materials) material.dispose();
    models.delete(id);
  };

  return {
    sync(spears) {
      seen.clear();
      for (const spear of spears) {
        seen.add(spear.id);
        let model = models.get(spear.id);
        if (!model) {
          model = createSpearModel(spear.itemId);
          models.set(spear.id, model);
          scene.add(model.group);
        }
        model.group.position.copy(spear.position);
        direction.copy(spear.velocity);
        if (direction.lengthSq() > 0.0001) model.group.quaternion.setFromUnitVectors(up, direction.normalize());
      }
      for (const id of models.keys()) {
        if (!seen.has(id)) removeModel(id);
      }
    },

    dispose() {
      for (const id of [...models.keys()]) removeModel(id);
    }
  };
}
```

**Model construction** (lines 24–36):
```typescript
function createSpearModel(itemId: string): SpearModel {
  const group = new THREE.Group();
  const shaftGeometry = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.035, 0.035, 1.15, 6);
  const tipGeometry = new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.13, 0.38, 4);
  const shaftMaterial = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x8d6035, roughness: 0.8 });
  const tipMaterial = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: materialColor(itemId), roughness: 0.45, metalness: 0.15 });
  const shaft = new THREE.Mesh(shaftGeometry, shaftMaterial);
  const tip = new THREE.Mesh(tipGeometry, tipMaterial);
  shaft.position.y = -0.18;
  tip.position.y = 0.585;
  group.add(shaft, tip);
  return { group, geometries: [shaftGeometry, tipGeometry], materials: [shaftMaterial, tipMaterial] };
}
```

**Key pattern:**
- **Per-spear model**: Unlike arrows (shared geometry), each spear gets its own `THREE.Group` holding a shaft (cylinder) + tip (cone).
- **Material color**: Tip color derived from itemId prefix (e.g., "iron_spear" → iron palette color).
- **Rotation**: Same pattern as arrows — rotate to face velocity direction via `setFromUnitVectors(up, velocity)`.
- **Cleanup**: Dispose all geometries + materials when spear is removed.

### 5. PICKUP / INVENTORY ADD

When arrows or spears are picked up or retrieved, items are added via:

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/inventory.ts` (lines 30–75)

```typescript
export function adjustSlotCount(slots: InventorySlot[], slotId: string, delta: number, preferredIndex?: number): InventorySlot[] | null {
  if (!slotId || delta === 0) return null;
  const next = cloneSlots(slots);
  let remaining = Math.abs(delta);

  if (delta < 0) {
    // Consume...
    const consumeFromIndex = (index: number) => {
      if (remaining <= 0) return;
      if (index < 0 || index >= next.length) return;
      const slot = next[index];
      if (slot.id !== slotId || slot.count <= 0) return;
      const take = Math.min(remaining, slot.count);
      slot.count -= take;
      remaining -= take;
      if (slot.count <= 0) next[index] = createEmptySlot();
    };
    if (typeof preferredIndex === "number") consumeFromIndex(preferredIndex);
    for (let i = 0; i < next.length && remaining > 0; i += 1) consumeFromIndex(i);
    if (remaining > 0) return null;
    return next;
  }

  if (!ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[slotId]) return null;
  const stackSize = maxStackSizeForItem(slotId);

  const fillIndex = (index: number) => {
    if (remaining <= 0) return;
    if (index < 0 || index >= next.length) return;
    const slot = next[index];
    if (slot.id !== slotId || slot.count >= stackSize) return;
    const add = Math.min(remaining, stackSize - slot.count);
    slot.count += add;
    remaining -= add;
  };

  if (typeof preferredIndex === "number") fillIndex(preferredIndex);
  for (let i = 0; i < next.length && remaining > 0; i += 1) fillIndex(i);
  for (let i = 0; i < next.length && remaining > 0; i += 1) {
    if (next[i].id !== null || next[i].count !== 0) continue;
    const add = Math.min(remaining, stackSize);
    next[i] = createSlot(slotId, add);
    remaining -= add;
  }
  return next;
}
```

**Usage pattern** (throughout GameEngine.ts):
```typescript
state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, "arrow", 1) ?? state.inventory;  // +1 arrow
state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, "iron_spear", 1) ?? state.inventory;  // +1 spear
```

```
# Fishing Feature: Validation + Execution Plan

## Part 1 — Validation of each established fact (read against the code)

### Water aim / `waterSurfaceRaycast` — CONFIRMED, with a refinement
- `voxelRaycast` (`lib/world/queries.ts:14`) is a 3D-DDA that stops at the first `world.isSolid` cell. `isSolid` (`voxelWorld.ts:53`) returns false for Air and Water, so water is passed through and never a target — `queries.test.ts:62` ("water is not a raycast target") proves it.
- A sibling `waterSurfaceRaycast` reusing the same DDA is correct: walk cells; return the first `BlockId.Water` cell hit; return null if a solid cell (`world.isSolid`) is hit first or `maxDist` is exceeded. `world.get` returns `BlockId.Air` out of bounds (`voxelWorld.ts:44`), so a ray leaving the world correctly yields null (no false water hit).
- Eye ray pattern confirmed identical across `interact.ts:61`, `mining.ts:14-17`: `eye = (px, py + EYE_HEIGHT, pz)` + `lookDirection(yaw, pitch, dir)`. `lookDirection` lives in `systems/playerMotion.ts:40`.
- **Refinement (decision flag):** requiring the cell above the hit to be Air (`world.get(x, y+1, z) === BlockId.Air`) makes the bobber land on the water *surface* rather than a submerged cell when the player aims steeply down into deep water. Recommended: include the air-above guard. Return type should mirror `RaycastResult` minimally — I recommend returning `THREE.Vector3 | null` (just the water cell), since the bobber only needs the cell, not `previous`/`distance`.

### Bobber = single nullable session field — CONFIRMED
- `GameRenderer.sync()` reads transient arrays **directly** from engine state, not the snapshot: `state.thrownSpears` (`GameRenderer.ts:186`), `state.projectiles` (`:187`), `state.mobs` (`:185`). A `state.fishing` field is read the same way. Session arrays are never serialized (`state.ts:163-166`; `serialize()` omits them, `GameEngine.ts:410`).
- A single nullable `state.fishing: FishingState | null` renders cleanly with a `bobberVisuals` that mirrors `projectileVisuals.ts` but for one optional mesh + one line:
  - create in the constructor after `this.projectileVisuals = ...` (`GameRenderer.ts:151`)
  - sync after `this.projectileVisuals.sync(...)` (`GameRenderer.ts:187`): `this.bobberVisuals.sync(state.fishing)`
  - dispose after `this.projectileVisuals.dispose()` (`GameRenderer.ts:469`)
- Shape recommendation: `FishingState = { position: THREE.Vector3; timer: number; biting: boolean }` is sufficient. Add `state.fishing: FishingState | null` to `GameState` (default `null` in the constructor object at `GameEngine.ts:124-171`) and clear it in `respawn()` (`GameEngine.ts:565`, alongside `state.thrownSpears = []`).

### Right-click flow / `tryFish` placement — CONFIRMED
- Precedence in `case "placeBlock"` (`GameEngine.ts:326-339`): throwSpear → feed → trade → interactBlock → summonBoss → useHeldItem → placeBlock, all gated by `isDead || inventoryOpen || sleepTimer>0` (`:327`).
- Insert `if (tryFish(state, this.emit, this.rng)) break;` immediately before `tryUseHeldItem` (`:337`). Safe because:
  - `tryThrowSelectedSpear` (`:329`) returns false for a non-`_spear` item (`spears.ts:23`).
  - `tryUseHeldItem` (`interact.ts:184-192`) early-returns false for any item that isn't hoe/seeds/torch/sapling/bone_meal — the rod falls through.
  - `placeSelectedBlock` (`mining.ts:156`) requires `slot.kind === "block"`, so a tool never places.
  - **Without `tryFish`, the rod's right-click currently does nothing** — so `tryFish` is both safe and necessary.
- Casting-while-active is already gated: `tryFish` reels when `state.fishing` exists, only casts when it's null. Correct.

### `tryFish` rng usage — note
`tryUseHeldItem`/`trySummonBoss` already receive `this.rng`. `tryFish` needs rng for the bite-delay roll and the loot roll, so pass `this.rng`. Signature: `tryFish(state, emit, rng): boolean`.

### Tick / `tickFishing` — CONFIRMED, with cancel detail
- New `systems/fishing.ts` `tickFishing(state, dt, rng)` called in `GameEngine.step` near `tickThrownSpears` (`GameEngine.ts:258`).
- Logic: if `!state.fishing` return; decrement `timer`; `!biting && timer<=0` → `biting=true`, `timer=FISHING_BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS`, emit `fishingBite`; `biting && timer<=0` → missed → `biting=false`, `timer=` new random delay (no event, or an optional miss event).
- Auto-cancel (`state.fishing = null`) when: held item isn't `fishing_rod`, player `isDead`, the bobber's cell `world.get(floor(pos)) !== BlockId.Water`, or `player.position.distanceTo(bobber.position) > FISHING_TETHER_DISTANCE`. **Important:** `step()` early-returns while dead (`:227`) and while sleeping (`:241`) before reaching the tick block — so the held-item/dead cancel mostly matters for the held-item-switch and water-drained cases. That's fine; the dead path simply leaves `state.fishing` stale until the next live tick clears it (it won't render specially). Optionally also clear `state.fishing` in `respawn()` for cleanliness (recommended).

### Items / durability — CONFIRMED, rod shape is safe
- Rod `{ id:"fishing_rod", label:"Fishing Rod", kind:"tool", minePower:0, mineTier:0, maxDurability:64 }` fits `ItemDef` (`types.ts:8`). `createSlot` (`items.ts:229`) sets `durability`/`maxDurability` for `kind:"tool"` with `maxDurability`. `maxStackSizeForItem` returns 1 (`items.ts:218`) → non-stackable. `consumeToolDurability` (`inventory.ts:78`) works on tools and empties the slot at zero.
- **Mining (left-click held) is safe with `minePower:0`:** `tickMining` only runs on `leftMouseHeld` (`mining.ts:78`). With the rod, `tier = 0` and `miningSpeed = minePower ?? BARE_HAND = 0` (`mining.ts:37`), so `mining.progress += dt*0*RATE = 0` — never breaks anything, no divide-by-zero (it is a multiply). It would only ever show progress 0 (i.e. no crack). Acceptable.
- **Left-click attack is safe:** rod is `kind:"tool"`, not `"weapon"`, so `weaponDamage` returns `FIST_DAMAGE` (`combat.ts:25-29`) and `weaponReach` returns `ATTACK_REACH` (`:31-35`) — the rod meleed acts as a fist, exactly like a pickaxe. On a landed hit the engine drains 1 durability (`GameEngine.ts:353`), same as any tool used as a fist. This is existing behavior — acceptable; flag if you'd rather the rod not take melee wear (would need a special-case, not recommended).
- **Correction to the prompt's claim about sprites:** "food/tool items without a custom grid fall through to the checker" is only **half right**:
  - `raw_fish`/`cooked_fish` (`kind:"food"`) → fall through ALL branches in `renderSpritePixels` to the magenta `UNKNOWN_GRID` (`spritePixels.ts:788`). **They MUST have `ITEM_SPRITE_GRIDS` entries** or `spritePixels.test.ts:16-24` (no item may equal the placeholder) fails. CONFIRMED required.
  - `fishing_rod` (`kind:"tool"`, not `_hoe`) → renders the shared `PICKAXE_GRID` with a STEEL palette (`spritePixels.ts:779` via `materialFor` fallback). It does **not** hit the magenta checker, so the no-magenta test passes even without a custom grid. A custom grid is recommended for UX, **not** required for tests.
  - **But there is a second test to mind:** `spritePixels.test.ts:57-65` asserts every tool/weapon prefix has a `MATERIAL_PALETTES` entry unless the id is in the `customGrid` exempt set `["knife","bow"]`. The rod's prefix is "fishing", which has no palette. So if you give the rod a custom grid you MUST add `"fishing_rod"` to that exempt set; if you do NOT give it a grid you MUST add a `"fishing"` entry to `MATERIAL_PALETTES`. **Recommended:** add a custom `FISHING_ROD_GRID` + add `"fishing_rod"` to the exempt set (cleanest, best-looking).

### Recipes — CONFIRMED
- `fishing_rod` recipe (3 wood + 2 string), result kind `tool` → auto-categorized "Tools" by `recipeCategory` (`recipes.ts:481-486`). No category wiring needed.
- `cook_fish` / `cook_fish_charcoal` with `station:"furnace"` → auto-categorized "Smelting", mirroring `cook_chicken`/`cook_chicken_charcoal` (`recipes.ts:60-79`). Add both to `CRAFTING_RECIPES`.

### Loot style — RECOMMENDATION: weighted single-pick
Existing `mobLoot`/`dungeonLoot` use independent `{itemId,min,max,chance?}` rolls (each entry rolled separately), which can yield zero or multiple items. For "one bite = one catch", a **weighted single-pick** is cleaner and correct. Recommend a self-contained `lib/game/fishingLoot.ts`:
- `FISHING_LOOT: Array<{ itemId: string; weight: number; min?: number; max?: number }>` (mostly raw_fish; junk = string/bone/seeds/rotten_flesh; rare emerald).
- `rollFishingCatch(rng): Array<{itemId,count}>` picks one entry by cumulative weight (clamp rng with the same `clampUnit` guard used elsewhere), returns a single-element array.
- Add `clampUnit` locally (mirrors `mobLoot.ts:49`).

### Config — CONFIRMED
Add a "Fishing" section to `config.ts`: `FISHING_REACH`, `FISHING_BITE_MIN_SECONDS`, `FISHING_BITE_MAX_SECONDS`, `FISHING_BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS` (~1.2), `FISHING_TETHER_DISTANCE`, `FISHING_ROD_DURABILITY` (64). No `WORLDGEN_VERSION` change.

### Audio + GameEvent — CONFIRMED
- Add SoundDefs to `soundParams.ts` (`FISHING_CAST_SOUND`, `FISHING_BITE_SOUND`, `FISHING_CATCH_SOUND`, optional `FISHING_REEL_EMPTY_SOUND`).
- Import them in `audioDirector.ts` and add cases in the `handleEvent` switch (`:190`) for `fishingCast`/`fishingBite`/`fishingCaught`/`fishingReeledEmpty`. No exhaustiveness test breaks (`audioDirector.test.ts` and `soundParams.test.ts` both check fixed subsets only).
- Extend `GameEvent` union in `state.ts` (`:267`) with the four events. `fishingCaught` should carry `{ items: Array<{itemId,count}> }` so the shell can toast it (reusing the `pickedUp` toast pattern at `useMinecraftGame.ts:263`). New events automatically reach `renderer.handleEvent` + `audio.handleEvent` (`useMinecraftGame.ts:269-270`) — no shell loop wiring needed beyond an optional `flashMessage` for `fishingCaught`.

### Save / worldgen — CONFIRMED
`state.fishing` is session-only (never in `serialize()`, `GameEngine.ts:410`). New items persist by string id via `SavedSlot {id,count,durability?}` (`types.ts:66`). No `SaveData` version bump (stays 5), no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump, no `generation.ts` change. `generation.test.ts` stays untouched and green.

## Part 3 — Decision flags to confirm

1. **Loot model:** weighted single-pick (recommended) vs independent-roll. Recommend weighted single-pick — matches "one bite, one catch."
2. **Fishing line (`THREE.Line`):** keep it? It adds modest render complexity (one Line whose endpoints update each frame; the player end must use the eye position passed into `sync`). Recommended: yes, it sells the mechanic and is cheap. Flag if you'd rather ship bobber-only first.
3. **Rod item shape:** `kind:"tool", minePower:0` (recommended — fully supported, mines nothing, frees no special-casing) vs a non-tool durable item (would need new handling for durability display and the held-item model). Recommend `kind:"tool"`. Sub-flag: should swinging the rod at a mob consume durability? Current behavior says yes (it's a fist with a tool held). Recommend leaving as-is.
4. **Water-surface guard:** require Air above the hit water cell (recommended) vs accept any water cell.
5. **Tether/cancel rules:** confirm `FISHING_TETHER_DISTANCE` value and whether water-drained + item-switch + tether are the full cancel set (recommended set). Also confirm whether a missed bite should emit an event/sound (recommend a subtle reel-empty handling only on manual reel; silent on auto-miss, or a faint plip — your call).
6. **Catch toast:** emit `fishingCaught {items}` and flash a `+N Raw Fish` message (recommended) vs silent.
```

> AGENT

The plan is written and validated. Here's the recommendation and what I've prepared.

## Suggested next feature: Fishing 🎣

A self-contained, low-risk addition that gives **water** a purpose (right now it's only a hazard) and adds a relaxed renewable food/loot loop — built almost entirely from patterns the codebase already has.

**The loop (per your choices):** craft a **fishing rod** (3 wood + 2 string) → right-click water to **cast** a bobber → after a random wait it **dips with a splash + sound (a bite)** → **reel in within ~1.2s** to catch — miss the window and it gets away. Catches are **mostly raw fish, sometimes junk (string/bone/seeds/rotten flesh), rarely an emerald**; cook raw fish at a furnace.

**Why it's a clean fit:** the bobber mirrors the existing thrown-spear/arrow lifecycle (session-only state, spawned from the held item, ticked each frame, rendered by reading engine state directly, cleared on reload) — so there's **no save-format or worldgen bump**. Loot reuses the `rollMobDrops`/`adjustSlotCount` pattern, the rod reuses tool durability, and fish reuse the cooked-meat recipe/food pattern.

**Gotchas the Plan agent caught (now baked into the plan):**
- A water-aware raycast is needed — the normal one passes through water.
- The fish items need sprite grids (or they render as magenta), and the rod's "fishing" prefix needs an entry in a tool-palette exempt set — a second sprite test most people would trip on.
- `minePower:0` on the rod is safe (it's a multiply, no divide-by-zero; it just mines nothing and melees as a fist).

The plan lays it out as **4 lint/test-green commits** (items+recipes+sprites → cast/bite/reel mechanic + water raycast → bobber/line rendering + audio → integration test + docs), with the full verify gate including a manual gameplay pass for the new visuals.

```
## Approved Plan:
# Fishing

## Context

Monecraft is a complete survival sandbox (the just-merged Living World feature made
trees/grass renewable). Fishing is a self-contained, low-risk next feature that adds
a relaxed, renewable food/loot loop and gives **water** — currently just a hazard you
avoid — a reason to seek out. The player crafts a **fishing rod**, right-clicks while
aiming at water to **cast** a bobber, waits for a **bite** (the bobber dips with a
splash + sound), and **reels in within a short window** to catch something. It reuses
the engine's established transient-entity, loot-roll, food/cooking, and tool-durability
patterns, so it's mostly wiring — **no save-format or worldgen-version bump** (the
bobber is session-only; new items save by string id).

## Confirmed decisions

- **Skill-timed bite**: cast → random delay → bite (bobber dips, splash) → reel within
  `FISHING_BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS` (~1.2s) to catch; miss it and a new delay starts. The
  bobber keeps fishing until reeled.
- **Catch table = fish + junk + treasure**: mostly `raw_fish`, sometimes junk
  (string/bone/seeds/rotten_flesh), rarely treasure (`emerald`). One fish type.
- **Defaults (baked in):** weighted single-pick loot (one bite = one catch); include a
  `THREE.Line` fishing line; rod is `kind:"tool", minePower:0` (mines nothing, melees as
  a fist — existing behavior); `waterSurfaceRaycast` requires Air above the hit cell;
  cancel a cast on rod-unequip / death / water-drained / beyond-tether; toast the catch.

## Key design facts (validated against the code)

- **Water aim**: `voxelRaycast` (`lib/world/queries.ts`) passes through Water and stops
  at solids, so it can't target water. Add a sibling **`waterSurfaceRaycast(world, origin,
  dir, maxDist): THREE.Vector3 | null`** — same DDA loop, returns the first `BlockId.Water`
  cell (with `Air` above), or `null` if a solid is hit first / no water in reach. Eye ray
  is the standard `eye=(px,py+EYE_HEIGHT,pz)` + `lookDirection(yaw,pitch,dir)` (`systems/playerMotion.ts`).
- **Bobber = one session-only field** `state.fishing: FishingState | null` where
  `FishingState = { position: THREE.Vector3; timer: number; biting: boolean }`. Mirrors
  the thrown-spear/arrow pattern: spawned from the held item, ticked each frame, **rendered
  by reading engine state directly** (`GameRenderer.sync` reads `state.thrownSpears`/
  `state.projectiles` — not the snapshot), never serialized → cleared on reload. Init `null`
  in the GameEngine state object; also clear it in `respawn()`.
- **Right-click flow** (`GameEngine.ts` `case "placeBlock"`): insert
  `if (tryFish(state, this.emit, this.rng)) break;` immediately **before** `tryUseHeldItem`.
  Safe: spear-throw/`tryUseHeldItem` ignore the rod, and `placeSelectedBlock` only places
  `kind:"block"` — so the rod's right-click currently does nothing; `tryFish` claims it.
- **Sprite tests (gotcha)**: `raw_fish`/`cooked_fish` (food) MUST get `ITEM_SPRITE_GRIDS`
  entries or they render the magenta checker → `spritePixels.test.ts` fails. The rod
  (tool) won't hit the checker, but a **second** test asserts every tool prefix has a
  `MATERIAL_PALETTES` entry unless the id is in the `customGrid` exempt set — so give the
  rod a custom grid AND add `"fishing_rod"` to that exempt set.
- **Rod safety**: `minePower:0` → mining progress is `dt*0*RATE = 0` (a multiply, no
  divide-by-zero) so it mines nothing; meleeing with it is fist damage (it's a tool, not a
  weapon) and drains 1 durability per hit — existing tool behavior.

## Implementation (lint/test-green per commit)

### Commit 1 — items, recipes, sprites (pure data)
- `lib/game/items.ts`: add `fishing_rod` (`kind:"tool", minePower:0, mineTier:0, maxDurability:64`),
  `raw_fish` (`kind:"food", hunger:2`), `cooked_fish` (`kind:"food", hunger:6`).
- `lib/ui/spritePixels.ts`: add `FISHING_ROD_GRID` + palette and a fish grid + raw/cooked
  palettes (can reuse `RAW_MEAT_GRID`); register all three in `ITEM_SPRITE_GRIDS`.
- `lib/ui/spritePixels.test.ts`: add `"fishing_rod"` to the tool-prefix exempt set.
- `lib/game/config.ts`: add the Fishing tunables (`FISHING_REACH`, `FISHING_BITE_MIN_SECONDS`,
  `FISHING_BITE_MAX_SECONDS`, `FISHING_BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS`, `FISHING_TETHER_DISTANCE`,
  `FISHING_ROD_DURABILITY`).
- `lib/game/recipes.ts`: `fishing_rod` (3 wood + 2 string → Tools), `cook_fish` (raw_fish +
  coal) and `cook_fish_charcoal` (raw_fish + charcoal), both `station:"furnace"` → cooked_fish.
- Tests: extend `recipes.test.ts` (new recipes resolve, correct categories) and `config.test.ts`.

### Commit 2 — water raycast + cast/bite/reel mechanic
- `lib/world/queries.ts` (+ export in `lib/world/index.ts`): `waterSurfaceRaycast`.
- `lib/game/engine/state.ts`: `FishingState` type; `fishing: FishingState | null` on `GameState`;
  add `GameEvent` variants `fishingCast`, `fishingBite`, `fishingCaught { items }`, `fishingReeledEmpty`.
- `lib/game/fishingLoot.ts` (new): `FISHING_LOOT` weighted table + `rollFishingCatch(rng): Array<{itemId,count}>`
  (one weighted pick; local `clampUnit`).
- `lib/game/engine/systems/fishing.ts` (new): `tryFish(state, emit, rng)` (reel branch when
  `state.fishing` set: success if `biting` → `rollFishingCatch` + `adjustSlotCount` +
  `consumeToolDurability` + emit `fishingCaught`; else clear + `fishingReeledEmpty`; cast branch
  → `waterSurfaceRaycast` → set `state.fishing` + random bite delay + emit `fishingCast`) and
  `tickFishing(state, dt, rng)` (bite/miss transitions + auto-cancel).
- `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`: init `fishing:null`; call `tickFishing` near `tickThrownSpears`;
  add the `tryFish` branch before `tryUseHeldItem`; clear `state.fishing` in `respawn()`.
- Tests: `queries.test.ts` (waterSurfaceRaycast: first water / null on solid-first / null on
  no-water / air-above), new `fishingLoot.test.ts` (valid ids, weighted distribution, one entry),
  new `systems/fishing.test.ts` (cast / bite-after-delay / catch-in-window / empty-reel /
  missed-restart / cancel on switch·water-drained·tether).

### Commit 3 — bobber + line rendering, audio
- `lib/game/render/bobberVisuals.ts` (new): mirror `projectileVisuals.ts` for one optional
  bobber mesh (small red/white sprite or sphere) + a `THREE.Line` (player eye → bobber);
  `sync(fishing, eyePos)` creates/repositions/removes on null-ness; `dispose()` frees geometry/material.
- `lib/game/render/GameRenderer.ts`: field + constructor + `sync` (pass `state.fishing` + eye) + `dispose`.
  Optional: a small splash particle burst on `fishingBite`.
- `lib/game/audio/soundParams.ts`: `FISHING_CAST_SOUND`, `FISHING_BITE_SOUND`, `FISHING_CATCH_SOUND`,
  `FISHING_REEL_EMPTY_SOUND`.
- `lib/game/audio/audioDirector.ts`: import + switch cases for the four events.
- Optional `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`: flash a `+N Raw Fish` toast on `fishingCaught` (reuse the
  `pickedUp` formatter).
- Tests: `bobberVisuals.test.ts` (mesh appears when fishing set, removed on null, no leak).

### Commit 4 — integration test + docs
- `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`: `describe("fishing")` following the chest/door pattern —
  put a rod in the selected slot, place a `BlockId.Water` cell in front, aim at it, dispatch
  `placeBlock` → assert `state.fishing` set; run until `biting`; dispatch again in-window → assert a
  catch in inventory + durability dropped; separate missed-window and cancel-on-switch cases.
- Docs: `manual.md` (player how-to), `reference.md` (rod/fish items + recipes; non-stackable note),
  `tuning.md` (the new constants), `adding-content.md` (the sprite-grid + tool-exempt-set gotcha),
  `save-format.md` (one line: `state.fishing` session-only, no version bump), `testing.md` (new test
  files), `CHANGELOG.md` (feat entry).

## Verification (AGENTS.md gate)

1. `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build` — all
   green. `generation.test.ts` must be **green and unchanged** (confirms no worldgen impact);
   `save.test.ts` unchanged (session-only state, items by id).
2. `bun run test:e2e` (renderer + input touched) for the menu→gameplay smoke.
3. Manual gameplay pass (renderer/appearance change): `bun run dev`, craft a rod, find/place water,
   cast, confirm the bobber + line render, watch for the dip/splash on a bite, reel in-window to
   catch (and miss the window to confirm it gets away), cook raw fish at a furnace.
```

```
5	export type RaycastResult = {
6	  hit: THREE.Vector3;
7	  previous: THREE.Vector3;
8	  /** Ray parameter where the ray enters the hit cell (0 when the origin cell is already solid). */
9	  distance: number;
10	};
11	
12	// DDA voxel traversal. `previous` is the last empty cell before the hit —
13	// face-adjacent to it, never diagonal — which is where placed blocks go.
14	export function voxelRaycast(world: VoxelWorld, origin: THREE.Vector3, direction: THREE.Vector3, maxDist = 6): RaycastResult | null {
15	  const dir = direction.clone().normalize();
16	  const pos = origin.clone();
17	
18	  let x = Math.floor(pos.x);
19	  let y = Math.floor(pos.y);
20	  let z = Math.floor(pos.z);
21	
22	  const stepX = dir.x > 0 ? 1 : -1;
23	  const stepY = dir.y > 0 ? 1 : -1;
24	  const stepZ = dir.z > 0 ? 1 : -1;
25	
26	  const invDx = Math.abs(1 / (dir.x || 1e-6));
27	  const invDy = Math.abs(1 / (dir.y || 1e-6));
28	  const invDz = Math.abs(1 / (dir.z || 1e-6));
29	
30	  let tMaxX = ((stepX > 0 ? x + 1 : x) - pos.x) / (dir.x || 1e-6);
31	  let tMaxY = ((stepY > 0 ? y + 1 : y) - pos.y) / (dir.y || 1e-6);
32	  let tMaxZ = ((stepZ > 0 ? z + 1 : z) - pos.z) / (dir.z || 1e-6);
33	  if (tMaxX < 0) tMaxX += invDx;
34	  if (tMaxY < 0) tMaxY += invDy;
35	  if (tMaxZ < 0) tMaxZ += invDz;
36	
37	  let t = 0;
38	  let previous = new THREE.Vector3(x, y, z);
39	
40	  while (t <= maxDist) {
41	    if (world.isSolid(x, y, z)) return { hit: new THREE.Vector3(x, y, z), previous, distance: t };
42	    previous = new THREE.Vector3(x, y, z);
43	
44	    if (tMaxX < tMaxY) {
45	      if (tMaxX < tMaxZ) {
46	        x += stepX;
47	        t = tMaxX;
48	        tMaxX += invDx;
49	      } else {
50	        z += stepZ;
51	        t = tMaxZ;
52	        tMaxZ += invDz;
53	      }
54	    } else if (tMaxY < tMaxZ) {
55	      y += stepY;
56	      t = tMaxY;
57	      tMaxY += invDy;
58	    } else {
59	      z += stepZ;
60	      t = tMaxZ;
61	      tMaxZ += invDz;
62	    }
63	  }
64	
65	  return null;
66	}

68	// AABB-vs-voxel test. `position` is the feet center; the box extends halfWidth
69	// on x/z and height on y. Water never collides.
70	export function collidesAt(world: VoxelWorld, position: THREE.Vector3, halfWidth: number, height: number): boolean {
71	  const eps = 0.001;
72	  const minX = Math.floor(position.x - halfWidth + eps);
73	  const maxX = Math.floor(position.x + halfWidth - eps);
74	  const minZ = Math.floor(position.z - halfWidth + eps);
75	  const maxZ = Math.floor(position.z + halfWidth - eps);
76	  const minY = Math.floor(position.y + eps);
77	  const maxY = Math.floor(position.y + height - eps);
78	
79	  for (let y = minY; y <= maxY; y += 1) {
80	    for (let z = minZ; z <= maxZ; z += 1) {
81	      for (let x = minX; x <= maxX; x += 1) {

83	        if (!world.isSolid(x, y, z)) continue;
84	        if (!isDoorBlock(block)) return true;
85	        const bounds = doorBounds(block)!;
86	        const bodyMinX = position.x - halfWidth + eps;
87	        const bodyMaxX = position.x + halfWidth - eps;
88	        const bodyMinZ = position.z - halfWidth + eps;
89	        const bodyMaxZ = position.z + halfWidth - eps;
90	        if (bodyMaxX > x + bounds.minX && bodyMinX < x + bounds.maxX && bodyMaxZ > z + bounds.minZ && bodyMinZ < z + bounds.maxZ) return true;
91	      }
92	    }
93	  }
94	
95	  return false;

98	export function hasSupportUnderPlayer(world: VoxelWorld, position: THREE.Vector3, halfWidth: number): boolean {
99	  const minX = Math.floor(position.x - halfWidth);
100	  const maxX = Math.floor(position.x + halfWidth);
101	  const minZ = Math.floor(position.z - halfWidth);
102	  const maxZ = Math.floor(position.z + halfWidth);
103	  const y = Math.floor(position.y - 0.05);
104	
105	  for (let z = minZ; z <= maxZ; z += 1) {
106	    for (let x = minX; x <= maxX; x += 1) {
107	      if (world.isSolid(x, y, z)) return true;
108	    }
109	  }
110
```

```json
  "old_string": "// AABB-vs-voxel test. `position` is the feet center; the box extends halfWidth",
  "new_string": "/**\n * Marches the ray and returns the first Water cell whose cell above is Air — the\n * water *surface* the player is aiming at (for casting a fishing bobber). Returns\n * null if a solid block is hit first (you can't fish through terrain) or no such\n * water cell is reached within `maxDist`. Mirrors `voxelRaycast`'s DDA; the normal\n * raycast can't be reused because it treats water as empty and passes through it.\n */\nexport function waterSurfaceRaycast(world: VoxelWorld, origin: THREE.Vector3, direction: THREE.Vector3, maxDist = 7): THREE.Vector3 | null {\n  const dir = direction.clone().normalize();\n  const pos = origin.clone();\n\n  let x = Math.floor(pos.x);\n  let y = Math.floor(pos.y);\n  let z = Math.floor(pos.z);\n\n  const stepX = dir.x > 0 ? 1 : -1;\n  const stepY = dir.y > 0 ? 1 : -1;\n  const stepZ = dir.z > 0 ? 1 : -1;\n\n  const invDx = Math.abs(1 / (dir.x || 1e-6));\n  const invDy = Math.abs(1 / (dir.y || 1e-6));\n  const invDz = Math.abs(1 / (dir.z || 1e-6));\n\n  let tMaxX = ((stepX > 0 ? x + 1 : x) - pos.x) / (dir.x || 1e-6);\n  let tMaxY = ((stepY > 0 ? y + 1 : y) - pos.y) / (dir.y || 1e-6);\n  let tMaxZ = ((stepZ > 0 ? z + 1 : z) - pos.z) / (dir.z || 1e-6);\n  if (tMaxX < 0) tMaxX += invDx;\n  if (tMaxY < 0) tMaxY += invDy;\n  if (tMaxZ < 0) tMaxZ += invDz;\n\n  let t = 0;\n  while (t <= maxDist) {\n    if (world.isSolid(x, y, z)) return null; // terrain blocks the cast\n    if (world.get(x, y, z) === BlockId.Water && world.get(x, y + 1, z) === BlockId.Air) {\n      return new THREE.Vector3(x, y, z);\n    }\n\n    if (tMaxX < tMaxY) {\n      if (tMaxX < tMaxZ) {\n        x += stepX;\n        t = tMaxX;\n        tMaxX += invDx;\n      } else {\n        z += stepZ;\n        t = tMaxZ;\n        tMaxZ += invDz;\n      }\n    } else if (tMaxY < tMaxZ) {\n      y += stepY;\n      t = tMaxY;\n      tMaxY += invDy;\n    } else {\n      z += stepZ;\n      t = tMaxZ;\n      tMaxZ += invDz;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return null;\n}\n\n// AABB-vs-voxel test. `position` is the feet center; the box extends halfWidth"
}
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/fishingLoot.ts",
  "content": "/**\n * The fishing catch table: one weighted pick per bite. Mostly raw fish, sometimes\n * junk (string/bone/seeds/rotten flesh), rarely a treasure (emerald/leather).\n * Weights are relative — summed at roll time — so adding an entry only reweights\n * the odds. Mirrors the other loot rollers' output shape so a catch is added to\n * the inventory the same way (`adjustSlotCount`).\n */\n\nexport type FishingLootEntry = {\n  itemId: string;\n  weight: number;\n  min?: number;\n  max?: number;\n};\n\nexport const FISHING_LOOT: FishingLootEntry[] = [\n  // Fish — the bulk of every catch table.\n  { itemId: \"raw_fish\", weight: 68, min: 1, max: 1 },\n  // Junk.\n  { itemId: \"string\", weight: 8 },\n  { itemId: \"bone\", weight: 7 },\n  { itemId: \"seeds\", weight: 6 },\n  { itemId: \"rotten_flesh\", weight: 5 },\n  // Treasure (rare).\n  { itemId: \"emerald\", weight: 3 },\n  { itemId: \"leather\", weight: 3 }\n];\n\nconst clampUnit = (v: number): number => (v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v);\n\n/** One weighted pick from FISHING_LOOT. `rng` is injectable for deterministic tests. */\nexport function rollFishingCatch(rng: () => number): Array<{ itemId: string; count: number }> {\n  const total = FISHING_LOOT.reduce((sum, entry) => sum + entry.weight, 0);\n  let roll = clampUnit(rng()) * total;\n  for (const entry of FISHING_LOOT) {\n    roll -= entry.weight;\n    if (roll < 0) {\n      const min = entry.min ?? 1;\n      const max = entry.max ?? 1;\n      const count = min + Math.floor(clampUnit(rng()) * (max - min + 1));\n      return [{ itemId: entry.itemId, count }];\n    }\n  }\n  // Floating-point guard: a roll landing exactly at the total falls to the last entry.\n  const last = FISHING_LOOT[FISHING_LOOT.length - 1];\n  return [{ itemId: last.itemId, count: last.min ?? 1 }];\n}\n"
}
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/fishing.ts",
  "content": "import * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport { BlockId, waterSurfaceRaycast } from \"@/lib/world\";\nimport {\n  EYE_HEIGHT,\n  FISHING_BITE_MAX_SECONDS,\n  FISHING_BITE_MIN_SECONDS,\n  FISHING_BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS,\n  FISHING_REACH,\n  FISHING_TETHER_DISTANCE\n} from \"@/lib/game/config\";\nimport { rollFishingCatch } from \"@/lib/game/fishingLoot\";\nimport { adjustSlotCount, consumeToolDurability } from \"@/lib/game/inventory\";\nimport type { EmitGameEvent, GameState } from \"../state\";\nimport { lookDirection } from \"./playerMotion\";\n\nconst scratchEye = new THREE.Vector3();\nconst scratchDir = new THREE.Vector3();\n\nfunction nextBiteDelay(rng: () => number): number {\n  return FISHING_BITE_MIN_SECONDS + rng() * (FISHING_BITE_MAX_SECONDS - FISHING_BITE_MIN_SECONDS);\n}\n\nfunction isHoldingRod(state: GameState): boolean {\n  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];\n  return slot?.id === \"fishing_rod\" && slot.count > 0;\n}\n\n/**\n * Right-click with a fishing rod: reel in the active cast (a catch if the bobber\n * is biting, otherwise nothing), or cast a new bobber at the aimed water surface.\n * Returns true whenever a rod is held (it always consumes the right-click), false\n * for any other item so the normal held-item/placement path runs.\n */\nexport function tryFish(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent, rng: () => number): boolean {\n  if (!isHoldingRod(state)) return false;\n\n  if (state.fishing) {\n    if (state.fishing.biting) {\n      const items = rollFishingCatch(rng);\n      for (const drop of items) {\n        state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, drop.itemId, drop.count) ?? state.inventory;\n      }\n      state.inventory = consumeToolDurability(state.inventory, state.selectedSlot, 1) ?? state.inventory;\n      emit({ type: \"fishingCaught\", items });\n    } else {\n      emit({ type: \"fishingReeledEmpty\" });\n    }\n    state.fishing = null;\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  const { world, player } = state;\n  scratchEye.set(player.position.x, player.position.y + EYE_HEIGHT, player.position.z);\n  lookDirection(player.yaw, player.pitch, scratchDir);\n  const cell = waterSurfaceRaycast(world, scratchEye, scratchDir, FISHING_REACH);\n  if (!cell) return true; // the rod still claims the click; there's just no water to cast at\n\n  state.fishing = {\n    position: new THREE.Vector3(cell.x + 0.5, cell.y + 1, cell.z + 0.5),\n    timer: nextBiteDelay(rng),\n    biting: false\n  };\n  emit({ type: \"fishingCast\" });\n  return true;\n}\n\n/**\n * Advances the active cast: count down to a bite, open the reel window, then let\n * the catch escape (restarting the wait) if it isn't reeled in time. Auto-cancels\n * the cast when the rod is no longer held, the player dies, the targeted water is\n * gone, or the player wanders past the tether.\n */\nexport function tickFishing(state: GameState, dt: number, rng: () => number, emit: EmitGameEvent): void {\n  const fishing = state.fishing;\n  if (!fishing) return;\n\n  const wx = Math.floor(fishing.position.x);\n  const wy = Math.floor(fishing.position.y) - 1;\n  const wz = Math.floor(fishing.position.z);\n  if (\n    state.isDead ||\n    !isHoldingRod(state) ||\n    state.world.get(wx, wy, wz) !== BlockId.Water ||\n    state.player.position.distanceTo(fishing.position) > FISHING_TETHER_DISTANCE\n  ) {\n    state.fishing = null;\n    return;\n  }\n\n  fishing.timer -= dt;\n  if (fishing.timer > 0) return;\n\n  if (fishing.biting) {\n    fishing.biting = false;\n    fishing.timer = nextBiteDelay(rng);\n  } else {\n    fishing.biting = true;\n    fishing.timer = FISHING_BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS;\n    emit({ type: \"fishingBite\" });\n  }\n}\n"
}
```

```json
  "content": "import { describe, expect, test } from \"bun:test\";\nimport { ITEM_DEF_BY_ID } from \"@/lib/game/items\";\nimport { FISHING_LOOT, rollFishingCatch } from \"@/lib/game/fishingLoot\";\n\n/** rng that yields a fixed sequence, then repeats the last value. */\nfunction seq(...values: number[]): () => number {\n  let i = 0;\n  return () => values[Math.min(i++, values.length - 1)];\n}\n\ndescribe(\"fishing loot\", () => {\n  test(\"every loot entry references a real item\", () => {\n    for (const entry of FISHING_LOOT) {\n      expect(ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[entry.itemId], entry.itemId).toBeDefined();\n    }\n  });\n\n  test(\"a roll always yields exactly one catch of a real item with a positive count\", () => {\n    for (let i = 0; i <= 20; i += 1) {\n      const result = rollFishingCatch(seq(i / 20, 0.5));\n      expect(result).toHaveLength(1);\n      expect(ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[result[0].itemId]).toBeDefined();\n      expect(result[0].count).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);\n    }\n  });\n\n  test(\"a low roll yields the common raw fish\", () => {\n    expect(rollFishingCatch(seq(0, 0))).toEqual([{ itemId: \"raw_fish\", count: 1 }]);\n  });\n\n  test(\"a high roll reaches the rare treasure tier\", () => {\n    // Weights sum to 100; the treasure entries sit at the top of the range.\n    const result = rollFishingCatch(seq(0.99, 0));\n    expect([\"emerald\", \"leather\"]).toContain(result[0].itemId);\n  });\n});\n"
}
```
