  "content": "import { describe, expect, test } from \"bun:test\";\nimport * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport { BlockId, VoxelWorld } from \"@/lib/world\";\nimport { FISHING_BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS } from \"@/lib/game/config\";\nimport { countsById } from \"@/lib/game/inventory\";\nimport { createEmptySlot, createSlot } from \"@/lib/game/items\";\nimport type { GameEvent, GameState } from \"../state\";\nimport { tickFishing, tryFish } from \"./fishing\";\n\n/**\n * Minimal GameState with just the fields the fishing system reads. A water surface\n * sits at (8,7,5); the player at (8.5,6,8.5) looking -Z aims straight at it.\n */\nfunction makeState(): GameState {\n  const world = new VoxelWorld(16, 16, 16, 1);\n  world.set(8, 7, 5, BlockId.Water); // air above by default → a castable surface\n  const inventory = Array.from({ length: 9 }, () => createEmptySlot());\n  inventory[0] = createSlot(\"fishing_rod\", 1);\n  return {\n    world,\n    inventory,\n    selectedSlot: 0,\n    fishing: null,\n    isDead: false,\n    player: { position: new THREE.Vector3(8.5, 6, 8.5), velocity: new THREE.Vector3(), yaw: 0, pitch: 0, onGround: true }\n  } as unknown as GameState;\n}\n\nfunction collector(): { emit: (e: GameEvent) => void; events: GameEvent[] } {\n  const events: GameEvent[] = [];\n  return { emit: (e) => events.push(e), events };\n}\n\ndescribe(\"fishing\", () => {\n  test(\"right-clicking the rod at water casts a bobber and emits fishingCast\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    const { emit, events } = collector();\n    expect(tryFish(state, emit, () => 0.5)).toBe(true);\n    expect(state.fishing).not.toBeNull();\n    expect(state.fishing!.biting).toBe(false);\n    expect(events.some((e) => e.type === \"fishingCast\")).toBe(true);\n  });\n\n  test(\"aiming the rod away from water consumes the click but starts no cast\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    state.player.pitch = 1.4; // look up at the sky\n    const { emit, events } = collector();\n    expect(tryFish(state, emit, () => 0.5)).toBe(true);\n    expect(state.fishing).toBeNull();\n    expect(events.some((e) => e.type === \"fishingCast\")).toBe(false);\n  });\n\n  test(\"a non-rod item is left to the normal placement path\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    state.inventory[0] = createSlot(\"dirt\", 10);\n    const { emit } = collector();\n    expect(tryFish(state, emit, () => 0.5)).toBe(false);\n  });\n\n  test(\"the bobber bites after the delay and emits fishingBite\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    tryFish(state, () => {}, () => 0); // timer = bite min\n    const { emit, events } = collector();\n    tickFishing(state, 5, () => 0, emit); // dt past the whole delay\n    expect(state.fishing!.biting).toBe(true);\n    expect(events.some((e) => e.type === \"fishingBite\")).toBe(true);\n  });\n\n  test(\"reeling during the bite window yields a catch and drains durability\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    state.fishing = { position: new THREE.Vector3(8.5, 8, 5.5), timer: 1, biting: true };\n    const { emit, events } = collector();\n    tryFish(state, emit, () => 0); // rng 0 → the common raw fish\n    expect(countsById(state.inventory).get(\"raw_fish\")).toBe(1);\n    expect(state.inventory[0].durability).toBe(state.inventory[0].maxDurability! - 1);\n    expect(state.fishing).toBeNull();\n    expect(events.some((e) => e.type === \"fishingCaught\")).toBe(true);\n  });\n\n  test(\"reeling with no bite comes back empty\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    state.fishing = { position: new THREE.Vector3(8.5, 8, 5.5), timer: 2, biting: false };\n    const { emit, events } = collector();\n    tryFish(state, emit, () => 0);\n    expect(countsById(state.inventory).get(\"raw_fish\")).toBeUndefined();\n    expect(state.inventory[0].durability).toBe(state.inventory[0].maxDurability!); // no wear on an empty reel\n    expect(state.fishing).toBeNull();\n    expect(events.some((e) => e.type === \"fishingReeledEmpty\")).toBe(true);\n  });\n\n  test(\"a missed bite window restarts the wait\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    state.fishing = { position: new THREE.Vector3(8.5, 8, 5.5), timer: 0.01, biting: true };\n    tickFishing(state, 1, () => 0, () => {});\n    expect(state.fishing).not.toBeNull();\n    expect(state.fishing!.biting).toBe(false);\n    expect(state.fishing!.timer).toBeGreaterThan(FISHING_BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS);\n  });\n\n  test(\"the cast cancels when the rod is unequipped\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    state.fishing = { position: new THREE.Vector3(8.5, 8, 5.5), timer: 2, biting: false };\n    state.selectedSlot = 1; // empty slot\n    tickFishing(state, 0.1, () => 0, () => {});\n    expect(state.fishing).toBeNull();\n  });\n\n  test(\"the cast cancels when the targeted water drains\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    state.fishing = { position: new THREE.Vector3(8.5, 8, 5.5), timer: 2, biting: false };\n    state.world.set(8, 7, 5, BlockId.Air); // the water under the bobber is gone\n    tickFishing(state, 0.1, () => 0, () => {});\n    expect(state.fishing).toBeNull();\n  });\n\n  test(\"the cast cancels when the player strays past the tether\", () => {\n    const state = makeState();\n    state.fishing = { position: new THREE.Vector3(8.5, 8, 5.5), timer: 2, biting: false };\n    state.player.position.set(8.5, 6, 60);\n    tickFishing(state, 0.1, () => 0, () => {});\n    expect(state.fishing).toBeNull();\n  });\n});\n"

1	import * as THREE from "three";
2	import { renderSpritePixels } from "@/lib/ui/spritePixels";
3	import type { ProjectileState } from "@/lib/game/engine/state";
4	import { buildExtrudedSpriteGeometry } from "./extrudedSprite";
5	
6	export type ProjectileVisuals = {
7	  /** Creates/removes arrow meshes to match the projectile list and orients each along its flight. */
8	  sync(projectiles: ProjectileState[]): void;
9	  dispose(): void;
10	};
11	
12	// The arrow sprite is drawn pointing up (+Y); rotate that axis onto the velocity.
13	const UP_Y = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0);
14	const scratchDir = new THREE.Vector3();
15	const scratchQuat = new THREE.Quaternion();
16	
17	/**
18	 * Renders in-flight arrows. One extruded-sprite geometry and one material are
19	 * shared across every live arrow — only each mesh's transform differs — so the
20	 * pool allocates nothing per shot and frees both once on dispose().
21	 */
22	export function createProjectileVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): ProjectileVisuals {
23	  const geometry = buildExtrudedSpriteGeometry(renderSpritePixels("arrow"));
24	  const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ vertexColors: true, roughness: 0.6, metalness: 0.1 });
25	  const meshes = new Map<number, THREE.Mesh>();
26	  const seen = new Set<number>();
27	
28	  const removeMesh = (id: number): void => {
29	    const mesh = meshes.get(id);
30	    if (!mesh) return;
31	    scene.remove(mesh);
32	    meshes.delete(id);
33	  };
34	
35	  return {
36	    sync(projectiles) {
37	      seen.clear();
38	      for (const p of projectiles) {
39	        seen.add(p.id);
40	        let mesh = meshes.get(p.id);
41	        if (!mesh) {
42	          mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
43	          meshes.set(p.id, mesh);
44	          scene.add(mesh);
45	        }
46	        mesh.position.set(p.position.x, p.position.y, p.position.z);
47	        if (p.velocity.lengthSq() > 1e-6) {
48	          scratchDir.copy(p.velocity).normalize();
49	          mesh.quaternion.copy(scratchQuat.setFromUnitVectors(UP_Y, scratchDir));
50	        }
51	      }
52	      for (const id of meshes.keys()) {
53	        if (!seen.has(id)) removeMesh(id);
54	      }
55	    },
56	
57	    dispose() {
58	      for (const id of [...meshes.keys()]) removeMesh(id);
59	      geometry.dispose();
60	      material.dispose();
61	    }
62	  };
63	}
64

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/bobberVisuals.ts",
  "content": "import * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport type { FishingState } from \"@/lib/game/engine/state\";\n\nexport type BobberVisuals = {\n  /** Shows the bobber + line when a cast is active, hides them otherwise. */\n  sync(fishing: FishingState | null, eye: THREE.Vector3): void;\n  dispose(): void;\n};\n\n/**\n * Renders the single active fishing bobber: a small red float on the water and a\n * taut line from the player's eye to it. The bobber dips slightly while a fish is\n * biting. One mesh, one line, one geometry/material each — added to the scene only\n * while fishing, removed when the cast ends or on dispose().\n */\nexport function createBobberVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): BobberVisuals {\n  const bobberGeometry = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.11, 8, 6);\n  const bobberMaterial = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xd03c34, roughness: 0.5 });\n  const bobber = new THREE.Mesh(bobberGeometry, bobberMaterial);\n\n  const linePositions = new Float32Array(6);\n  const lineGeometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();\n  lineGeometry.setAttribute(\"position\", new THREE.BufferAttribute(linePositions, 3));\n  const lineMaterial = new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color: 0xdedede });\n  const line = new THREE.Line(lineGeometry, lineMaterial);\n\n  let present = false;\n  const setPresent = (next: boolean): void => {\n    if (next === present) return;\n    present = next;\n    if (next) scene.add(bobber, line);\n    else scene.remove(bobber, line);\n  };\n\n  return {\n    sync(fishing, eye) {\n      if (!fishing) {\n        setPresent(false);\n        return;\n      }\n      setPresent(true);\n      const dip = fishing.biting ? -0.09 : 0; // the strike pulls the float under\n      bobber.position.set(fishing.position.x, fishing.position.y + dip, fishing.position.z);\n      linePositions[0] = eye.x;\n      linePositions[1] = eye.y;\n      linePositions[2] = eye.z;\n      linePositions[3] = bobber.position.x;\n      linePositions[4] = bobber.position.y;\n      linePositions[5] = bobber.position.z;\n      lineGeometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;\n    },\n\n    dispose() {\n      setPresent(false);\n      bobberGeometry.dispose();\n      bobberMaterial.dispose();\n      lineGeometry.dispose();\n      lineMaterial.dispose();\n    }\n  };\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "    const stage = state.world.get(x, y, z);\n    expect(stage).toBeGreaterThan(BlockId.WheatStage0);\n    expect(stage).toBeLessThanOrEqual(BlockId.WheatStage3);\n    expect(state.inventory[state.selectedSlot].count).toBe(2);\n    expect(engine.consumeEvents().some((e) => e.type === \"usedBoneMeal\")).toBe(true);\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe(\"fishing\", () => {\n  /** Settles the player, equips a rod, and carves a clear line of sight to a water surface 2 cells ahead (-Z). */\n  function castSetup(engine: GameEngine): { state: GameEngine[\"state\"] } {\n    calmDaytime(engine);\n    engine.state.mobs = [];\n    run(engine, 1);\n    const { state } = engine;\n    const px = Math.floor(state.player.position.x);\n    const pz = Math.floor(state.player.position.z);\n    state.player.position.x = px + 0.5;\n    state.player.position.z = pz + 0.5;\n    state.player.yaw = 0; // looking -Z\n    state.player.pitch = 0;\n    const eyeY = Math.floor(state.player.position.y + EYE_HEIGHT);\n    state.blockChanges.set(px, eyeY, pz - 1, BlockId.Air);\n    state.blockChanges.set(px, eyeY, pz - 2, BlockId.Water);\n    state.blockChanges.set(px, eyeY + 1, pz - 2, BlockId.Air);\n    state.inventory = [...state.inventory];\n    state.inventory[state.selectedSlot] = createSlot(\"fishing_rod\", 1);\n    return { state };\n  }\n\n  test(\"casting at water starts a bobber, and reeling on a bite yields a catch\", () => {\n    const engine = makeEngine();\n    const { state } = castSetup(engine);\n\n    engine.dispatch({ type: \"placeBlock\" });\n    expect(state.fishing).not.toBeNull();\n\n    // Advance until the bite window opens (delay is bounded by FISHING_BITE_MAX_SECONDS).\n    let guard = 0;\n    while (!state.fishing!.biting && guard < 2000) {\n      engine.step(1 / 60, input());\n      guard += 1;\n    }\n    expect(state.fishing!.biting).toBe(true);\n\n    engine.consumeEvents();\n    engine.dispatch({ type: \"placeBlock\" }); // reel in during the bite\n    expect(state.fishing).toBeNull();\n    // A catch always lands and wears the rod one point (the item is random).\n    expect(state.inventory[state.selectedSlot].durability).toBe(state.inventory[state.selectedSlot].maxDurability! - 1);\n    expect(engine.consumeEvents().some((e) => e.type === \"fishingCaught\")).toBe(true);\n  });\n\n  test(\"reeling before a bite comes back empty with no rod wear\", () => {\n    const engine = makeEngine();\n    const { state } = castSetup(engine);\n\n    engine.dispatch({ type: \"placeBlock\" }); // cast\n    expect(state.fishing).not.toBeNull();\n    expect(state.fishing!.biting).toBe(false);\n\n    engine.consumeEvents();\n    engine.dispatch({ type: \"placeBlock\" }); // reel immediately, before any bite\n    expect(state.fishing).toBeNull();\n    expect(state.inventory[state.selectedSlot].durability).toBe(state.inventory[state.selectedSlot].maxDurability);\n    expect(engine.consumeEvents().some((e) => e.type === \"fishingReeledEmpty\")).toBe(true);\n  });\n});"

16	## A new item or recipe
17	
18	- Add to `ITEM_DEFS` in `lib/game/items.ts` — tools take `minePower`/`mineTier`/`maxDurability`, weapons `attack`/`maxDurability`, armor `armorSlot`/`defense`/`maxDurability`. `kind: "food"` items take a `hunger` value (restored on eat); `kind: "material"` items are inert craft ingredients.
19	- Give it an inventory sprite in `lib/ui/spritePixels.ts`: pickaxes, swords, and
20	  spears get one for free when named `<material>_pickaxe`, `<material>_sword`, or
21	  `<material>_spear` and the material exists in `MATERIAL_PALETTES`;
22	  food/material items need a 16×16 grid + palette in `ITEM_SPRITE_GRIDS`. The
23	  sprite integrity test rejects placeholder fallbacks.
24	- Any item with `maxDurability` is automatically non-stackable. Spears also set
25	  `meleeReach` and `throwDamage`; `systems/spears.ts` handles throwing.
26	- `ITEM_DEF_BY_ID` is derived from `ITEM_DEFS`; never edit it directly.
27	- Recipes are `{ id, label, cost: [{slotId, count}], result: {slotId, count} }` in `lib/game/recipes.ts`. An optional `station` makes a recipe station-gated: it only crafts while that station's panel is open, enforced in the `craft` command and shown locked in the recipe book. The stations are `"furnace"` (smelting) and `"villager"` (a **trade** — see below).
28	- **Villager trades** (`lib/game/trades.ts`) ARE just `station: "villager"` recipes spread into `RECIPES`, so they reuse the whole crafting pipeline and recipe-book UI for free. To open them, an interaction sets `state.craftingStation = "villager"` (right-clicking a villager via `tryTradeAimedVillager` in `interact.ts`); the panel then shows the trades as a **Trading** book and the `craft` command runs them. Emerald is the currency — add sell offers (material → emerald) and buy offers (emerald → goods) to keep the economy two-sided. There's no persisted trade state, so this needs no save-format change.
29	- Items with durability don't stack; durability is initialized in `createSlot` and persisted in saves.
30

They are **never serialized** (left out of `serialize()`), so they vanish on reload and must be cleared in `respawn()`.\n- Spawn from the held-item action (e.g. `tryFish`/`tryThrowSelectedSpear` in their systems, wired into the `placeBlock`/`attack` precedence in `GameEngine.ts`), advance them in a per-frame `tick*` system called from `GameEngine.step`, and remove them on expiry/collision/cancel.\n- Render by reading the field **directly from engine state** in `GameRenderer.sync` (the snapshot does not carry them) — add a `*Visuals` module mirroring `projectileVisuals.ts`/`bobberVisuals.ts` (create/sync/dispose, freeing its geometry/material). Because nothing is persisted, there is no save-format or worldgen impact."

Four lint/test-green commits on `feat/fishing`:

**How it plays:** craft a rod (3 wood + 2 string) → right-click water to cast a bobber → after a random 3–9s wait it dips with a splash → right-click within ~1.2s to reel in a catch (mostly raw fish, sometimes junk, rarely an emerald), which wears the rod one point. Miss the window and it gets away while the bobber keeps fishing.

**Design highlights (all validated against the code):**
- The cast is one session-only `state.fishing` field — never serialized, cleared on respawn — mirroring the arrow/spear transient-entity pattern, so **no save or worldgen bump**.
- New `waterSurfaceRaycast` finds the surface to aim at (the normal raycast passes through water).
- Bobber + a `THREE.Line` render by reading engine state directly, mounted only while fishing.
- The rod is a `minePower:0` tool (mines nothing); I fixed the sprite test's tool-palette exemption so custom-grid tools like it are handled correctly.

> AGENT

Confirmed the hooks that already exist, which makes this an easy call. The game already has a `flashMessage` toast (used by `pickedUp` → "+1 Raw Fish"), a particle system, and the `fishingCaught` event already carries the caught `items` — so either path is cheap.

My take: **animation for every catch, a message only for the rare treasure.** Here's the reasoning.

**What the catch already tells the player:** a distinct reel sound, the hotbar count ticking up, and the bobber+line vanishing. So this isn't about *whether* there's feedback — it's about what to add on top.

**Why not a toast on every catch:** fishing is a repetitive loop. A "+1 Raw Fish" popup on every single reel becomes visual spam you stop reading within a minute, and it pulls your eyes to the HUD corner and away from the water. Minecraft itself shows no text when you catch a fish — the fish arcs out of the water with a sound, all diegetic. Toasts are best for things you might *miss* or *need to read*, not for a thing you do 50 times a session.

**Why animation as the default:** an in-world cue (a small splash particle burst at the bobber as you reel, riding the bobber-dip that's already there + the catch sound) is immersive, satisfying, and — crucially — doesn't fatigue with repetition. It says "you caught something!" without making you read.

**Where a message earns its place — the rare treasure.** Animation conveys *feel* but not *what*; a message conveys *what* but spams. So split by frequency: stay silent (animation only) on common fish/junk, and fire a one-line toast **only when you reel in the rare emerald** — the infrequent, exciting moment actually worth calling out. The `fishingCaught` event already carries `items`, so the shell just checks the catch and toasts treasure.

So, concretely:
- **Always:** a splash particle on reel-in (+ the existing dip + sound). ~immersive, no fatigue.
- **Rare only:** reuse `flashMessage` for a treasure catch, e.g. "Reeled in a treasure: Emerald!".

One caveat worth naming: if you care about onboarding clarity (a brand-new player unsure what they got), the cheapest middle ground is a toast on the **first** catch only, then animation-only thereafter — but I'd default to the treasure-only split.

Want me to wire it up? It's small: a `fishingBite`/`fishingCaught` splash via the particle system, plus a treasure-gated `flashMessage` in `useMinecraftGame.ts`. I can add it to the `feat/fishing` branch with tests before you review.

38	const VERTEX_SHADER = /* glsl */ `
39	  attribute vec3 acolor;
40	  attribute float psize;
41	  attribute float palpha;
42	  varying vec3 vColor;
43	  varying float vAlpha;
44	  uniform float uScale;
45	  void main() {
46	    vColor = acolor;
47	    vAlpha = palpha;
48	    vec4 mv = modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
49	    gl_PointSize = max(1.0, psize * uScale / -mv.z);

52	`;

55	  precision mediump float;
56	  varying vec3 vColor;
57	  varying float vAlpha;
58	  void main() {
59	    vec2 d = gl_PointCoord - vec2(0.5);
60	    float r = dot(d, d);
61	    if (r > 0.25) discard;
62	    float edge = smoothstep(0.25, 0.04, r);
63	    gl_FragColor = vec4(vColor, vAlpha * edge);
64	  }
65	`;

67	export function createParticleSystem(scene: THREE.Scene): ParticleSystem {
68	  const pool = createParticlePool();
69	  const cap = pool.cap;
70	
71	  const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
72	  const position = new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(cap * 3), 3);
73	  const acolor = new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(cap * 3), 3);
74	  const psize = new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(cap), 1);
75	  const palpha = new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(cap), 1);
76	  position.setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage);
77	  acolor.setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage);
78	  psize.setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage);
79	  palpha.setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage);
80	  geometry.setAttribute("position", position);
81	  geometry.setAttribute("acolor", acolor);
82	  geometry.setAttribute("psize", psize);
83	  geometry.setAttribute("palpha", palpha);
84	  geometry.setDrawRange(0, 0);
85	
86	  const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
87	    uniforms: { uScale: { value: 620 } },
88	    vertexShader: VERTEX_SHADER,
89	    fragmentShader: FRAGMENT_SHADER,
90	    transparent: true,
91	    depthWrite: false
92	  });
93	
94	  const points = new THREE.Points(geometry, material);
95	  points.frustumCulled = false;
96	  points.raycast = () => {};
97	  points.renderOrder = 4;
98	  scene.add(points);
99	
100	  return {
101	    emitBurst(opts) {
102	      const spread = opts.spread ?? 1;
103	      const [lifeMin, lifeMax] = opts.life ?? [0.3, 0.6];
104	      const size = opts.size ?? 0.14;
105	      const jitter = opts.colorJitter ?? 0;
106	      const upBias = opts.upBias ?? 0;
107	      for (let n = 0; n < opts.count; n += 1) {
108	        // Random direction on a sphere, scaled by speed + per-particle spread.
109	        const theta = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;
110	        const phi = Math.acos(2 * Math.random() - 1);
111	        const sp = opts.speed * (0.5 + Math.random());
112	        spawnParticle(pool, {
113	          x: opts.x,
114	          y: opts.y,
115	          z: opts.z,
116	          vx: Math.sin(phi) * Math.cos(theta) * sp + (Math.random() - 0.5) * spread,
117	          vy: Math.cos(phi) * sp + (Math.random() - 0.5) * spread + upBias,
118	          vz: Math.sin(phi) * Math.sin(theta) * sp + (Math.random() - 0.5) * spread,
119	          life: lifeMin + Math.random() * (lifeMax - lifeMin),
120	          size: size * (0.7 + Math.random() * 0.6),
121	          r: clamp01(opts.color[0] + (Math.random() - 0.5) * jitter),
122	          g: clamp01(opts.color[1] + (Math.random() - 0.5) * jitter),
123	          b: clamp01(opts.color[2] + (Math.random() - 0.5) * jitter),
124	          gravity: opts.gravity ?? 0,
125	          drag: opts.drag ?? 0
126	        });
127	      }
128	    },
129	
130	    update(dtMs) {
131	      updateParticlePool(pool, dtMs / 1000);
132	      const n = pool.count;
133	      const pos = position.array as Float32Array;
134	      const col = acolor.array as Float32Array;
135	      const sz = psize.array as Float32Array;
136	      const al = palpha.array as Float32Array;
137	      for (let i = 0; i < n; i += 1) {
138	        pos[i * 3] = pool.px[i];
139	        pos[i * 3 + 1] = pool.py[i];
140	        pos[i * 3 + 2] = pool.pz[i];
141	        col[i * 3] = pool.cr[i];
142	        col[i * 3 + 1] = pool.cg[i];
143	        col[i * 3 + 2] = pool.cb[i];
144	        sz[i] = pool.size[i];
145	        // Fade out over the back half of life.
146	        const t = pool.age[i] / pool.life[i];
147	        al[i] = t < 0.5 ? 1 : Math.max(0, 1 - (t - 0.5) * 2);
148	      }
149	      geometry.setDrawRange(0, n);
150	      if (n > 0) {
151	        position.needsUpdate = true;
152	        acolor.needsUpdate = true;
153	        psize.needsUpdate = true;
154	        palpha.needsUpdate = true;
155	      }
156	    },
157	
158	    dispose() {
159	      scene.remove(points);
160	      geometry.dispose();
161	      material.dispose();
162	    }
163	  };
164	}

> AGENT

Done — catch feedback implemented exactly as recommended.

## What I added

**Splash animation (always-on, diegetic):**
- A water-blue particle burst when a fish **bites** (a sharp little plume at the bobber) and a bigger one on the **reel-in**, both riding the existing reel sound and bobber dip.
- The `fishingCast`/`fishingBite`/`fishingCaught` events now carry the bobber position so the renderer can place the splash; bursts go through the existing particle system (zero new assets).

**Message (rare only):**
- A one-line toast **only when you reel in the treasure** (emerald), reusing the existing `flashMessage` path. Common fish/junk catches stay silent — splash + sound + the hotbar count tell the story without spamming the HUD, exactly the split we discussed.

## Verification — full gate green
- `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check` ✓
- `bun test` — **585 pass / 0 fail** (fishing tests now also assert the cast/catch events carry the bobber coordinates)
- `bun run build` ✓ · `test:e2e` — **14/14** ✓

The feedback is its own commit (`e027d90`) on top of the four fishing commits, so the branch now has 5 commits. As before, I haven't pushed.

Two things worth a quick decision:
1. **Treasure scope:** I gated the toast to `emerald` only. In the loot table both emerald and leather are the rare tier — I deliberately left leather as a silent "junk-ish" catch. Happy to flip leather into the toast too, or mark treasure in the loot data instead of hardcoding `emerald` in the shell, if you'd prefer.
2. **Push/PR:** want me to push `feat/fishing` and open a PR against `hutusi/monecraft:main`?

> DEVELOPER

the random 3–9s wait fish dips seems too long, is it better be short? what do you think?

> AGENT

Good instinct — 3–9s is on the sluggish side for a browser game's pacing. My take: **shorten it, but don't make it near-instant.**

**Why shorter:** the wait is the whole cost of a catch. The bobber stays cast, so each catch is basically `wait → reel → recast`, and with an average of 6s (worst case 9s) the loop drags — you're staring at a still bobber more than you're doing anything. For reference, Minecraft is 5–30s and is widely considered tedious; we're already well under that, but we can go further since this game's loops are snappier.

**Why not near-instant (1–2s):** a tiny wait kills the small beat of anticipation that makes the bite *feel* like an event rather than a metronome, and — more concretely — bite speed is the throttle on the whole catch table. Faster bites = faster everything, including the rare **emerald treasure** (3% weight). Make bites near-instant and you can farm emeralds in a couple of minutes, which cheapens the villager economy. A modest wait keeps fishing rewarding without trivializing it.

**My recommendation: 2–5s** (avg ~3.5s — roughly halves the current perceived wait while keeping a real "wait for it…" moment). If you want a hair more variance, 2–6s also works. I'd keep the 1.2s reel window as is — at this cadence you're attentive, so the timing still asks something of you.

One coupling to keep in mind: if you ever want bites *much* faster than this, I'd drop the emerald weight a notch to hold the treasure rate steady. At 2–5s it's a small enough change that I'd leave the loot table alone.

It's a two-line change (`FISHING_BITE_MIN_SECONDS` / `FISHING_BITE_MAX_SECONDS` in `config.ts`) plus the "3–9 s" mention in `docs/tuning.md`. Want me to set it to **2–5s**, or pick different bounds?

> DEVELOPER

ok, 2-5s seems good, and remember to update the docs and tests, what do you think?

> AGENT

Agreed — and on the tests: nothing currently pins the bounds (the tests read the constants, so they'd silently pass any values), so I'll add a small guard test that asserts the cast wait actually falls within `[MIN, MAX]`. That way this decision is locked in and a future accidental change gets caught. Let me make the changes.

> AGENT

CodeRabbit completed its review — **all CI green** (`verify`, `e2e`, `CodeRabbit` all pass), with **2 inline suggestions**. I've assessed both against the actual code:

## 1. Bobber fishing line — frustum culling ⚠️ *Real, worth fixing*
`lib/game/render/bobberVisuals.ts` — the line's vertices update every frame but its cached bounding sphere never does, so Three.js frustum-culling can use stale bounds and make the line **flicker/disappear** as the player moves.

This is a legitimate Three.js gotcha and a real visual bug — exactly the kind of thing my "haven't done a manual gameplay pass" caveat would've surfaced. The fix is one line, `line.frustumCulled = false`, which is **already how the codebase handles dynamic geometry** (the particle system does `points.frustumCulled = false`). The line is always within ~12 blocks of the player, so there's no culling benefit to lose. **I'd fix this.**

## 2. Loot count off-by-one 🟠 *Technically valid, but inert here — I'd skip it*
`lib/game/fishingLoot.ts:40` — `min + Math.floor(clampUnit(rng()) * (max - min + 1))` would yield `max + 1` *if* `rng()` ever returned exactly `1`.

But it can't, for two independent reasons:
- **The rng contract is `[0, 1)`** — `mulberry32` divides by 2³² and `Math.random()` is `< 1`, so the value is never exactly 1. This same idiom is used verbatim in `mobLoot.ts` and `dungeonLoot.ts`; changing only fishing would make it inconsistent with the established pattern.
- **The fishing table has no ranged entries** — every entry is a single count (`raw_fish` is min=1/max=1, the rest default to 1), so `span` is always 1 and the count roll can only ever produce the minimum anyway.

So it's a theoretical edge case that's unreachable in practice and out of step with the sibling rollers. I'd **decline it** (and if we ever wanted to harden it, the right move is fixing the shared idiom across all three loot files in a separate change, not diverging one).

No formal human review yet (CodeRabbit left the one auto-comment).

My recommendation: **apply fix #1, skip #2.** Want me to make that change on the branch (it'll re-trigger CI)? I can also post a brief reply on the #2 thread explaining why it's being declined, if you'd like the rationale on the PR.

> AGENT

Confirmed the machinery: there's a one-shot `triggerSwing()` that arcs both the first-person held item and the third-person arm. Today it fires **only on left-click attacks** — so right-click fishing (cast and reel) currently produces **no rod motion at all**. The rod just sits in your hand while the bobber appears or vanishes.

My take: **yes, add motion on cast and reel — it's the weakest part of the feel right now.** Mining animates (a chop loop) and attacks animate (a swing), so a dead-still rod during its *only* two actions is both underwhelming and inconsistent with the polish bar you've already set. The bobber/line/splash/sound sell the *water* side; the rod animation sells the *player* side.

**The cheap, high-ROI version (what I'd do):** call the existing `triggerSwing()` on the fishing events — `fishingCast`, `fishingCaught`, and `fishingReeledEmpty` — the same way `attackSwung` already does in `useMinecraftGame.ts`. That's ~3 lines, reuses the whole swing system, and instantly makes the rod flick when you cast and yank when you reel. Big readability win for almost nothing.

**Honest caveat:** `triggerSwing` is a generic forward arc, so cast and reel would look *identical* (a quick flick). In practice the context disambiguates them — cast spawns the bobber, reel removes it + splash + a different sound — so it reads fine. A *distinct* "pull the rod back toward you" reel motion would need a new parameterized pose in `heldItem.ts`/`playerPose.ts` — more work, and I'd treat it as optional later polish, not now.

### 1. **Player Third-Person Arm/Body Animation**

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/playerPose.ts`

**Input Type Signature:**
```typescript
export type PlayerPoseInput = {
  timeMs: number;
  /** 0..1 horizontal speed relative to walk speed — scales the walk gait. */
  moveFactor: number;
  /** True while mining — the arm chop loops instead of stopping after one cycle. */
  miningActive: boolean;
  /** Start of the most recent swing; -Infinity when the player has never swung. */
  swingStartMs: number;
};
```

**Output Type Signature:**
```typescript

  leftArmX: number;
  rightArmX: number;
  leftLegX: number;
  rightLegX: number;
};
```

**Pose Math (quoted from lines 27–45):**
```typescript
export function computePlayerPose(input: PlayerPoseInput): PlayerPose {
  // Walk gait: legs counter-phased, each arm counter-phased to its same-side
  // leg, all scaled by horizontal speed so the body idles when standing.
  const gait = Math.sin(input.timeMs * 0.012) * 0.8 * input.moveFactor;
  const pose = {
    leftLegX: gait,
    rightLegX: -gait,
    leftArmX: -gait * 0.8,
    rightArmX: gait * 0.8
  };

  // Attack/mining chop: the right arm raises forward and falls back, matching
  // the first-person held-item swing timing.
  let t = (input.timeMs - input.swingStartMs) / PLAYER_SWING_MS;
  if (input.miningActive && t >= 0) t %= 1;
  if (t >= 0 && t <= 1) pose.rightArmX -= Math.sin(t * Math.PI) * 1.9;

  return pose;
}
```

**Key Constants:**
```typescript
export const PLAYER_SWING_MS = 260;
```

**How it drives limbs:** Each limb's rotation is applied as `rotation.x` to a pivot group at the joint:
- Left/right legs rotate at hip pivots (y=0.72)
- Left/right arms rotate at shoulder pivots (y=1.26)
- Gait oscillates continuously via `Math.sin(input.timeMs * 0.012)`, scaled by `moveFactor`
- Attack swing adds a sinusoidal arc `Math.sin(t * Math.PI) * 1.9` to rightArmX only while 0 ≤ t ≤ 1

### 3. **Data Flow: Frame Update through Pose Computation**

**State inputs available to renderer at sync time:**

- `state.mining.targetKey !== ""` → whether mining is active
- `state.player.velocity` + `state.player.onGround` → walk speed for bobbing

- `timeMs` (parameter) → current wall-clock time
- **`state.fishing`** → `FishingState | null` (present but **not passed to heldItem.update yet**)

**`heldItem.ts:51-94`**:

1. **Visibility & queue clearing** (lines 52–57):

2. **Model swap on item change** (lines 59–76):

   - If key changed: clear old geometry/materials, build new model via `buildItemModel(slot)`, attach to holder, reset swing/equip timers

3. **Swing state machine** (lines 78–83):
   - If `swingQueued`, consume it and set `swingStartMs = frame.timeMs`
   - If `frame.miningActive` and wasn't mining last frame, set `swingStartMs = frame.timeMs` (loop trigger)
   - Track `wasMining` for the rising edge

### 4. **Pose Math: HeldPoseInput & Swing/Equip/Bob Computation**

**`heldItemPose.ts:23-33`** (the input to pose computation):

```typescript
export type HeldPoseInput = {
  timeMs: number;
  swingStartMs: number;        // Start of most recent swing; -Infinity when never swung
  continuousSwing: boolean;    // True while mining — swing arc loops instead of one-shot
  equipStartMs: number;        // Start of most recent equip (item switch); -Infinity to skip dip
  moveFactor: number;          // 0..1 horizontal speed relative to walk speed
};
```

**Base pose in camera space (`heldItemPose.ts:18`)**:

```typescript
export const BASE_POSE: HeldPose = { posX: 0.34, posY: -0.28, posZ: -0.55, rotX: -0.35, rotY: -0.55, rotZ: -0.12 };
```

**Swing arc math (`heldItemPose.ts:40-49`)**:

```typescript
// Swing: a sin(t*PI) chop arc — out and down, with a slight inward twist.
let t = (input.timeMs - input.swingStartMs) / SWING_MS;
if (input.continuousSwing && t >= 0) t %= 1;  // Loop in mining mode
if (t >= 0 && t <= 1) {
  const s = Math.sin(t * Math.PI);            // 0 → 1 → 0 over the arc
  pose.rotX -= s * 1.15;                      // Pitch down
  pose.rotY += s * 0.35;                      // Yaw in
  pose.posZ -= s * 0.16;                      // Forward
  pose.posY -= s * 0.1;                       // Down
}
```

**Constants (`heldItemPose.ts:20-21`)**:
```typescript
export const SWING_MS = 260;   // One swing cycle duration
export const EQUIP_MS = 220;   // Item equip dip duration
```

**Equip dip (`heldItemPose.ts:52-55`)**:

```typescript
const e = clamp01((input.timeMs - input.equipStartMs) / EQUIP_MS);
const q = 1 - (1 - e) * (1 - e);              // ease-out (quadratic)
pose.posY -= (1 - q) * 0.4;                   // Drop 0.4 units then rise
pose.rotX -= (1 - q) * 0.5;                   // Pitch up then settle
```

**Idle sway + walk bob (`heldItemPose.ts:57-64`)**:

```typescript
// Idle sway: barely-visible drift so the item never looks frozen.
pose.posY += Math.sin(input.timeMs * 0.0016) * 0.006;
pose.rotZ += Math.sin(input.timeMs * 0.0013) * 0.015;

// Walk bob: figure-eight-ish sway scaled by horizontal speed.
const p = input.timeMs * 0.012;
pose.posX += Math.sin(p) * 0.02 * input.moveFactor;
pose.posY -= Math.abs(Math.sin(p)) * 0.025 * input.moveFactor;
```

### 5. **Item Model Building**

**`itemModel.ts:21-35`** (main builder):

```typescript
export function buildItemModel(slot: InventorySlot | undefined): ItemModel | null {
  if (!slot?.id || slot.count <= 0 || !slot.kind) return null;

  if (slot.kind === "block" && slot.id !== "door") {
    const geometry = new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.22, 0.22, 0.22);
    const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: blockColor(slot.blockId), roughness: 0.7, metalness: 0.05 });
    return { object: new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material), geometry, material };
  }

  // Doors, tools, weapons, food, armor: extrude the same 16x16 pixel grid the
  // inventory icon uses, so the in-hand model always matches the sprite.
  const geometry = buildExtrudedSpriteGeometry(renderSpritePixels(slot.id));
  const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ vertexColors: true, roughness: 0.7, metalness: 0.05 });
  return { object: new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material), geometry, material };
}
```

**Extruded sprite geometry (`extrudedSprite.ts:16`)**:
- Converts 16x16 RGBA pixel grid → voxel mesh (one pixel-thick box per opaque pixel)
- Centered at origin; default depth 0.03 units
- Front/back always render; sides only where neighbors are transparent (outline silhouette)
- Vertex colors baked with per-axis shading (1.0 front/back, 0.85 top/bottom, 0.7 left/right)

**No special handling in `itemModel.ts` for tools or rods** — the `fishing_rod` item id just renders like any other tool (extruded from its 16x16 sprite).

### Summary

The held-item animation system is a clean **pose-composition pipeline**:

1. **Frame input** (6 scalar/boolean fields) enters `heldItem.update()`
2. **Model swapping** happens on item id change (no cross-fade; direct swap)
3. **Pose computation** in pure `heldItemPose` stacks: swing arc + equip dip + idle sway + walk bob = final transform
4. **Transform applied** to the holder group every frame; mesh stays local
5. **Visibility gating** by camera mode (first-person only)
6. **Attack swings** flow: event → `triggerSwing()` → flag → latched on next update

**For fishing rod animations**, the data (`state.fishing`) already exists in the renderer's sync context; it just needs to be threaded through to `HeldItemFrame` and incorporated into the pose math as another conditional layer (like the swing/equip layers). 2	 * Pure pose math for the first-person held item. No Three.js — heldItem.ts

4	 * of wall-clock timeMs plus a few timestamps, so poses are deterministic and

7	
8	export type HeldPose = {
9	  posX: number;
10	  posY: number;
11	  posZ: number;
12	  rotX: number;
13	  rotY: number;
14	  rotZ: number;
15	};
16	
17	/** Rest pose in camera space — lower-right of the view, matching the old static placement. */
18	export const BASE_POSE: HeldPose = { posX: 0.34, posY: -0.28, posZ: -0.55, rotX: -0.35, rotY: -0.55, rotZ: -0.12 };
19	
20	export const SWING_MS = 260;
21	export const EQUIP_MS = 220;
22	
23	export type HeldPoseInput = {
24	  timeMs: number;
25	  /** Start of the most recent swing; -Infinity when the item has never swung. */
26	  swingStartMs: number;
27	  /** True while mining — the swing arc loops instead of stopping after one cycle. */
28	  continuousSwing: boolean;
29	  /** Start of the most recent equip (item switch); -Infinity to skip the dip. */
30	  equipStartMs: number;
31	  /** 0..1 horizontal speed relative to walk speed — scales the walk bob. */
32	  moveFactor: number;
33	};
34	
35	const clamp01 = (v: number) => Math.max(0, Math.min(1, v));
36	
37	export function computeHeldPose(input: HeldPoseInput): HeldPose {
38	  const pose = { ...BASE_POSE };
39	
40	  // Swing: a sin(t*PI) chop arc — out and down, with a slight inward twist.
41	  let t = (input.timeMs - input.swingStartMs) / SWING_MS;
42	  if (input.continuousSwing && t >= 0) t %= 1;
43	  if (t >= 0 && t <= 1) {
44	    const s = Math.sin(t * Math.PI);
45	    pose.rotX -= s * 1.15;
46	    pose.rotY += s * 0.35;
47	    pose.posZ -= s * 0.16;
48	    pose.posY -= s * 0.1;
49	  }
50	
51	  // Equip: the item rises into frame from below after a slot switch.
52	  const e = clamp01((input.timeMs - input.equipStartMs) / EQUIP_MS);
53	  const q = 1 - (1 - e) * (1 - e);
54	  pose.posY -= (1 - q) * 0.4;
55	  pose.rotX -= (1 - q) * 0.5;
56	
57	  // Idle sway: barely-visible drift so the item never looks frozen.
58	  pose.posY += Math.sin(input.timeMs * 0.0016) * 0.006;
59	  pose.rotZ += Math.sin(input.timeMs * 0.0013) * 0.015;
60	
61	  // Walk bob: figure-eight-ish sway scaled by horizontal speed.
62	  const p = input.timeMs * 0.012;
63	  pose.posX += Math.sin(p) * 0.02 * input.moveFactor;
64	  pose.posY -= Math.abs(Math.sin(p)) * 0.025 * input.moveFactor;
65	
66	  return pose;
67	}
68

describe("computeHeldPose", () => {
  test("rests at the base pose when nothing is animating", () => {
    // timeMs 0 keeps the idle-sway sine terms at zero.
    expect(computeHeldPose({ timeMs: 0, ...REST })).toEqual(BASE_POSE);
  });

  test("a one-shot swing peaks mid-arc and returns to base", () => {
    const mid = computeHeldPose({ timeMs: SWING_MS / 2, ...REST, swingStartMs: 0 });
    expect(mid.rotX).toBeLessThan(BASE_POSE.rotX - 0.5);
    expect(mid.posZ).toBeLessThan(BASE_POSE.posZ);

    const after = computeHeldPose({ timeMs: SWING_MS * 1.5, ...REST, swingStartMs: 0 });
    const idle = computeHeldPose({ timeMs: SWING_MS * 1.5, ...REST });
    expect(after).toEqual(idle); // swing fully over, only idle sway remains
  });

  test("continuous swing loops while a one-shot swing does not", () => {
    const looped = computeHeldPose({ timeMs: SWING_MS * 1.5, ...REST, swingStartMs: 0, continuousSwing: true });
    const oneShot = computeHeldPose({ timeMs: SWING_MS * 1.5, ...REST, swingStartMs: 0 });
    expect(looped.rotX).toBeLessThan(oneShot.rotX - 0.5);

# Polished Fishing-Rod Animations — Execution Plan

## Part 1: Seam confirmation and corrections

### 1a. Sim/event seams (confirmed by reading `fishing.ts`, `state.ts`, `useMinecraftGame.ts`)

- `state.fishing: FishingState | null` is `{ position: THREE.Vector3, timer, biting }`. `position` is `(cell.x+0.5, cell.y+1, cell.z+0.5)` — i.e. the water *surface* (top face of the water cell). This is the bobber's resting `target`. Confirmed render-only safe; do not touch this.
- **Cast edge**: `tryFish` sets `state.fishing = {...}` and emits `fishingCast` in the *same* tick. So the null→non-null edge of `state.fishing` and the `fishingCast` event coincide. Either can drive the cast; the plan uses the event for rod poses (timestamped) and the `state.fishing` edge for the bobber (no event timestamp needed since the bobber tweens off its own captured `castFrom`).
- **Reel edge**: on a manual reel, `tryFish` emits `fishingCaught` (biting) or `fishingReeledEmpty` (not biting) and sets `state.fishing = null` in the same tick. **Gotcha confirmed**: `state.fishing` is null the same frame the reel happens, so the bobber must capture `reelFrom` on the non-null→null *edge* (last-seen position), exactly as the design says.
- **Silent cancel** (CONFIRMED, important correction): `tickFishing` also sets `state.fishing = null` with **no event** when the rod is unequipped, the player dies, the water block is gone, or the player walks past `FISHING_TETHER_DISTANCE`. So the bobber sees a null→edge with no `fishingCaught`/`fishingReeledEmpty` to pair it. **Decision**: the bobber's reel animation should be driven purely by the `state.fishing` non-null→null edge (always animate a short reel-back), NOT by the events. That makes the bobber robust to silent cancels. The *rod* poses, by contrast, are driven by events (`fishingCast`→cast, `fishingCaught|fishingReeledEmpty`→reel); on a silent cancel the rod simply returns to its base idle (fishingActive flips false), which looks fine. This split is the cleanest correct design and I recommend it over trying to pair the bobber to events.
- Loop order (confirmed `useMinecraftGame.ts` ~280): `minimap.sync` → `renderer.sync(state, now)` → `audio.sync` → `renderer.render()`. Events are consumed *before* `renderer.sync` (lines 242–276), and `renderer.handleEvent` already runs there, so `triggerCast/triggerReel` latched in `handleEvent` are consumed by the `heldItem.update`/`playerVisuals.sync` calls inside the very next `renderer.sync`. Good — the queue pattern matches `triggerSwing`/`attackSwung` exactly.

### 1b. Matrix-currency gotcha (CONFIRMED real — this is the most important correction)

Grep shows **zero** `updateMatrixWorld`/`getWorldPosition`/`localToWorld` calls anywhere in `lib/game/render/*` today. Three.js only refreshes world matrices inside `WebGLRenderer.render()` (which calls `scene.updateMatrixWorld()`). The loop is `sync()` then `render()`. Therefore, during `sync()`:

- `this.camera.matrixWorld` reflects the pose set during the *previous* `render()` (one frame stale).
- The third-person `itemHolder.matrixWorld` (Group on right arm on player group) likewise reflects the previous frame — and worse, `playerVisuals.sync` mutates the arm rotations *during* this same `sync`, so reading `itemHolder.getWorldPosition` before flushing would be two-source stale (stale group transform AND pre-rotation arm).

**Exact required ordering inside `GameRenderer.sync`** (the rod tip must be read from *fresh* matrices):

1. `this.syncCamera(state)` — sets `this.camera.position/rotation` (already there, line 179).
2. **NEW**: `this.camera.updateMatrixWorld()` — flush the camera so `localToWorld` is correct this frame. (The camera has no animated parent; the held-item `root`/`holder` are children of the camera and are positioned in camera-local space, so they don't need the rod tip — only the *bobber line* needs the world-space tip.)
3. `this.heldItem.update(...)` (line 182, unchanged position) — first-person rod pose, camera-local, fine.
4. `this.playerVisuals.sync(state, timeMs)` — **move this to run BEFORE the rod-tip read** (currently line 193, after the bobber). It mutates `model.group` transform + arm rotations.
5. **NEW**: inside `playerVisuals.getRodTip(out)`, call `this.model.itemHolder.updateWorldMatrix(true, false)` (update-parents=true so the group/arm/holder chain is fresh) then `this.model.itemHolder.getWorldPosition(out)`. Calling `updateWorldMatrix(true,false)` on just the holder is cheaper than a whole-scene flush and is self-contained.
6. Compute `rodTip` (a `this.bobberTip` scratch `Vector3`):
   - First-person (`cameraMode === "first"`): `rodTip = this.camera.localToWorld(scratch.copy(ROD_TIP_OFFSET))`. Reset the scratch each frame (`localToWorld` mutates in place). `ROD_TIP_OFFSET` is a camera-space point near the rod's far end — lower-right-forward, deeper than `BASE_POSE.posZ`. Start near `(0.34, -0.18, -0.95)` and tune (the rod sprite extrudes forward from the hand).
   - Third/front person: `this.playerVisuals.getRodTip(scratch)`.
7. `this.bobberVisuals.sync(state.fishing, rodTip, dtMs)` (was line 192 with `bobberEye`; now uses `rodTip` and threads `dtMs`).

**Net effect**: one extra `camera.updateMatrixWorld()` and one `itemHolder.updateWorldMatrix(true,false)` per frame, plus reordering `playerVisuals.sync` above the bobber sync. The one-frame staleness was previously masked because the old line just used `state.player.position + EYE_HEIGHT` (no matrices at all). Removing `bobberEye` is fine; it was the eye-anchored start point being replaced by the rod tip.

**Should `dtMs` be threaded into `playerVisuals.sync` too?** Not required for the pose math (poses are pure functions of `timeMs` + timestamps, like `heldItemPose`, so they need no `dt`). Keep `playerVisuals.sync(state, timeMs)` signature unchanged; the third-person cast/reel timestamps are captured from latched triggers using `timeMs`, identical to the existing `swingStartMs` mechanism. Only `bobberVisuals.sync` genuinely needs `dtMs` (it integrates a tween clock across frames because the bobber tween clock starts on a state edge, not on a wall-clock timestamp we control). This keeps the change surface minimal.

## Part 2: Exact signatures and pose math

### 2a. `bobberVisuals.ts` — state machine

```ts
export type BobberVisuals = {
  sync(fishing: FishingState | null, rodTip: THREE.Vector3, dtMs: number): void;
  dispose(): void;
};
```

Module constants:
```ts
const CAST_S = 0.35;   // arc out
const REEL_S = 0.25;   // arc back
const LOB_HEIGHT = 0.9;       // peak of the cast parabola above the chord
const BOB_AMP = 0.04, BOB_HZ = 1.1;  // idle bob
const BITE_DIP = -0.09;       // existing strike dip
```

Internal state (closure vars):
```ts
type Phase = "hidden" | "casting" | "waiting" | "reeling";
let phase: Phase = "hidden";
let t = 0;                         // seconds elapsed in current phase
let wasFishing = false;            // edge detector
const castFrom = new THREE.Vector3();
const target = new THREE.Vector3();
const reelFrom = new THREE.Vector3();
const lastBobber = new THREE.Vector3();  // captured every frame for reelFrom on the null edge
const cur = new THREE.Vector3();         // current bobber position this frame
```

Logic per `sync(fishing, rodTip, dtMs)`:
```ts
const dt = dtMs / 1000;
const isFishing = fishing !== null;

// Edge: null -> set  => start cast
if (isFishing && !wasFishing) {
  phase = "casting"; t = 0;
  castFrom.copy(rodTip);
  target.copy(fishing!.position);
}
// Edge: set -> null => start reel (covers manual reel AND silent cancel)
if (!isFishing && wasFishing) {
  phase = "reeling"; t = 0;
  reelFrom.copy(lastBobber);
}
wasFishing = isFishing;

if (phase === "hidden") { setPresent(false); return; }

t += dt;

if (phase === "casting") {
  // target may drift only if re-cast; re-read each frame is cheap & safe
  if (fishing) target.copy(fishing.position);
  const k = Math.min(1, t / CAST_S);
  cur.lerpVectors(castFrom, target, k);
  cur.y += Math.sin(k * Math.PI) * LOB_HEIGHT;   // lobbed parabola
  if (k >= 1) phase = "waiting";
}
else if (phase === "waiting") {
  cur.copy(fishing!.position);
  cur.y += Math.sin(t * BOB_HZ * Math.PI * 2) * BOB_AMP;  // gentle bob
  if (fishing!.biting) cur.y += BITE_DIP;                  // strike dip preserved
}
else if (phase === "reeling") {
  const k = Math.min(1, t / REEL_S);
  cur.lerpVectors(reelFrom, rodTip, k);   // arc BACK toward live rod tip
  cur.y += Math.sin(k * Math.PI) * (LOB_HEIGHT * 0.4);  // small return hop
  if (k >= 1) { phase = "hidden"; setPresent(false); return; }
}

setPresent(true);
bobber.position.copy(cur);
lastBobber.copy(cur);   // so the null-edge can capture the live position next frame
// line: rodTip -> bobber (replaces eye -> bobber)
linePositions[0..2] = rodTip; linePositions[3..5] = cur; needsUpdate.
```

Notes:
- During `waiting`, `cur` no longer carries the `casting` lob — clean handoff.
- `reeling` lerps toward the *live* `rodTip` each frame (the rod is yanking), which looks better than a frozen tip and is free.
- The existing `bobber.frustumCulled`/line `frustumCulled = false` stays. The bobber mesh itself: consider `bobber.frustumCulled = false` too, since during the cast it moves far from its cached bounding sphere; low risk but recommend setting it (one line).
- **Test seam preserved**: existing tests call `sync(fishing, eye)` with 2 args. They WILL break (signature change). That's expected and intended — they get updated in the same commit (see test plan). The "positions the bobber at the cast point" test currently asserts an instant snap; after the change, casting tweens, so the assertion must advance the clock past `CAST_S` (pass a large `dtMs`, e.g. `sync(fishing, tip, 1000)`) to land at the target.

### 2b. `heldItemPose.ts` — first-person rod layer

Extend input + add constants:
```ts
export const CAST_MS = 350;
export const REEL_MS = 250;

export type HeldPoseInput = {
  timeMs: number;
  swingStartMs: number;
  continuousSwing: boolean;
  equipStartMs: number;
  moveFactor: number;
  // NEW (all optional-with-default so existing tests/callers compile):
  castStartMs?: number;     // default -Infinity
  reelStartMs?: number;     // default -Infinity
  fishingActive?: boolean;  // default false  (held-out stance)
  fishingBiting?: boolean;  // default false  (tip twitch)
};
```

Compose AFTER the swing/equip/idle/walk layers (so it overrides for the fishing stance) — pure, additive deltas:
```ts
const castStart = input.castStartMs ?? -Infinity;
const reelStart = input.reelStartMs ?? -Infinity;

// Held-out stance: while fishing, push the rod up/forward and level it out,
// blended in over EQUIP_MS-ish so entering/leaving fishing isn't a pop.
if (input.fishingActive) {
  pose.posY += 0.10;        // raise
  pose.posZ -= 0.10;        // push forward over the water
  pose.rotX += 0.30;        // tilt tip up
  pose.rotZ += 0.05;
  // bite twitch: a fast damped wiggle at the tip
  if (input.fishingBiting) {
    pose.rotX += Math.sin(input.timeMs * 0.05) * 0.04;
  }
}

// Cast: a quick wind-up (rod back) then flick forward. One-shot sin lobe split:
let c = (input.timeMs - castStart) / CAST_MS;
if (c >= 0 && c <= 1) {
  // wind-up for first 35%, flick for the rest
  if (c < 0.35) {
    const w = c / 0.35;            // 0..1 wind-up
    pose.rotX += Math.sin(w * Math.PI * 0.5) * 0.55;  // tip back/up
  } else {
    const f = (c - 0.35) / 0.65;   // 0..1 flick
    const s = Math.sin(f * Math.PI);
    pose.rotX -= s * 0.85;          // snap forward/down
    pose.posZ -= s * 0.12;
  }
}

// Reel: yank back and up, single sin lobe.
let r = (input.timeMs - reelStart) / REEL_MS;
if (r >= 0 && r <= 1) {
  const s = Math.sin(r * Math.PI);
  pose.rotX += s * 0.7;    // pull tip up
  pose.posY += s * 0.12;
  pose.posZ += s * 0.08;   // draw toward the body
}
```

Keep `computeHeldPose`'s defaulting at the top (`const castStartMs = input.castStartMs ?? -Infinity`) so `?? -Infinity` math is clean and the existing `REST` test fixture (which omits these) still yields `BASE_POSE` at `timeMs:0`.

### 2c. `heldItem.ts` — triggers + frame wiring

```ts
export type HeldItemFrame = {
  timeMs: number;
  miningActive: boolean;
  moveFactor: number;
  visible: boolean;
  // NEW:
  fishingActive: boolean;
  fishingBiting: boolean;
};

export type HeldItemView = {
  update(slot, frame): void;
  triggerSwing(): void;
  triggerCast(): void;   // NEW
  triggerReel(): void;   // NEW
  dispose(): void;
};
```

Closure additions mirroring swing exactly:
```ts
let castQueued = false, castStartMs = -Infinity;
let reelQueued = false, reelStartMs = -Infinity;
// in update():
if (castQueued) { castQueued = false; castStartMs = frame.timeMs; }
if (reelQueued) { reelQueued = false; reelStartMs = frame.timeMs; }
// also clear castQueued/reelQueued on !visible (like swingQueued) and on item-switch reset.
// pass castStartMs, reelStartMs, frame.fishingActive, frame.fishingBiting into computeHeldPose.
triggerCast() { castQueued = true; }
triggerReel() { reelQueued = true; }
```
On item switch (`nextKey !== key`), reset `castStartMs/reelStartMs = -Infinity` and clear the queues, same as `swingStartMs`.

### 2d. `playerPose.ts` — third-person rod layer

```ts
export const PLAYER_CAST_MS = 350;
export const PLAYER_REEL_MS = 250;

export type PlayerPoseInput = {
  timeMs: number;
  moveFactor: number;
  miningActive: boolean;
  swingStartMs: number;
  // NEW (optional-with-default):
  castStartMs?: number;
  reelStartMs?: number;
  fishingActive?: boolean;
};
```
`PlayerPose` gains nothing new structurally (still per-limb `rotation.x`); the fishing layer adjusts `rightArmX` (the rod arm). Add after the swing chop:
```ts
if (input.fishingActive) pose.rightArmX -= 1.1;  // held out forward toward the water
let c = (input.timeMs - (input.castStartMs ?? -Infinity)) / PLAYER_CAST_MS;
if (c >= 0 && c <= 1) {
  if (c < 0.35) pose.rightArmX += Math.sin((c/0.35) * Math.PI * 0.5) * 0.6;  // wind back
  else pose.rightArmX -= Math.sin(((c-0.35)/0.65) * Math.PI) * 1.4;          // flick
}
let r = (input.timeMs - (input.reelStartMs ?? -Infinity)) / PLAYER_REEL_MS;
if (r >= 0 && r <= 1) pose.rightArmX += Math.sin(r * Math.PI) * 1.0;          // yank up/back
```
Optionally also nudge a leg/torso, but arm-only keeps it consistent with how the body already handles swing. (`PlayerPose` has no torso field; arm-only is the low-risk choice. Decision flag below.)

### 2e. `playerVisuals.ts` — triggers, fishing state, getRodTip

```ts
export type PlayerVisualsState = {
  ...existing...
  fishing: FishingState | null;  // NEW slice — narrow; used only for fishingActive boolean
};

export type PlayerVisuals = {
  sync(state, timeMs): void;
  triggerSwing(): void;
  triggerCast(): void;   // NEW
  triggerReel(): void;   // NEW
  getRodTip(out: THREE.Vector3): THREE.Vector3;  // NEW
  setPalette(palette): void;
  dispose(): void;
};
```
Closure mirrors swing: `castQueued/castStartMs`, `reelQueued/reelStartMs`. In `sync`, latch them, compute `fishingActive = state.fishing !== null`, pass `{ castStartMs, reelStartMs, fishingActive }` into `computePlayerPose`. Clear queues on `!visible` (same guard as `swingQueued`).
```ts
getRodTip(out) {
  model.itemHolder.updateWorldMatrix(true, false);
  return model.itemHolder.getWorldPosition(out);
}
```
Note: `PlayerVisualsState` is widened, but `GameState` already has `fishing`, so the cast at the `GameRenderer.sync` call site (`this.playerVisuals.sync(state, timeMs)`) still passes the whole state — fine, the narrow type just documents the new field. Confirm `state.ts` exports `FishingState` (it does, line 96) for the import in `playerVisuals.ts`.

### 2f. `GameRenderer.ts` — wiring

- Add scratch: `private readonly bobberTip = new THREE.Vector3();` and `private static readonly ROD_TIP_OFFSET = new THREE.Vector3(0.34, -0.18, -0.95);` (or module const). Remove `bobberEye` usage (can keep the field or delete; deleting is cleaner).
- In `sync`, reorder/insert per Part 1b. Compute `fishingActive = state.fishing !== null`, `fishingBiting = state.fishing?.biting ?? false`, pass into the held-item frame.
- In `triggerSwing` keep as is. No new public renderer method strictly needed for cast/reel because they're event-driven in `handleEvent`:
  - In `handleEvent`, add to the existing `fishingCast` case: `this.heldItem.triggerCast(); this.playerVisuals.triggerCast();` (alongside the existing particle burst).
  - Add `this.heldItem.triggerReel(); this.playerVisuals.triggerReel();` to BOTH `fishingCaught` and `fishingReeledEmpty` cases. `fishingReeledEmpty` currently has no case (it emits no particles) — add a minimal case that only triggers the reel pose. `fishingCaught` already has a particle case; append the triggers there.
- No change to `useMinecraftGame.ts` needed for cast/reel poses — `renderer.handleEvent(event, state)` already runs for every event (line 274), so the triggers fire automatically. (Unlike `attackSwung`, which needed an explicit `renderer.triggerSwing()` because there's no particle/`handleEvent` branch for it.) This is a nice simplification — flag it.

## Part 4: Test plan

All new tests follow the existing headless patterns (pure functions for poses; a `new THREE.Scene()` for bobber — no WebGL).

**`bobberVisuals.test.ts`** (rewrite signature + add):
- Update existing 2 tests to `sync(fishing, tip, dtMs)`. The "positions at cast point" test: call once to start the cast, then `sync(fishing, tip, 1000)` to fast-forward past `CAST_S`, assert `bobber.position` ≈ `fishing.position` (x/z exact, y within bob amplitude).
- New: "casting arcs above the chord" — start cast with `castFrom` far below target, sample at `dtMs = CAST_S*1000/2`, assert bobber.y > `lerp(from,target,0.5).y` (the lob).
- New: "shows then hides across a full reel" — `sync(fishing,...)` (present), `sync(null, tip, dtMs)` starts reeling (still present), `sync(null, tip, 1000)` finishes reel → `scene.children` length 0.
- New: "silent cancel still reels and hides" — same as above (no event involved), proving event-independence.
- New: "line runs rod tip → bobber" — assert `linePositions[0..2]` equals the passed `rodTip`.
- New: "biting dips the float while waiting" — advance to waiting, compare `biting:true` vs `false` y.

**`heldItemPose.test.ts`**:
- "rests at base when not fishing" (existing, unchanged — defaults keep `BASE_POSE`).
- "fishing stance raises and tilts the rod" — `fishingActive:true` vs false: posY up, rotX up.
- "cast winds up then flicks forward" — sample at `c=0.2` (rotX > base) and `c=0.7` (rotX < base), back to idle after `CAST_MS`.
- "reel yanks the tip up" — mid-`REEL_MS` rotX/posY up, returns to idle after.
- "bite adds a tip twitch" — `fishingBiting:true` differs from false at a non-zero `timeMs`.
- "deterministic for same input" with the new fields.

**`playerPose.test.ts`**:
- "fishing extends the right arm forward" — `fishingActive:true` → `rightArmX` more negative than idle.
- "cast and reel move the rod arm and return to rest" — mirror the held-item tests on `rightArmX`.
- Existing idle/walk/swing tests unchanged (new inputs default off).

**Untouched (confirm no sim impact)**: `generation.test.ts` and `save.test.ts` — these exercise worldgen/serialization. Nothing in this plan touches `lib/game/engine/**`, `lib/world/**`, the save format, or `FishingState`'s shape, so both stay green without edits. `fishing.test.ts` (sim) also stays untouched. Run `bun test` (whole suite) + `bun run lint` after each commit.

## Part 5: Item-fly-to-player on catch — assessment

**Feasible, low-risk, but optional.** `fishingCaught` carries `items` + `x/y/z` (the bobber pos), and `buildItemModel(slot)` already produces a sprite mesh for any item id (used by both held-item and third-person hand), so a catch sprite is trivial to build. Plug-in point: a new tiny `caughtItemVisuals.ts` (mirroring `projectileVisuals.ts`'s pooled-mesh-in-scene pattern) with `spawn(itemId, from, timeMs)` and `sync(timeMs, playerHeadPos)` that arcs the sprite from `(x,y,z)` toward the player's head over ~0.4s then removes it. Drive it from `GameRenderer.handleEvent`'s `fishingCaught` case (spawn) and `GameRenderer.sync` (advance). It needs the catch *item id* (have it) and the player head position (have it: `state.player.position + EYE_HEIGHT`).

**Catch**: the item flies toward the *player*, but in third-person the catch should arc to the player's hand and in first-person toward the camera; using head/eye for both is a fine approximation. Tween clock can be wall-clock `timeMs` (spawn timestamp), no `dtMs` needed.

**Recommendation**: nice polish, but **defer to a follow-up** — it's the only piece that adds a new file + new scratch state and isn't required by the three core goals. Keep commit (d) as an optional stretch; ship (a)–(c)+(e) first. If included, it's ~60 lines + one small test ("spawns a sprite on catch, removes it after the flight"). Worth it only if you want the extra game-feel; the splash particles already sell the catch.

---

## Part 6: Decision flags for the user

1. **Bobber reel is `state.fishing`-edge-driven, not event-driven** (so silent cancels — rod unequipped, died, water gone, tether exceeded — also play the reel-back). Rod poses are event-driven and just relax to idle on silent cancel. Confirm this split is acceptable (recommended; the alternative — pairing the bobber to `fishingCaught`/`fishingReeledEmpty` — would make silent cancels snap the bobber away with no animation).
2. **`ROD_TIP_OFFSET` is a magic camera-space constant** for the first-person line origin; it'll need eyeball tuning against the actual rod sprite extrusion. Initial guess `(0.34, -0.18, -0.95)`. Acceptable to ship a "good enough" value and tune later?
3. **Extra per-frame matrix work**: one `camera.updateMatrixWorld()` always + one `itemHolder.updateWorldMatrix(true,false)` only in third-person. Negligible cost; flagging because it's the one place this touches Three.js lifecycle ordering.
4. **No `useMinecraftGame.ts` change** for cast/reel (handled in `renderer.handleEvent`, which already runs per event). Confirm you're happy with the asymmetry vs `attackSwung` (which needs the explicit `renderer.triggerSwing()` call because it has no `handleEvent` branch). Could optionally route cast/reel through `useMinecraftGame` for consistency, but that's redundant.

> AGENT

The plan is written. Here's the shape of it.

## Polished fishing animations — plan summary

A render-side-only upgrade (no engine/save/worldgen impact) that makes fishing *feel* great in both first- and third-person:

- **Cast** — rod winds up + flicks; the bobber **arcs out from the rod tip** to the water (a lobbed parabola), line trailing.
- **Idle** — a distinct "rod held over the water" stance, gentle bob, line taut **from the rod tip**, a tip twitch on a bite.
- **Reel** — rod yanks back; the bobber **arcs back** then vanishes.
- **Catch** — the caught item sprite **flies to you** (~0.4s), the iconic Minecraft moment.

**The two findings that shaped the design** (both validated by the Plan agent against the code):
1. **Matrix currency** — the renderer has *no* `updateMatrixWorld` calls today, so naively reading the rod-tip world position would use a stale matrix. The plan pins the exact flush/ordering in `GameRenderer.sync`.
2. **Edge-driven bobber reel** — silent cancels (rod unequipped, death, water drained, walking off) null the cast with *no* event, so the bobber animates its reel-back off the `state.fishing` null-edge (robust), while the rod poses stay event-driven and relax to idle.

It reuses the existing pure pose pipeline (`heldItemPose`/`playerPose`), the `triggerSwing` latch pattern, and `buildItemModel` for the flying catch — so it's mostly composing new layers, not new machinery.

**Structure:** 5 render-only commits, each lint/test-green — (a) bobber arc + rod-tip line + matrix flush, (b) first-person rod poses, (c) third-person rod poses, (d) fly-to-you catch, (e) docs. Pure-pose and bobber state-machine tests follow the existing headless patterns; `generation`/`save`/`fishing` sim tests stay untouched. Because this is a visual-feel change, a **manual gameplay pass is required** (and where I'd tune the rod-tip offset + timing).

One open question for when this lands: it builds on the unmerged `feat/fishing` branch (PR #26). I'd stack these commits on that same branch so they ship together — unless you'd rather merge #26 first and do animations as a follow-up PR.

2	import type { FishingState } from "@/lib/game/engine/state";

4	export type BobberVisuals = {
5	  /** Shows the bobber + line when a cast is active, hides them otherwise. */
6	  sync(fishing: FishingState | null, eye: THREE.Vector3): void;
7	  dispose(): void;
8	};
9	
10	/**
11	 * Renders the single active fishing bobber: a small red float on the water and a
12	 * taut line from the player's eye to it. The bobber dips slightly while a fish is
13	 * biting. One mesh, one line, one geometry/material each — added to the scene only
14	 * while fishing, removed when the cast ends or on dispose().
15	 */
16	export function createBobberVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): BobberVisuals {
17	  const bobberGeometry = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.11, 8, 6);
18	  const bobberMaterial = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xd03c34, roughness: 0.5 });
19	  const bobber = new THREE.Mesh(bobberGeometry, bobberMaterial);
20	
21	  const linePositions = new Float32Array(6);
22	  const lineGeometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
23	  lineGeometry.setAttribute("position", new THREE.BufferAttribute(linePositions, 3));
24	  const lineMaterial = new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color: 0xdedede });
25	  const line = new THREE.Line(lineGeometry, lineMaterial);
26	  // Endpoints move every frame; skip frustum culling so the stale cached bounding
27	  // sphere can't cull the line off-screen (matches the particle system).
28	  line.frustumCulled = false;
29	
30	  let present = false;
31	  const setPresent = (next: boolean): void => {
32	    if (next === present) return;
33	    present = next;
34	    if (next) scene.add(bobber, line);
35	    else scene.remove(bobber, line);
36	  };
37	
38	  return {
39	    sync(fishing, eye) {
40	      if (!fishing) {
41	        setPresent(false);
42	        return;
43	      }
44	      setPresent(true);
45	      const dip = fishing.biting ? -0.09 : 0; // the strike pulls the float under
46	      bobber.position.set(fishing.position.x, fishing.position.y + dip, fishing.position.z);
47	      linePositions[0] = eye.x;
48	      linePositions[1] = eye.y;
49	      linePositions[2] = eye.z;
50	      linePositions[3] = bobber.position.x;
51	      linePositions[4] = bobber.position.y;
52	      linePositions[5] = bobber.position.z;
53	      lineGeometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;
54	    },
55	
56	    dispose() {
57	      setPresent(false);
58	      bobberGeometry.dispose();
59	      bobberMaterial.dispose();
60	      lineGeometry.dispose();
61	      lineMaterial.dispose();
62	    }
63	  };
64	}
65

91	      wasMining = miningActive;

94	      const pose = computePlayerPose({ timeMs, moveFactor, miningActive, swingStartMs });
95	      model.leftArm.rotation.x = pose.leftArmX;
96	      model.rightArm.rotation.x = pose.rightArmX;
97	      model.leftLeg.rotation.x = pose.leftLegX;
98	      model.rightLeg.rotation.x = pose.rightLegX;

100

  "content": "import * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport type { FishingState } from \"@/lib/game/engine/state\";\n\nexport type BobberVisuals = {\n  /**\n   * Animates the bobber + line each frame: it arcs out from the rod tip on a cast,\n   * bobs on the water while waiting (dipping on a bite), and arcs back to the rod\n   * tip on reel-in. Driven by the `state.fishing` null↔set edges (so a silent\n   * cancel still plays the reel-back) plus the per-frame `dtMs`.\n   */\n  sync(fishing: FishingState | null, rodTip: THREE.Vector3, dtMs: number): void;\n  dispose(): void;\n};\n\nconst CAST_S = 0.35; // bobber flight time, cast\nconst REEL_S = 0.25; // bobber flight time, reel\nconst LOB_HEIGHT = 0.9; // peak of the cast parabola above the straight-line path\nconst BOB_AMP = 0.04; // idle bob amplitude on the water\nconst BOB_HZ = 1.1; // idle bob frequency\nconst BITE_DIP = -0.09; // the strike pulls the float under\n\ntype Phase = \"hidden\" | \"casting\" | \"waiting\" | \"reeling\";\n\n/**\n * Renders the single active fishing bobber as a small red float on a line from the\n * rod tip. One mesh + one line, added to the scene only while a cast is in flight\n * or on the water, removed once the reel-back finishes or on dispose().\n */\nexport function createBobberVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): BobberVisuals {\n  const bobberGeometry = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.11, 8, 6);\n  const bobberMaterial = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xd03c34, roughness: 0.5 });\n  const bobber = new THREE.Mesh(bobberGeometry, bobberMaterial);\n  // It travels far from its cached bounds during the arc — don't let culling drop it.\n  bobber.frustumCulled = false;\n\n  const linePositions = new Float32Array(6);\n  const lineGeometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();\n  lineGeometry.setAttribute(\"position\", new THREE.BufferAttribute(linePositions, 3));\n  const lineMaterial = new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color: 0xdedede });\n  const line = new THREE.Line(lineGeometry, lineMaterial);\n  line.frustumCulled = false;\n\n  let present = false;\n  const setPresent = (next: boolean): void => {\n    if (next === present) return;\n    present = next;\n    if (next) scene.add(bobber, line);\n    else scene.remove(bobber, line);\n  };\n\n  let phase: Phase = \"hidden\";\n  let t = 0; // seconds elapsed in the current phase\n  let wasFishing = false;\n  const castFrom = new THREE.Vector3();\n  const target = new THREE.Vector3();\n  const reelFrom = new THREE.Vector3();\n  const cur = new THREE.Vector3();\n  const lastBobber = new THREE.Vector3();\n\n  return {\n    sync(fishing, rodTip, dtMs) {\n      const dt = dtMs / 1000;\n      const isFishing = fishing !== null;\n\n      // Cast (null -> set): arc out from the rod tip. Reel (set -> null, including\n      // a silent cancel that emits no event): arc back to the rod tip.\n      if (isFishing && !wasFishing) {\n        phase = \"casting\";\n        t = 0;\n        castFrom.copy(rodTip);\n        target.copy(fishing.position);\n      } else if (!isFishing && wasFishing) {\n        phase = \"reeling\";\n        t = 0;\n        reelFrom.copy(lastBobber);\n      }\n      wasFishing = isFishing;\n\n      if (phase === \"hidden\") {\n        setPresent(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      t += dt;\n\n      if (phase === \"casting\") {\n        if (fishing) target.copy(fishing.position);\n        const k = Math.min(1, t / CAST_S);\n        cur.lerpVectors(castFrom, target, k);\n        cur.y += Math.sin(k * Math.PI) * LOB_HEIGHT;\n        if (k >= 1) {\n          phase = \"waiting\";\n          t = 0;\n        }\n      } else if (phase === \"waiting\" && fishing) {\n        cur.copy(fishing.position);\n        cur.y += Math.sin(t * BOB_HZ * Math.PI * 2) * BOB_AMP;\n        if (fishing.biting) cur.y += BITE_DIP;\n      } else if (phase === \"reeling\") {\n        const k = Math.min(1, t / REEL_S);\n        cur.lerpVectors(reelFrom, rodTip, k); // reel toward the live rod tip\n        cur.y += Math.sin(k * Math.PI) * (LOB_HEIGHT * 0.4);\n        if (k >= 1) {\n          phase = \"hidden\";\n          setPresent(false);\n          return;\n        }\n      }\n\n      setPresent(true);\n      bobber.position.copy(cur);\n      lastBobber.copy(cur); // so the set->null edge can capture the live position\n      linePositions[0] = rodTip.x;\n      linePositions[1] = rodTip.y;\n      linePositions[2] = rodTip.z;\n      linePositions[3] = cur.x;\n      linePositions[4] = cur.y;\n      linePositions[5] = cur.z;\n      lineGeometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;\n    },\n\n    dispose() {\n      setPresent(false);\n      bobberGeometry.dispose();\n      bobberMaterial.dispose();\n      lineGeometry.dispose();\n      lineMaterial.dispose();\n    }\n  };\n}\n"
}

// cast begins → bobber + line present\n    expect(scene.children).toHaveLength(2);\n\n    v.sync(fishing(), TIP, 1000); // cast lands → waiting\n    expect(scene.children).toHaveLength(2);\n\n    v.sync(null, TIP, 16); // fishing→null edge starts the reel (no event needed)\n    expect(scene.children).toHaveLength(2);\n\n    v.sync(null, TIP, 1000); // reel finishes → hidden\n    expect(scene.children).toHaveLength(0);\n    v.dispose();\n  });\n\n  test(\"the cast arcs above the straight-line path\", () => {\n    const scene = new THREE.Scene();\n    const v = createBobberVisuals(scene);\n    v.sync(fishing(), TIP, 175); // cast complete\n    v.sync(fishing(), TIP, 16); // a waiting frame\n    const bob = meshOf(scene);\n    expect(bob.position.x).toBe(5);\n    expect(bob.position.z).toBe(5);\n    expect(Math.abs(bob.position.y - 1)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0.05); 1	import * as THREE from "three";
2	import type { InventorySlot } from "@/lib/game/types";
3	import { computeHeldPose } from "./heldItemPose";
4	import { buildItemModel } from "./itemModel";
5	
6	export type HeldItemFrame = {
7	  timeMs: number;
8	  /** True while the player is actively mining a block — loops the swing arc. */
9	  miningActive: boolean;
10	  /** 0..1 horizontal speed relative to walk speed — scales the walk bob. */
11	  moveFactor: number;
12	  /** False in third person — the body's hand shows the item instead. */
13	  visible: boolean;
14	};
15	
16	export type HeldItemView = {
17	  /** Applies the animated pose every frame and rebuilds the model when the selected item changes. */
18	  update(slot: InventorySlot | undefined, frame: HeldItemFrame): void;
19	  /** Queues a one-shot swing (attack click); latched on the next update. */
20	  triggerSwing(): void;
21	  dispose(): void;
22	};
23	
24	export function createHeldItemView(camera: THREE.Camera): HeldItemView {
25	  const root = new THREE.Group();
26	  camera.add(root);
27	
28	  // The holder carries the animated pose; the model inside stays geometry-local.
29	  const holder = new THREE.Group();
30	  root.add(holder);
31	
32	  const geometries: THREE.BufferGeometry[] = [];
33	  const materials: THREE.Material[] = [];
34	  let mesh: THREE.Object3D | null = null;
35	  let key = "";
36	
37	  let swingQueued = false;
38	  let swingStartMs = -Infinity;
39	  let equipStartMs = -Infinity;
40	  let wasMining = false;
41	
42	  const clear = () => {
43	    if (mesh) holder.remove(mesh);
44	    mesh = null;
45	    key = "";
46	    while (geometries.length) geometries.pop()?.dispose();
47	    while (materials.length) materials.pop()?.dispose();
48	  };
49	
50	  return {
51	    update(slot, frame) {
52	      root.visible = frame.visible;
53	      if (!frame.visible) {
54	        // Drop queued swings so they don't replay when the view returns.
55	        swingQueued = false;
56	        return;
57	      }
58	
59	      const nextKey = slot?.id && slot.count > 0 && slot.kind ? `${slot.id}` : "";
60	      if (nextKey !== key) {
61	        clear();
62	        // The new item starts from its own equip transition — don't let it
63	        // inherit the previous item's swing phase.
64	        swingQueued = false;
65	        swingStartMs = -Infinity;
66	        wasMining = false;
67	        const model = buildItemModel(slot);
68	        if (model) {
69	          geometries.push(model.geometry);
70	          materials.push(model.material);
71	          mesh = model.object;
72	          holder.add(mesh);
73	          key = nextKey;
74	          equipStartMs = frame.timeMs;
75	        }
76	      }
77	
78	      if (swingQueued) {
79	        swingQueued = false;
80	        swingStartMs = frame.timeMs;
81	      }
82	      if (frame.miningActive && !wasMining) swingStartMs = frame.timeMs;
83	      wasMining = frame.miningActive;
84	
85	      const pose = computeHeldPose({
86	        timeMs: frame.timeMs,
87	        swingStartMs,
88	        continuousSwing: frame.miningActive,
89	        equipStartMs,
90	        moveFactor: frame.moveFactor
91	      });
92	      holder.position.set(pose.posX, pose.posY, pose.posZ);
93	      holder.rotation.set(pose.rotX, pose.rotY, pose.rotZ);
94	    },
95	
96	    triggerSwing() {
97	      swingQueued = true;
98	    },
99	
100	    dispose() {
101	      clear();
102	      camera.remove(root);
103	    }
104	  };
105	}
106
