  "old_string": "  // Equip: the item rises into frame from below after a slot switch.\n  const e = clamp01((input.timeMs - input.equipStartMs) / EQUIP_MS);\n  const q = 1 - (1 - e) * (1 - e);\n  pose.posY -= (1 - q) * 0.4;\n  pose.rotX -= (1 - q) * 0.5;\n\n  // Idle sway: barely-visible drift so the item never looks frozen.",
  "new_string": "  // Equip: the item rises into frame from below after a slot switch.\n  const e = clamp01((input.timeMs - input.equipStartMs) / EQUIP_MS);\n  const q = 1 - (1 - e) * (1 - e);\n  pose.posY -= (1 - q) * 0.4;\n  pose.rotX -= (1 - q) * 0.5;\n\n  // Fishing: hold the rod out over the water, plus one-shot cast/reel arcs.\n  if (input.fishingActive) {\n    pose.posY += 0.1; // raise\n    pose.posZ -= 0.1; // push forward over the water\n    pose.rotX += 0.3; // tilt the tip up\n    pose.rotZ += 0.05;\n    if (input.fishingBiting) pose.rotX += Math.sin(input.timeMs * 0.05) * 0.04; // tip twitch on a bite\n  }\n  // Cast: a quick wind-up (tip back) for the first third, then a forward flick.\n  const c = (input.timeMs - (input.castStartMs ?? -Infinity)) / CAST_MS;\n  if (c >= 0 && c <= 1) {\n    if (c < 0.35) {\n      pose.rotX += Math.sin((c / 0.35) * (Math.PI / 2)) * 0.55;\n    } else {\n      const s = Math.sin(((c - 0.35) / 0.65) * Math.PI);\n      pose.rotX -= s * 0.85;\n      pose.posZ -= s * 0.12;\n    }\n  }\n  // Reel: yank the tip up and draw the rod toward the body.\n  const r = (input.timeMs - (input.reelStartMs ?? -Infinity)) / REEL_MS;\n  if (r >= 0 && r <= 1) {\n    const s = Math.sin(r * Math.PI);\n    pose.rotX += s * 0.7;\n    pose.posY += s * 0.12;\n    pose.posZ += s * 0.08;\n  }\n\n  // Idle sway: barely-visible drift so the item never looks frozen."
}

1	/**
2	 * Pure pose math for the third-person player body. No Three.js —
3	 * playerVisuals.ts applies the rotation.x values to the limb pivots each
4	 * frame. Deterministic in timeMs, like heldItemPose.ts.
5	 */
6	
7	export const PLAYER_SWING_MS = 260;
8	
9	export type PlayerPoseInput = {
10	  timeMs: number;
11	  /** 0..1 horizontal speed relative to walk speed — scales the walk gait. */
12	  moveFactor: number;
13	  /** True while mining — the arm chop loops instead of stopping after one cycle. */
14	  miningActive: boolean;
15	  /** Start of the most recent swing; -Infinity when the player has never swung. */
16	  swingStartMs: number;
17	};
18	
19	/** rotation.x per limb pivot; negative swings the limb forward (toward -Z). */
20	export type PlayerPose = {
21	  leftArmX: number;
22	  rightArmX: number;
23	  leftLegX: number;
24	  rightLegX: number;
25	};
26	
27	export function computePlayerPose(input: PlayerPoseInput): PlayerPose {
28	  // Walk gait: legs counter-phased, each arm counter-phased to its same-side
29	  // leg, all scaled by horizontal speed so the body idles when standing.
30	  const gait = Math.sin(input.timeMs * 0.012) * 0.8 * input.moveFactor;
31	  const pose = {
32	    leftLegX: gait,
33	    rightLegX: -gait,
34	    leftArmX: -gait * 0.8,
35	    rightArmX: gait * 0.8
36	  };
37	
38	  // Attack/mining chop: the right arm raises forward and falls back, matching
39	  // the first-person held-item swing timing.
40	  let t = (input.timeMs - input.swingStartMs) / PLAYER_SWING_MS;
41	  if (input.miningActive && t >= 0) t %= 1;
42	  if (t >= 0 && t <= 1) pose.rightArmX -= Math.sin(t * Math.PI) * 1.9;
43	
44	  return pose;
45	}
46

  "new_string": "  // Attack/mining chop: the right arm raises forward and falls back, matching\n  // the first-person held-item swing timing.\n  let t = (input.timeMs - input.swingStartMs) / PLAYER_SWING_MS;\n  if (input.miningActive && t >= 0) t %= 1;\n  if (t >= 0 && t <= 1) pose.rightArmX -= Math.sin(t * Math.PI) * 1.9;\n\n  // Fishing: hold the rod arm out forward (negative = toward -Z), with one-shot\n  // cast (wind back then flick) and reel (yank up/back) arcs on the rod arm.\n  if (input.fishingActive) pose.rightArmX -= 1.1;\n  const c = (input.timeMs - (input.castStartMs ?? -Infinity)) / PLAYER_CAST_MS;\n  if (c >= 0 && c <= 1) {\n    if (c < 0.35) pose.rightArmX += Math.sin((c / 0.35) * (Math.PI / 2)) * 0.6;\n    else pose.rightArmX -= Math.sin(((c - 0.35) / 0.65) * Math.PI) * 1.4;\n  }\n  const r = (input.timeMs - (input.reelStartMs ?? -Infinity)) / PLAYER_REEL_MS;\n  if (r >= 0 && r <= 1) pose.rightArmX += Math.sin(r * Math.PI) * 1.0;\n\n  return pose;\n}"
}

  "content": "import * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport { renderSpritePixels } from \"@/lib/ui/spritePixels\";\nimport { buildExtrudedSpriteGeometry } from \"./extrudedSprite\";\n\nconst FLIGHT_S = 0.4; // bobber → player flight time\nconst LIFT = 0.6; // peak of the arc above the straight-line path\n\ntype Flier = {\n  mesh: THREE.Mesh;\n  geometry: THREE.BufferGeometry;\n  material: THREE.Material;\n  from: THREE.Vector3;\n  /** null until its first sync, then the wall-clock start; keeps spawn() time-free. */\n  startMs: number | null;\n};\n\nexport type CaughtItemVisuals = {\n  /** Launches a caught item's sprite from the bobber position; it arcs to the player and vanishes. */\n  spawn(itemId: string, fromX: number, fromY: number, fromZ: number): void;\n  /** Advances every in-flight catch toward `target` (the player's head). Call once per frame. */\n  sync(timeMs: number, target: THREE.Vector3): void;\n  dispose(): void;\n};\n\n/**\n * The \"fish flies to you\" flourish: on a catch, a small sprite of the caught item\n * arcs from the bobber to the player's head over ~0.4 s, then disposes. One mesh\n * per in-flight catch (rare and short-lived), built from the same sprite the\n * inventory icon uses; mirrors the transient-visual pattern of projectileVisuals.\n */\nexport function createCaughtItemVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): CaughtItemVisuals {\n  const fliers: Flier[] = [];\n  const cur = new THREE.Vector3();\n\n  const remove = (f: Flier): void => {\n    scene.remove(f.mesh);\n    f.geometry.dispose();\n    f.material.dispose();\n  };\n\n  return {\n    spawn(itemId, fromX, fromY, fromZ) {\n      const geometry = buildExtrudedSpriteGeometry(renderSpritePixels(itemId));\n      const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ vertexColors: true, roughness: 0.6, metalness: 0.1 });\n      const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);\n      mesh.frustumCulled = false;\n      mesh.position.set(fromX, fromY, fromZ);\n      scene.add(mesh);\n      fliers.push({ mesh, geometry, material, from: new THREE.Vector3(fromX, fromY, fromZ), startMs: null });\n    },\n\n    sync(timeMs, target) {\n      for (let i = fliers.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {\n        const f = fliers[i];\n        if (f.startMs === null) f.startMs = timeMs;\n        const k = (timeMs - f.startMs) / (FLIGHT_S * 1000);\n        if (k >= 1) {\n          remove(f);\n          fliers.splice(i, 1);\n          continue;\n        }\n        cur.lerpVectors(f.from, target, k);\n        cur.y += Math.sin(k * Math.PI) * LIFT;\n        f.mesh.position.copy(cur);\n        f.mesh.rotation.y = timeMs * 0.012; // a little spin for flair\n      }\n    },\n\n    dispose() {\n      for (const f of fliers) remove(f);\n      fliers.length = 0;\n    }\n  };\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { describe, expect, test } from \"bun:test\";\nimport * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport { createCaughtItemVisuals } from \"@/lib/game/render/caughtItemVisuals\";\n\nconst TARGET = new THREE.Vector3(0, 2, 0);\nconst meshOf = (scene: THREE.Scene) => scene.children.find((c) => (c as THREE.Mesh).isMesh) as THREE.Mesh;\n\ndescribe(\"caughtItemVisuals\", () => {\n  test(\"spawns a sprite on a catch and removes it after the flight\", () => {\n    const scene = new THREE.Scene();\n    const v = createCaughtItemVisuals(scene);\n    v.spawn(\"raw_fish\", 5, 1, 5);\n\n    v.sync(0, TARGET); // first sync latches the start time, k=0\n    expect(scene.children).toHaveLength(1);\n\n    v.sync(200, TARGET); // mid-flight (FLIGHT_S 0.4s)\n    expect(scene.children).toHaveLength(1);\n\n    v.sync(1000, TARGET); // past the flight → removed\n    expect(scene.children).toHaveLength(0);\n    v.dispose();\n  });\n\n  test(\"the catch travels from the bobber toward the player\", () => {\n    const scene = new THREE.Scene();\n    const v = createCaughtItemVisuals(scene);\n    v.spawn(\"raw_fish\", 5, 1, 5);\n    v.sync(0, TARGET);\n    const start = meshOf(scene).position.clone();\n    v.sync(200, TARGET);\n    const mid = meshOf(scene).position;\n    // Closer to the target (origin-ish) on x/z than where it started.\n    expect(Math.abs(mid.x - TARGET.x)).toBeLessThan(Math.abs(start.x - TARGET.x));\n    expect(Math.abs(mid.z - TARGET.z)).toBeLessThan(Math.abs(start.z - TARGET.z));\n    v.dispose();\n  });\n\n  test(\"dispose clears any in-flight catches\", () => {\n    const scene = new THREE.Scene();\n    const v = createCaughtItemVisuals(scene);\n    v.spawn(\"emerald\", 3, 1, 3);\n    v.sync(0, TARGET);\n    expect(scene.children).toHaveLength(1);\n    v.dispose();\n    expect(scene.children).toHaveLength(0);\n  });\n});\n"
}

5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Added
8	
9	- **Fishing**: water was only ever a hazard to avoid — now it's a place to fish, a relaxed renewable food source with the odd lucky find, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural rod/fish sprite + synthesized splashes). **No save-format or worldgen change** — the cast is transient session state and the new items save by string id
10	  - **Fishing rod** (craft 3 wood + 2 string): right-click while aiming at water to **cast** a bobber. After a random wait it **dips with a splash** (a bite) — right-click again within ~1.2 s to **reel in** a catch; miss the window and it gets away while the bobber keeps fishing
11	  - **Catch table**: a weighted single pick per bite — mostly **raw fish** (cook it at a furnace, like the meats), sometimes junk (string/bone/seeds/rotten flesh), and rarely a treasure (emerald). Only a successful reel wears the rod
12	  - **Feedback**: a water-splash particle burst when a fish bites and again on the reel-in, plus the reel sound. Common fish/junk catches stay diegetic (splash + sound + the hotbar count) so frequent fishing never spams the HUD; only the rare **treasure** catch raises a one-line toast
13	  - **Architecture**: the cast is one session-only `state.fishing` field (a bobber position + a bite timer), never serialized and cleared on respawn — the same transient-entity pattern as arrows and thrown spears. A new water-aware `waterSurfaceRaycast` (`lib/world/queries.ts`) finds the surface to aim at, since the normal raycast passes through water. The bobber and a `THREE.Line` fishing line render by reading engine state directly (`lib/game/render/bobberVisuals.ts`); `tryFish`/`tickFishing` (`lib/game/engine/systems/fishing.ts`) drive cast/bite/reel and auto-cancel when the rod is unequipped, the player dies, the water drains, or they stray past the tether
14	- **Living world — saplings, bone meal & grass spread**: the world now renews and heals itself, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural sprout atlas tile + a recolored powder sprite). **No save-format or worldgen change** — every effect is an ordinary block edit riding the save diff, and the hash-pinned worldgen tree code is left untouched
15	  - **Saplings**: breaking **leaves** now drops a **sapling** (its only yield, ~8% per break) instead of the old placeholder dirt. Right-click a sapling onto grass/dirt to plant it; once it sits on soil it matures into a tree through the existing random-tick system (`SAPLING_GROWTH_CHANCE`). Trees are renewable at last
16	  - **Bone meal**: grind a skeleton's **bone** into **bone meal** (1 → 3, in the recipe book's Materials section), then right-click it on a sapling to grow the tree **instantly**, or on immature wheat to advance it a random **1–2** stages. A second, renewable use for bones beyond the cursed totem
17	  - **Grass spread**: exposed **dirt** (a column's top block) **re-grasses** over time when one of its four face-neighbour columns has grass on top, healing mined or built-over terrain
18	  - **Architecture**: tree building lives in `lib/game/engine/systems/treeGrowth.ts`, shared by the sapling random-tick handler and the bone-meal use; it writes through the `blockChanges` chokepoint (so the tree persists and relights) using the engine rng, and deliberately shares **no** code with worldgen's `placeTrees`, so the generation hashes stay **byte-identical**. Saplings render like wheat — a solid cube with an atlas-painted texture — so there is no new geometry path. The `Sapling` `BlockId` is appended at the end of the enum (id 50) so existing saved block ids never shift

## Recap

**PR #26 (fishing) merged** into `main`, then implemented the animation polish on a fresh `feat/fishing-animations` branch and opened **PR #27**: https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/pull/27

**5 commits, all render-side (no engine/save/worldgen impact):**
1. Bobber arcs from the rod tip; line anchored at the tip + the camera/hand matrix-flush ordering
2. First-person rod poses — cast wind-up/flick, held-out stance, bite twitch, reel yank
3. Third-person rod-arm poses (mirrored)
4. Fly-to-you catch — the item sprite arcs from the bobber to the player
5. Docs (CHANGELOG + testing coverage map)

**The two gotchas the plan flagged, both handled:**
- The renderer had *zero* `updateMatrixWorld` calls, so the rod-tip world position would've read a stale matrix — `sync` now flushes the camera and runs the body before the rod-tip read.
- Silent cancels (rod unequipped, death, water drained, tether) null the cast with no event, so the bobber's reel-back is driven by the `state.fishing` edge, not the catch event.

**Verify gate green:** lint, typecheck, format:check, `bun test` (**599 pass**), build, and `bun run test:e2e` (**14/14**). New headless tests cover the bobber state machine, both pose layers, and the catch flight; the worldgen/save/fishing-sim tests are untouched, confirming this is purely presentation.

## **Status Effect System Integration Map**

### **1. HEALTH REGENERATION & DAMAGE APPLICATION**

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/playerStats.ts`

**Health Regen Function (lines 62-73):**
```typescript
export function tickHealthRegen(state: GameState, dt: number): void {
  if (!state.isDead && state.hearts < MAX_HEARTS && state.hunger >= REGEN_MIN_HUNGER) {
    state.timers.regenTimer += dt;
    if (state.timers.regenTimer >= HEALTH_REGEN_INTERVAL_SECONDS) {
      state.hearts = Math.min(MAX_HEARTS, state.hearts + 1);  // +1 = +0.5 hearts
      state.timers.regenTimer = 0;
    }
  } else {
    state.timers.regenTimer = 0;
  }
}
```

**Integration points for Regeneration effect:**
- **Add effect check gate** before the hunger check: `state.hunger >= REGEN_MIN_HUNGER` needs an `|| hasRegenerationEffect(state)`
- **Modify heal amount**: Currently adds `1` per interval → can be scaled by effect level (e.g., `state.hearts + (1 * regenerationLevel)`)
- **Separate timer per effect**: Consider reusing `state.timers.regenTimer` (shared with base regen) or add `statusEffects.regeneration.timer` to state

### **2. WATER EXPOSURE & DROWNING**

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/playerStats.ts`

**Water Damage (lines 75-95):**
```typescript
export function tickWaterExposure(state: GameState, dt: number, applyDamage: (amount: number) => void): void {
  // ... detects head immersion at WATER_DAMAGE_DELAY_SECONDS (60s) ...
  if (timers.waterExposureTimer <= WATER_DAMAGE_DELAY_SECONDS) return;
  timers.waterDamageTimer += dt;
  while (timers.waterDamageTimer >= WATER_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS && !state.isDead) {
    timers.waterDamageTimer -= WATER_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS;
    applyDamage(WATER_DAMAGE_HP);  // 3 HP (1.5 hearts)
  }
}
```

**Drowning / Oxygen (lines 138-160):**
```typescript
export function tickOxygen(state: GameState, dt: number, applyDamage: (amount: number) => void): void {
  // ... head in water check ...
  if (world.get(x, headY, z) === BlockId.Water) {
    state.oxygen = Math.max(0, state.oxygen - (MAX_OXYGEN / OXYGEN_HOLD_SECONDS) * dt);  // drain over 15s
    if (state.oxygen > 0) {
      timers.drownTimer = 0;
      return;
    }
    timers.drownTimer += dt;
    while (timers.drownTimer >= OXYGEN_DROWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS && !state.isDead) {
      timers.drownTimer -= OXYGEN_DROWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS;
      applyDamage(OXYGEN_DROWN_HP);  // 2 HP (1 heart)
    }
    return;
  }
  state.oxygen = Math.min(MAX_OXYGEN, state.oxygen + (MAX_OXYGEN / OXYGEN_REFILL_SECONDS) * dt);  // refill over 1.5s
  timers.drownTimer = 0;
}
```

**Integration points for Water Breathing effect:**
- **Gate entire oxygen drain** at the head-immersion check: wrap the drain logic with `if (world.get(...) !== BlockId.Water || hasWaterBreathingEffect(state))`
- **Or skip both damage functions**: Add check at GameEngine's `tickOxygen()` call (line 257) to skip it when effect is active
- **Oxygen refill is automatic** so it's only the drain+drown that needs gating

**Integration points for Poison effect (damage over time):**

### **3. LAVA & BURN DAMAGE**

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/playerStats.ts` (lines 103-129)

```typescript
export function tickLavaExposure(state: GameState, dt: number, applyDamage: (amount: number) => void): void {
  const touching =
    world.get(x, Math.floor(py - 0.1), z) === BlockId.Lava ||
    world.get(x, Math.floor(py), z) === BlockId.Lava ||
    world.get(x, Math.floor(py + PLAYER_HEIGHT * 0.5), z) === BlockId.Lava;

  if (touching) {
    if (timers.lavaBurnTimer <= 0) timers.lavaDamageTimer = LAVA_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS;
    timers.lavaBurnTimer = LAVA_BURN_SECONDS;  // 3s burn after leaving
  }

  if (timers.lavaBurnTimer <= 0) {
    timers.lavaDamageTimer = 0;
    return;
  }
  timers.lavaBurnTimer = Math.max(0, timers.lavaBurnTimer - dt);
  timers.lavaDamageTimer += dt;
  while (timers.lavaDamageTimer >= LAVA_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS && !state.isDead) {
    timers.lavaDamageTimer -= LAVA_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS;
    applyDamage(LAVA_DAMAGE_HP);  // 6 HP (3 hearts)
  }
}
```

### **4. DAMAGE ENTRY POINTS (THE CHOKEPOINT)**

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/playerLife.ts`

There are **two separate chokepoints** (not one):

**A) Combat/Fall/Explosion Damage (armor-mitigated):**
```typescript
export function applyDamageWithArmor(state: GameState, amount: number): boolean {
  if (state.isDead) return false;
  const value = Math.max(0, Math.floor(amount));
  if (value <= 0) return false;
  
  state.inventory = consumeEquippedArmorDurability(...);
  const reduction = armorReduction(...);
  const mitigated = Math.max(1, Math.floor(value * (1 - reduction)));
  
  state.hearts = Math.max(0, state.hearts - mitigated);
  if (state.hearts > 0) return false;
  state.isDead = true;
  state.respawnTimer = RESPAWN_SECONDS;
  return true;
}
```

**Callers:**
- `GameEngine.applyDamage()` (line 488-498 in GameEngine.ts) — wraps it with event emission
- Receives: fall damage (playerMotion.ts line 125), void damage (playerMotion.ts line 132), projectile hits (projectileAI.ts line 118), mob melee attacks (mobAI.ts line 220), explosions (explosion.ts line 110)

**B) Environmental Damage (no armor, no floor at ~0.5 hearts):**
```typescript
export function applyUnmitigatedDamage(state: GameState, amount: number): boolean {
  if (state.isDead) return false;
  const value = Math.max(0, Math.floor(amount));
  if (value <= 0) return false;
  
  state.hearts = Math.max(0, state.hearts - value);
  if (state.hearts > 0) return false;
  state.isDead = true;
  state.respawnTimer = RESPAWN_SECONDS;
  return true;
}
```

**Callers:**
- `GameEngine.applyEnvironmentalDamage()` (line 500-509) — wraps it with event emission
- Receives: water damage (tickWaterExposure line 93), lava damage (tickLavaExposure line 127), drowning (tickOxygen line 153)

**Integration point for Poison:**
- Add a `hasPoison` check **inside** `applyUnmitigatedDamage()` before the final hearts subtraction:
  ```typescript
  const isFatal = state.hearts - value <= 0;
  if (isFatal && hasPoison(state)) {
    state.hearts = 0.5;  // or Math.floor(MAX_HEARTS * 0.25) for 0.5 hearts
    return false;  // don't die
  }
  state.hearts = Math.max(0, state.hearts - value);
  ```

```typescript
export function tryTradeAimedVillager(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  const index = findAimedMobIndex(state);
  if (index < 0 || state.mobs[index].kind !== "villager") return false;
  state.inventoryOpen = true;
  state.craftingStation = "villager";
  emit({ type: "openedStation", station: "villager" });
  return true;
}

### 4. The Eat → Consume Path (lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts)

**Eat Command** (lines 318-328 in GameEngine.ts):
```typescript
case "eatFood": {
  if (state.isDead || state.inventoryOpen || state.sleepTimer > 0) break;
  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];
  if (!slot?.id || slot.kind !== "food" || !slot.hunger || slot.count <= 0) break;
  const next = inv.adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, slot.id, -1, state.selectedSlot);
  if (!next) break;
  state.inventory = next;
  state.hunger = restoreHunger(state.hunger, slot.hunger);
  this.emit({ type: "ateFood" });
  break;
}
```

**Craft Command** (lines 294-305 in GameEngine.ts):
```typescript
case "craft": {
  const recipe = RECIPES.find((entry) => entry.id === command.recipeId);
  if (!recipe || state.isDead) break;
  if (recipe.station && recipe.station !== state.craftingStation) break;
  const next = inv.craft(state.inventory, recipe);
  if (!next) break;
  state.inventory = next;
  if (recipe.station) this.emit({ type: "smelted" });
  break;
}
```

export function renderSpritePixels(itemId: string): Uint8ClampedArray {
  const def = ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[itemId];
  const custom = ITEM_SPRITE_GRIDS[itemId];
  if (custom) return paintGrid(custom.grid, custom.palette);
  if (def?.kind === "block" && def.blockId !== undefined) return paintIsoBlock(def.blockId);
  if (def?.kind === "tool" && itemId.endsWith("_hoe")) return paintGrid(HOE_GRID, toolPalette(materialFor(itemId)));
  if (def?.kind === "tool") return paintGrid(PICKAXE_GRID, toolPalette(materialFor(itemId)));
  if (def?.kind === "weapon") { /* ... */ }
  if (def?.kind === "armor" && def.armorSlot) { /* ... */ }
  return paintGrid(UNKNOWN_GRID, { p: [240, 40, 240], P: [40, 8, 40] });
}

## Status-Effect System Plumbing Map

I've mapped the state/snapshot/HUD architecture. Here are the exact signatures, data flow, and code patterns for integrating a status-effect system.

### 1. State Architecture & Snapshot Construction

**File: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/state.ts` (lines 139–278)**

The core types are:

```typescript
export type GameState = {
  // ... existing fields ...
  /** Session-only; never persisted. */
  mobs: MobState[];
  projectiles: ProjectileState[];
  fishing: FishingState | null;
  primedTnt: Map<number, number>;
  timers: GameTimers;
  // ... etc
};

export type GameTimers = {
  voidTimer: number;
  regenTimer: number;
  // ... 14 other transient timers ...
  daylightHudTimer: number;  // Throttles HUD updates to 4 Hz (0.25s)
  debugHudTimer: number;
};

export type GameSnapshot = {
  // Immutable view for React UI
  api: GameApi | null;
  hearts: number;
  hunger: number;
  oxygen: number;
  armorPoints: number;
  // ... 14 other fields ...
  boss: ({ hpPercent: number } & BossTracking) | null;
  victory: boolean;
};
```

**Where to add effects**: `GameState.effects` should be a `Map<string, ActiveEffect>` or `ActiveEffect[]` (session-only, like `projectiles`, `primedTnt`).

### 2. Snapshot Construction & Change Detection

**File: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` (lines 644–680)**

```typescript
private buildSnapshot(): GameSnapshot {
  const state = this.state;
  return {
    api: this,
    inventory: state.inventory,
    // ... directly copies immutable refs ...
    armorPoints: inv.equippedDefense(state.inventory, state.equippedArmor),
    // ... derived computations ...
    boss: this.bossSnapshot(),  // Ref-stable memoization pattern
    victory: state.victory
  };
}

private refreshSnapshot(): void {
  const next = this.buildSnapshot();
  const prev = this.snapshot;
  const changed = (Object.keys(next) as Array<keyof GameSnapshot>).some(
    (key) => next[key] !== prev[key]
  );
  if (!changed) return;
  this.snapshot = next;
  for (const listener of this.listeners) listener();
}
```

**Key pattern**: Shallow equality check on snapshot keys. If `snapshot.effects !== prev.effects` by reference, React re-renders. **Per-effect timer decrement mutates the object, breaking change detection.** Solution: Use a throttle timer like `daylightHudTimer` (see below).

  // Position/velocity reset
  state.player.position.set(/* ... */);
  state.player.velocity.set(0, 0, 0);
  resetMining(state);

  this.events.push({ type: "respawned" });
}
```

**Pattern**: Session-only player-specific fields clear on death; world state (mobs, blocks, projectiles) persists. **Add effects to session-only clear set if they're player-specific** (e.g., Speed, Jump Boost). **Mob effects belong on `MobState` instead.**

### 4. HUD Integration — Snapshot-to-Component Plumbing

**File: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/components/game/StatusBars.tsx` (lines 1–69)**

Example component consuming snapshot fields:

```typescript
type StatusBarsProps = {
  hearts: number;
  maxHearts: number;
  hunger: number;
  maxHunger: number;
  armorPoints: number;  // Computed from snapshot
  oxygen: number;
  maxOxygen: number;
};

export default function StatusBars({
  hearts,
  maxHearts,
  hunger,
  maxHunger,
  armorPoints,
  oxygen,
  maxOxygen
}: StatusBarsProps) {
  const oxygenIcons = Math.ceil(Math.max(0, Math.min(oxygen, maxOxygen)));
  return (
    <div className="status-bars">
      <div className="status-bars-left">
        {armorPoints > 0 && (
          <IconRow kind="armor" value={armorPoints} max={20} label="Armor" />
        )}
        <IconRow kind="heart" value={Math.max(0, Math.round(hearts))} max={maxHearts} label="Health" />
      </div>
      <div className="status-bars-right">
        {oxygen < maxOxygen && (
          <IconRow kind="bubble" value={oxygenIcons} max={maxOxygen} label="Air" reversed />
        )}
        <IconRow kind="hunger" value={Math.max(0, Math.round(hunger))} max={maxHunger} label="Hunger" reversed />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

**Icon rendering** (via `lib/ui/sprites.ts` → `lib/ui/hudPixels.ts`):

```typescript
export type HudIconName =
  | "heart_full" | "heart_half" | "heart_container"
  | "hunger_full" | "hunger_half" | "hunger_container"
  | "armor_full" | "armor_half" | "armor_container"
  | "bubble_full" | "bubble_half" | "bubble_container";

export function hudIconUrl(name: HudIconName): string {
  return spriteDataUrl(`hud:${name}`, () => renderHudIconPixels(name));
}
```

**Icons are procedurally generated pixel-art canvases**, cached as data-URLs. `PixelImg` renders them as `<img style={{ imageRendering: "pixelated" }}>`—pure CSS, no custom canvas drawing in the HUD.

### 6. Throttle Pattern for Per-Second HUD Updates

**File: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/dayNight.ts` (lines 15–25)**

The daylight timer demonstrates the pattern for avoiding per-frame snapshot changes:

```typescript
export function tickDayNight(state: GameState, dt: number): void {
  state.dayClock += dt;
  state.daylight = daylightAt(state.dayClock);

  // The HUD percentage refreshes at 4 Hz to avoid re-rendering React every frame.
  state.timers.daylightHudTimer += dt;
  if (state.timers.daylightHudTimer >= 0.25) {
    state.timers.daylightHudTimer = 0;
    state.daylightPercent = Math.round(state.daylight * 100);  // Only update snapshot field here
  }
}
```

**Key insight**: `state.daylight` updates every frame, but `state.daylightPercent` (on the snapshot) updates only every 0.25s. Snapshot change detection only triggers when `daylightPercent` changes.

**For effects**: Store remaining seconds in `GameState.effects[id].remainingSeconds` (mutated every frame), but expose a **rounded display value** on the snapshot that updates on a throttle:

```typescript
// In a new effects system tick (called in GameEngine.step()):
tickEffects(state: GameState, dt: number) {
  for (const effect of state.effects.values()) {
    effect.remainingSeconds = Math.max(0, effect.remainingSeconds - dt);
  }
  
  state.timers.effectsHudTimer += dt;
  if (state.timers.effectsHudTimer >= 0.25) {  // Update HUD 4 Hz
    state.timers.effectsHudTimer = 0;
    // Rebuild snapshot-exposed effects here (so only this line triggers change detection)
  }
}
```

### 7. Persistence & Session-Only Pattern

**File: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/types.ts` (lines 99–123)**

Current save shape (v5):

```typescript

  version: 5;
  lootedChests?: number[];
  worldType?: WorldType;
};
```

**Session-only state** is never in `SaveData`:
- `projectiles`, `primedTnt`, `fishing`, `mobs` (except `lootedDungeonChests` gates dungeon resets)

# Status-Effect System + Brewing/Potions — Validated Implementation Plan

## 1. Seam validation (read against the code)

### Effect application seams

**Regeneration → `tickHealthRegen` (`playerStats.ts:63`)** — CORRECT but mind the early-return. The current body only advances `regenTimer` when `hearts < MAX_HEARTS && hunger >= REGEN_MIN_HUNGER`, else it *resets* `regenTimer = 0`. A Regen effect must be a **separate accumulator** (don't piggyback `regenTimer`, which the hunger gate zeroes). Add the Regen heal inside `tickStatusEffects` with its own `regenEffectTimer`, gated only on `hasEffect(state, "regeneration") && !state.isDead && hearts < MAX_HEARTS`. Keep it out of `tickHealthRegen` entirely so the hunger-gate regen and potion regen stay independent (the spec asked for hunger-independent — this is the way).

**Poison → DoT that floors at 0.5 heart** — IMPORTANT CORRECTION. Do **not** route Poison through `applyUnmitigatedDamage`/`applyEnvironmentalDamage`. That helper (`playerLife.ts:27`) sets `isDead`/`respawnTimer` on reaching 0 and `Math.floor`s the amount — it *can kill* and floors fractional damage to 0. For "never kills, floors at 0.5 heart (1 HP)" you need a dedicated path. Add to `playerLife.ts`:
```ts
/** Poison-style damage that can never kill: clamps hearts down to at least `floorHp`. */
export function applyNonLethalDamage(state: GameState, amount: number, floorHp = 1): boolean {
  if (state.isDead) return false;
  const value = Math.max(0, Math.floor(amount));
  if (value <= 0 || state.hearts <= floorHp) return false;
  state.hearts = Math.max(floorHp, state.hearts - value);
  return true; // dealt damage (for a playerHurt emit); never lethal
}
```
`floorHp = 1` = half a heart (hearts are HP on a 20-pt scale, 2 HP/heart). Wire a new engine arrow `applyPoisonDamage` that calls this and emits `playerHurt` when hearts dropped (mirroring `applyEnvironmentalDamage` at `GameEngine.ts:500`, minus the death branch). Tick it inside `tickStatusEffects` with a `poisonTimer` accumulator (1 HP per ~1.5s, Minecraft-like). This keeps all other environmental damage untouched.

**Fire Resistance → gate `tickLavaExposure` (`playerStats.ts:103`)** — CORRECT. Cleanest gate: in `GameEngine.step`, skip/guard the lava tick when `hasEffect(state, "fire_resistance")`. But note `tickLavaExposure` also maintains `lavaBurnTimer`/`lavaDamageTimer` and the "first touch fires immediately" logic. If you simply don't call it while fire-resistant, the burn timer won't tick down — acceptable (it resets to 0 on next non-resisted call since `touching` recomputes). Recommended: pass a `fireResist: boolean` into `tickLavaExposure` and skip only the `applyDamage(LAVA_DAMAGE_HP)` line (keep the timer bookkeeping) so behavior is continuous when the effect expires mid-lava. Either works; the parameter form is safer.

**Water Breathing → gate `tickOxygen` (`playerStats.ts:138`)** — CORRECT. With the effect active, skip the oxygen drain and the drown-damage `while` loop, and instead refill (`state.oxygen = MAX_OXYGEN`, `drownTimer = 0`). Pass a `waterBreathing: boolean` param; the function already takes `applyDamage`, so add one more param. This keeps the bubble HUD full while active (nice signal).

**Speed → `tickPlayerMotion` (`playerMotion.ts:80`)** — CORRECT. `speed` is computed as `crouch ? CROUCH_SPEED : sprint ? SPRINT_SPEED*speedScale : WALK_SPEED*speedScale`. Apply the effect multiplier **after** this line: `const effectMult = speedMultiplier(state); ... speed *= effectMult` (refactor `const speed` to `let speed`, or fold the multiplier into the expression). `speedScale` (hunger) stays as the inner factor — matches the spec ("after the existing hunger speedScale"). No Slowness in v1 set, but the same hook serves it later.

**Strength → `combat.ts` / attack dispatch** — CORRECT, with a recommendation. Two options:
- (a) Add the bonus inside `weaponDamage(state)` (`combat.ts:25`) — but `weaponDamage` is pure-ish and also you'd want bow arrows unaffected (Strength is melee in Minecraft).
- (b) Preferred: apply at the dispatch site `GameEngine.ts:354` — `tryAttackMob(state, weaponDamage(state) + strengthBonus(state), ...)`. This keeps `weaponDamage` honest (UI/tooltips read it) and scopes Strength to melee only (the bow branch at `:350` is untouched). Use additive bonus (e.g. +3 HP, ~Minecraft Strength I ≈ +3) rather than a multiplier, so a fist hit also benefits sanely.

**Damage chokepoints** — CONFIRMED: `applyDamageWithArmor` (mob/fall hits, via `this.applyDamage`) and `applyUnmitigatedDamage` (env, via `this.applyEnvironmentalDamage`). `applyUnmitigatedDamage` is called **only** from `applyEnvironmentalDamage` (grep-confirmed). Poison gets a *third* helper as above — do not overload either existing one.

**Step order** — CONFIRMED CORRECT. Insert `tickStatusEffects(state, dt, deps)` between `tickHealthRegen` (`GameEngine.ts:254`) and the env-damage ticks (`:255-257`). This sets the `fireResist`/`waterBreathing` gates and applies regen/poison before lava/oxygen run. Place the countdown-and-expire of all timers at the top of `tickStatusEffects` so an effect that expires this frame doesn't gate this frame's lava (minor; acceptable either way). Death already early-returns at `:229` so effects don't tick while dead — and they must be cleared on death/respawn anyway (see §2).

### Snapshot throttle (does it actually prevent re-render thrash?)

CONFIRMED the throttle is necessary and the `daylightHudTimer` pattern is the right model. Quoting the code:

- `refreshSnapshot` (`GameEngine.ts:673-680`): `const changed = (Object.keys(next)...).some((key) => next[key] !== prev[key]); if (!changed) return; ... for (const listener of this.listeners) listener();` — a **shallow per-key `!==`**. If you put a live `activeEffects` array on the snapshot and rebuild it every `buildSnapshot()` (every `step`), `next.activeEffects !== prev.activeEffects` is **always true** (new array identity each frame) → a React render every frame. That's the thrash.
- `buildSnapshot` (`:644`) is called from both `step`'s `refreshSnapshot` and `dispatch`'s. So the projection must be a **ref-stable cached array**, rebuilt only at 4 Hz or when the *visible* content changes — exactly how `bossSnapshot()` (`:625`) caches `this.lastBoss` and only reassigns when a rounded value moves, and how `daylightPercent` is recomputed at 4 Hz in `dayNight.ts:19-24`.

Recommended implementation: a `this.lastEffectsProjection` cache + an `effectsHudTimer`. In `tickStatusEffects` (or a small `tickEffectsHud`), every 0.25s build `{id, remaining: Math.ceil(remainingSeconds)}[]`, compare to the cached array by **content** (same length, same ids, same ceil'd seconds); only if different, replace `this.lastEffectsProjection` with the new array. `buildSnapshot` returns `this.lastEffectsProjection` (stable identity between rebuilds). Because remaining is `Math.ceil`'d, identity changes ~1/sec per active effect, not 60/sec — and never when no effects are active (stays the same empty array). This satisfies the shallow `!==` check.

One subtlety: `buildSnapshot` is also called from `dispatch` (e.g. selecting a slot). Since it returns the cached array reference, those snapshots keep the same `activeEffects` identity — no spurious renders. Good.

### Brewing end-to-end

CONFIRMED: open stand → `craftingStation="brewing"` → `InventoryPanel` passes `craftingStation` into `groupRecipes`/`stationLocked` (`:106-108`) → Brewing recipes unlock and float to top of the "Brewing" group → click → `onCraft` → `craft` command gates on station (`:299`) → `inv.craft` consumes ingredients, produces the potion item. Zero new crafting plumbing. The only required UI touch is the `STATION_LABELS` entry and the category.

## 2. Effects data structure on `GameState`

**Recommendation: `Map<EffectId, number>` where the value is `remaining` seconds.**
- Per-frame tick is a simple `for (const [id, t] of map) { const n = t - dt; if (n <= 0) { map.delete(id); emit expired } else map.set(id, n) }`.
- The throttled projection iterates the Map once.
- A fixed `Record<EffectId, number>` (0 = inactive) avoids Map churn but bloats every snapshot/iteration and complicates "is it active." An array of `{id, remaining}` requires linear scans for `hasEffect`. Map gives O(1) `has`/`get`/`set`/`delete`, clean iteration, and natural absence semantics. With only ~6 effect kinds the Map is tiny.
- A plain number value (not `{remaining}`) is enough for v1 (single level, no amplifier). If you later want tiers, widen to `Map<EffectId, {remaining: number; level: number}>` — keep the helpers as the seam so callers don't change.

Note: `GameState` already uses `Map` for session-only data (`containers`, `primedTnt`), so this matches the file's conventions and the constructor-literal init style (`GameEngine.ts:145-147`).

Helper module `lib/game/engine/systems/statusEffects.ts`:
```ts
export type EffectId =
  | "speed" | "strength" | "regeneration"
  | "fire_resistance" | "water_breathing" | "poison";

export type EffectConfig = {
  id: EffectId;
  label: string;
  positive: boolean;
  defaultSeconds: number;
  hudIcon: HudEffectIcon;        // procedural icon key (hudPixels)
  tint: PixelPalette;            // for the procedural icon
};
export const EFFECT_CONFIG: Record<EffectId, EffectConfig>;

export function hasEffect(state: GameState, id: EffectId): boolean;        // map.has
export function effectRemaining(state: GameState, id: EffectId): number;   // map.get ?? 0
export function addEffect(state: GameState, id: EffectId, seconds?: number): void; // map.set max(existing, seconds)
export function clearEffects(state: GameState): void;                      // map.clear — call on death + respawn

// the per-frame system (countdown + expire emits + regen/poison application + hud throttle)
export function tickStatusEffects(state: GameState, dt: number, deps: {
  applyPoison: (amount: number) => void;
  emit: EmitGameEvent;
}): void;

// pure modifier readers used by motion/combat
export function speedMultiplier(state: GameState): number;   // hasEffect speed ? 1.3 : 1
export function strengthBonus(state: GameState): number;     // hasEffect strength ? 3 : 0
```
`addEffect` should take `seconds = EFFECT_CONFIG[id].defaultSeconds` and apply `max(existing, seconds)` (re-drinking refreshes, never stacks duration weirdly). State field: `effects: Map<EffectId, number>` on `GameState` (init `new Map()` in the constructor literal at `GameEngine.ts:~145`). Clear in `respawn()` (`:569`) and at death (in `applyDamage`/`applyEnvironmentalDamage` death branch, or once in `tickRespawnTimer`'s revive — but spec says "cleared on respawn/death," so clear in both `applyDamage` death emit and `respawn`). Add `effectsHudTimer` + (optional) `regenEffectTimer`/`poisonTimer` to `GameTimers` (`state.ts:111`, `createTimers:200`).

The `every tool/weapon material prefix has a palette` test (`:57`) only checks `kind==="tool"|"weapon"` — potions are `kind:"material"` (or a new `kind`), so they're exempt without touching the `customGrid` set. Simpler: `kind:"material"` + the `effect` field; drink path keys off `slot.effect`, not kind.

## 4. Test plan

Headless (bun test, `new GameEngine({ worldSize:{x:64,y:150,z:64}, rng: mulberry32(...) })`, mutate `engine.state.*`, `engine.step(dt, frame)` — matches `GameEngine.test.ts` patterns):
- **Speed mult**: set `effects.set("speed", 10)`, run motion with W held; horizontal distance per step > baseline by ~the multiplier. (Compare two engines, one with/without effect, same input/hunger.)
- **Strength**: spawn a mob in reach, `dispatch attack`; mob `hp` drops by `weaponDamage + STRENGTH_EFFECT_BONUS` vs baseline.
- **Regen**: `hearts = MAX-4`, `hunger = 0` (proves hunger-independence), `effects.set("regeneration", 30)`, step past interval; hearts increase. Without effect at hunger 0, no regen.
- **Poison floor-at-0.5**: `hearts = 2` (one heart), `effects.set("poison", 30)`, step many intervals; hearts clamp at `POISON_FLOOR_HP` (1) and never set `isDead`. Also assert a `playerHurt` event fires while damaging and stops at the floor.
- **Fire-resist gate**: place lava under player, `effects.set("fire_resistance", 30)`, step; `hearts` unchanged. Remove effect → lava damages.
- **Water-breathing gate**: head submerged (set player into water cell), `effects.set("water_breathing", 30)`, step past `OXYGEN_HOLD_SECONDS`; `oxygen` stays max, no drown damage. Without it, oxygen drains and drown damage applies (existing behavior).
- **Drink command**: put a potion in selected slot, `dispatch drinkPotion`; `effects.has(id)` true, slot count −1, `drankPotion` event emitted; non-potion slot → no-op.
- **Expiry**: `addEffect(id, 0.1)`, step 0.2s; effect removed, `effectExpired` emitted.
- **Clear on death/respawn**: add effects, force lethal hit → effects cleared; after respawn effects empty.
- **Brewing**: open stand sets `craftingStation==="brewing"`; `dispatch craft` of a brewing recipe with ingredients succeeds and yields the potion; same recipe with `craftingStation==="furnace"` is rejected (station gate).
- **Throttle**: two consecutive `step(1/60)` calls with active effects → `getSnapshot().activeEffects` is the **same reference** (identity unchanged) within a sub-second window; crossing a whole-second boundary changes the ceil'd `remaining` → new reference. (Mirrors the `daylightPercent`/boss tests.)

Recipe/sprite/category tests:
- `recipes.test.ts`: `recipeCategory(brewingRecipe) === "Brewing"`; `groupRecipes` still passes its `every(g => g.recipes.length > 0)` assertion (empty categories dropped — Brewing non-empty because we add recipes); ordering assertion holds (Brewing slotted into `RECIPE_CATEGORY_ORDER`).
- `spritePixels.test.ts`: passes automatically — every new ITEM_DEFS id (bottle, potions, brewing_stand) renders non-empty and ≠ checker; potions are `material`, exempt from the tool/weapon palette test; brewing_stand is a block (iso cube) so it renders.
- `hudPixels.test.ts`: extend `ALL_ICONS` with effect icons; the "variants differ" style assertions apply per icon.

Component:
- `ActiveEffects.test.tsx`: given `activeEffects=[{id:"speed",remaining:7}]`, renders one row with the "7" readout and the right `data-*`/alt; empty array → nothing.

Regression confirmations (already verified):
- `save.test.ts` asserts `version: 5` and migration chain ends at 5 (`:42,83,105,198,302,310`). Session-only `effects` are not in `serialize()` (`GameEngine.ts:414`) → stays v5 → green.
- `generation.test.ts` is worldgen-only; adding `BlockId.BrewingStand` doesn't change `WORLDGEN_VERSION` or terrain (no worldgen placement) → green. (Only bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` if you place brewing stands in dungeons — don't, for v1.)

## 5. Decision flags for the user

1. **Effect set** — confirm the six (Speed, Strength, Regeneration, Fire Resistance, Water Breathing, Poison). Slowness/Weakness are free later via the same `speedMultiplier`/`strengthBonus` hooks; not in v1.
2. **Session-only vs persisted** — recommend session-only (matches oxygen/weather/projectiles; keeps SaveData at v5, no migration, no `save.test`/`generation.test` churn). Persisting would require a `SaveDataV6`, `serialize` version bump, migration `v5→v6`, and new save tests — only do it if effects-across-reload matters.
3. **Single-level vs tiered** — recommend single-level v1 (`Map<EffectId, number>`). Tiering = widen value to `{remaining, level}` and add amplifier handling in `speedMultiplier`/`strengthBonus`/poison rate; defer.
4. **Ingredient → potion mapping (avoid new worldgen)** — pick from existing items so no new drops/ores are needed. Suggested, all craftable today:
   - Glass bottle: from existing `glass` (sand→glass recipe exists at `recipes.ts:160`).
   - Speed ← `sugar`? (no sugar item) → use `feather` (chicken drop) or `seeds`.
   - Strength ← `gunpowder` (creeper) or `bone`.
   - Regeneration ← `wheat`/`bread` ingredient or `dragon_heart` (endgame-gated, strong).
   - Fire Resistance ← `coal`/`charcoal` (fits "fire").
   - Water Breathing ← `raw_fish` (fishing).
   - Poison ← `rotten_flesh` (zombie) or `cactus`.
   Confirm the exact pairs; all reuse current drops/blocks, zero worldgen.
5. **Rotten-flesh-poison hook (Commit E)** — opt-in. Adds risk to eating rotten flesh (Minecraft-authentic) and exercises the negative-effect path in real gameplay. Include or skip?

Additional flags surfaced by the read that differ from the brief:
- The "zero UI changes beyond a category" is actually **one category + one `STATION_LABELS` entry** (exhaustive Record). Confirm OK.
- Poison must use a **new non-lethal helper**, not `applyUnmitigatedDamage` (which can kill and floors fractional damage). Confirm OK.
- Drink key: reuse `KeyF` (potion-aware) vs a dedicated key. Recommend potion-aware `KeyF` to avoid new bindings. Confirm.

- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/state.ts

The plan is written. Here's the recommendation and what it covers.

## Recommended next feature: Status effects + brewing/potions

This is the deepest of the four options and the one that adds genuinely new infrastructure — a status-effect system that also future-proofs enchanting. The exploration confirmed the scope is tractable because two big things reuse existing patterns: **brewing is just station-gated recipes** (like furnace smelting), and **each effect is a one-line modifier at an existing seam**.

**What ships:** a Brewing Stand (new station block) where you brew 5 positive potions — **Speed, Strength, Regeneration, Fire Resistance, Water Breathing** — from a glass bottle + an existing ingredient; drink to apply a timed effect shown in a new HUD readout. **Poison** is a never-kill hazard from eating rotten flesh. Per your calls: effects **persist across reload** (save v5→v6), and poison is included as a hazard.

**The corrections the Plan agent caught (now baked in):**
- Poison needs a **dedicated non-lethal damage helper** — the existing environmental-damage path can kill and floors fractional damage.
- The regen effect can't reuse the hunger-gated `regenTimer` (it gets zeroed) — it needs its own accumulator.
- The HUD must use a **ref-stable cached projection** rebuilt at 4 Hz (like the boss bar), or the per-second countdown re-renders React every frame.
- The station union lives in **4 places** plus an exhaustive `STATION_LABELS` and `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` — all flagged.

**Structure:** 7 lint/test-green commits (effect core → potions+drink → brewing stand+recipes → HUD → persistence → rotten-flesh poison → docs), with headless tests for every modifier (speed, strength, regen, poison-floor, fire-resist gate, water-breathing gate), the drink command, brewing recipes, the throttled snapshot, and the v5→v6 save migration. `generation.test.ts` stays untouched (no worldgen change). A manual gameplay pass is the place to confirm feel and tune durations.

One thing to confirm at review time: the ingredient→potion mapping (feather→Speed, gunpowder→Strength, wheat→Regen, coal→Fire Resist, raw_fish→Water Breathing) is a balance default I picked to avoid any new worldgen — easy to adjust.

> AGENT

Good question to raise before we commit. My honest take: **XP isn't needed for potions, and I'd defer it — but bundle it with enchanting when it does come, not on its own.**

Here's the reasoning:
- **Potions don't use XP at all.** Brewing is ingredient-based (bottle + drop → potion), and drinking is free. So nothing in the planned feature needs an XP system — adding it here would be a non-sequitur.
- **XP is only meaningful with a sink.** Its whole purpose is to be *spent* — on enchanting (and anvil repair / mending). An XP bar that fills from mining/mobs/fishing with nothing to spend it on is a hollow number that invites "why is this here?" So XP should ship *together with* enchanting, as one feature, not standalone.
- **Order matters in our favor.** The status-effect system we're about to build is actually a stepping stone toward enchanting — several enchantments (fire protection, respiration, etc.) are eff-ects-like, and the modifier seams we're adding (damage, speed, damage-gates) are exactly what enchantments hook into. So doing potions first makes the later XP+enchanting work *easier*, not redundant.

So I'd keep the current plan as-is and slate **XP + enchanting** as a strong follow-up. That said, it's your call on sequencing — let me confirm which way you want to go.
